title: Apply Heat, Melt ICE: Flashpoints in the Fight : A Guide to Resisting ICE around the Country this October
content:
All around the United States, people are organizing to resist the federal mercenaries who carry out Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Here, we announce three upcoming mobilizations and share reports from two recent confrontations.


In

Arizona

, people have been blocking the construction of the border wall since July 27; they are calling for people from around the country to come join them. In the

Twin Cities

, people are calling for a countrywide day of action on October 3 to express solidarity with the Minnesota 15, who have been federally charged for allegedly conspiring to resist Operation Metro Surge. In

Vermont

, people have organized a week of action for October 4-9 and are inviting people to come participate or carry out solidarity actions elsewhere. Clashes with federal mercenaries have recently broken out in

Austin, Texas

 and

Frederick, Maryland

.


Awareness of the harm that ICE is inflicting on communities peaked in January, during the

massive popular resistance

 against the federal occupation of the Twin Cities. Yet deportations have only

increased

 since then, with most of the abductions taking place behind closed doors as ICE agents work with police and jails to capture immigrants. The recent wave of resistance to ICE offers a crucial chance to take the offensive ahead of what is bound to be a tumultuous fall.


As many liberals shift to focusing on the midterm elections this November, naïvely hoping that elections alone will provide change, it is especially important to continue to focus on what we can accomplish directly by means of collective power. However the elections turn out, only effective grassroots action can create a situation in which neither party will be able to continue the violence of ICE.


Remember, the abduction and deportation of immigrants

did not begin under Donald Trump

; as recently as last year,

mainstream Democrats

 were proposing to

adopt

 Trump’s xenophobic policies wholesale. Even if the far right loses control of the government, whoever inherits state power will maintain every repressive policy that we do not force them to discontinue. The victory that the movement against ICE achieved in the Twin Cities, forcing Trump to end Operation Metro Surge and fire ICE and Department of Homeland Security officials, shows what we can accomplish when we don’t wait on politicians.


It is time to shift from

reactive

 to

proactive

—from organizing rapid response networks to seizing the initiative. Pick the struggle that is nearest to you geographically or politically and participate in it, whether by traveling to join it or by organizing a local action in solidarity.


Wherever you are, you are probably close to ICE infrastructure, ICE profiteers, or a current hotspot in this struggle. Make plans to travel to a flashpoint near you or organize something at a relevant local target. You can help to boost all of the other events by mentioning all of them in your messaging.


Apply heat, melt ICE!


Minnesota


Out of the tens of thousands who participated in

resisting

 Operation Metro Surge in Minnesota between December and February 2026,

fifteen people

 have been federally charged for allegedly conspiring to resist the violence that ICE agents inflicted on their communities.


The Minnesota 15 Anti-Repression Committee is calling for

a nationwide day of solidarity actions on Saturday, October 3

 to express support for the defendants and all those targeted by ICE. Plan an action at your local ICE office or federal building!


In Minneapolis, on October 3, a labor-led march will traverse downtown to show solidarity with the defendants and to call out the federal government and their corporate enablers. Meet at Peavey Plaza, 1101 Nicollet Mall.


Vermont


From October 4-9, in Chittenden County, Vermont, people will host a week of mass action to end ICE surveillance, targeting, and separation. Everyone is invited!


Vermont is a national nerve center for ICE surveillance. Through the Law Enforcement Support Center and the National Criminal Analysis Targeting Center, both of which are located in Williston, Vermont, ICE collects tips on our immigrant neighbors, spies on civilian social media accounts, and builds lists of targets for kidnapping and deportation. Alongside a dozen other offices scattered around Chittenden County, these sites provide the bureaucratic backbone and surveillance infrastructure for ICE activity countrywide.

author: Emma Jacobs
title: What the climate movement can learn from organized labor
content:
This article

What the climate movement can learn from organized labor

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


Climate activists engaged in nonviolent direct action are used to the rinse and repeat of arrest: handcuffs, short trip to jail, a misdemeanor charge and then release to friends for a post-action pizza dinner. Show up at court a few weeks later for a brief arraignment and wait for the case to be dismissed. Low drama.


That’s changed under Trump. From the

Declare Emergency activists charged with felonies

 (for applying washable paint to the protective case around a Degas sculpture) to the

Extinction Rebellion activists under investigation by an FBI terrorism task force

 (for undisclosed reasons), activists can no longer depend on walking away unscathed from direct actions.

Multiple states have passed anti-protest laws

 since Trump was elected, increasing penalties imposed on activists. Grassroots action has a higher cost now. 


Simultaneously, with the gutting of the Inflation Reduction Act and its attendant tax credits for clean energy investment, the federal path to climate action is blocked. And local wins, while important, cannot surmount the incredible rollbacks happening at the federal level, as Sunrise Movement Executive Director Aru Shiney-Ajay

recently pointed out

. 


Indeed, the U.S. climate movement is in

deep trouble

. If all that weren’t enough, the climate crisis is no longer top of mind for many on the left, especially with the rising authoritarian threat and the focus on affordability. With civil disobedience demanding greater risk, traditional policy advocacy for climate action at the federal level closed off and public attention turned elsewhere, what tactics do we in the climate movement have left?


What’s left is deep engagement with the labor movement — its members and its tactics. 


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


Organized labor has a broad base, a track record of major wins and the power to shut down the economy. And make no mistake: Economic leverage is a necessary ingredient in the struggle to bring down companies as profitable as those in the fossil fuel industry. 


Climate activists have relied heavily on tactics of protest and persuasion (see Gene Sharp’s

categories

), underinvesting in tactics of economic noncooperation. While the environmental movement has a history of consumer boycotts, there have been fewer instances of work stoppages or rent strikes. The climate groups that do engage in symbolic work and school stoppages (most famously, Fridays for the Future), have mostly been confined to students and are largely to make a political statement rather than a strategic attempt to gain concrete concessions from a specific target. 


Strategically aligning workers with a rapid energy transition not only broadens the coalition needed to win durable policy victories, but builds power with a movement versed in strikes, walkouts, slowdowns and other forms of economic disruption. (Not to mention a bevy of tools like

community benefit agreements

 and

co-enforcement

 to promote follow-through on corporate environmental promises.)


Labor-climate alliances go back decades (see Blue Green Alliance, Climate Jobs National Resource Center and Labor Network for Sustainability), and unions have long advocated for a

just transition

 that supports workers employed in polluting industries. But in the current political environment, we need these relationships to be stronger than ever.  


One major opportunity for the climate movement is the May Day Strong coalition, which brings labor and community groups together to organize mass strikes and make big demands for systemic change. The coalition’s demands don’t yet include climate, but the climate movement can still organize with them to learn nonparticipation tactics and build solidarity toward a broad base that sees climate, anti-authoritarianism and affordability as one united fight. 


Lessons from labor

 


Think about the situation at your job. Workplaces are pretty authoritarian: the leader doesn’t care much for the input of the people on the shop floor, and what the leader says goes. If someone gets hurt, let the government step in to help them. As unions teach us, for a group of workers to extract real concessions from a profit-maximizing boss requires building enough power among workers to shut the workplace down (or at least threaten to do so) …

author: Admin100
title: One Million Hands Flourishing: Nicaragua and the Neverending Task of Planting
content:
By Tamaya F.C.


The indigenous neighborhood of Monimbo in Masaya, Nicaragua has a long legacy of resistance. Masaya is located less than an hour Southeast of the capital, Managua. In 1978, the people of Monimbo barricaded themselves, used makeshift weapons and prevented the National Guard from coming into the city, winning the first major victory for the Sandinistas as they were able to take control of an urban city. Forty years later, the people of Monimbo barricaded themselves with paving stones and were able to prevent riot police from entering. The next day however, they had lost most of the city to riot police. Masaya, the city where I am from, has become a battlefield where police attack citizens.


The Unrest


The latest civil unrest has had many university students from across the capital city of Managua protesting against the government’s social security reforms this past week. These students hail from various universities like the Universidad Centroamericana (UCA), Universidad Nacional de Ingenieria (UNI), Universidad Nacional Agraria (UNA), Universidad Autónoma Nacional de Nicaragua – Managua (UNAN)

,

and Universidad Politécnica de Nicaragua (UPOLI). The  proposal was to increase social security contribution from both workers and employers and

reduce retiree benefits

 by 5%.


Last week, students barricaded the Metropolitan Cathedral in Managua which serves as a refuge for protesters. There, they collected donations and distributed provisions such as water and had student doctors help tend to the wounded. Police and pro-government Sandinista youth eventually surrounded the cathedral and held them hostage until prominent Catholic church official, Monsignor Silvio Jóse Báez, who has been critical of Ortega and supportive of protesters, aided and helped assure the release of the students.


Sandinista Legacy


When the Sandinistas (FSLN) overthrew the Somoza regime in July 1979, they had to work toward reconstructing the social, political and economic structure of the country. They implemented

agrarian reforms

 for redistribution of land, launched

 vaccination campaigns

 to open access to healthcare and created

literacy campaigns

 that reduced illiteracy from 80 percent to 12 percent, among other reforms. This was only possible because of the work everyday people put in day after day.


Over the last five days, more than 30 people have died, many of them students as well as a journalist. Over 100 are being held prisoner, around 50 remain missing and the overall count of those injured is unknown.


On April 22nd, Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega, who rose to power as a prominent leader of the Sandinistas, revoked the proposed changes to social security. After he pulled the reforms, riot police entered a prominent symbol of the student resistance, UPOLI, which students had barricaded. Five students were shot in the process and two were killed. Ortega also attacked the student movement as “delinquents” who were backed by right-wing parties and funded by the CIA. The student movement does not allow

political parties to participate

 though. But many Nicaraguans know this is an issue greater than social security. They are tired of corrupt governments and want the current government out.


I am an anarchist. So w

hen I say “I am a Sandinista” to me it means I believe in the popular movement that rose up to overthrow capitalist imperialism. The movement that fought for freedom. The movement that dared to dream of bringing a just and equitable society.


The current government of Ortega does not represent the values of Sandino nor of the Sandinistas who spilled blood to break free from their chains in previous decades. The Sandinista Youth of today is not the same one that my mother joined many years ago. It is not the one that participated in literacy campaigns to teach the people to read and write, nor is it the one she joined to help pick coffee and rebuild Nicaragua.


The Demands of the Students


The future is uncertain and it is unclear where this is all heading but there is much work to be done on the ground. Today, students from the

Movimiento 19 de Abril

, who embody the spirit of liberation are undertaking the never ending task of building a new world, one from the bottom up. Approximately 500 students continue their barricaded occupation of UPOLI and their organizing against Ortega. They are currently working on establishing a coordinating body to represent students from different …

author: anred
title: Caso AySA: organizaciones ambientales, sindicales y sociales se reunieron con Magario
content:
Ayer se llevó a cabo una reunión entre la vicegobernadora Verónica Magario y distintas organizaciones ambientalistas, sindicales, sociales, de defensa del consumidor en el salón Dorado del Honorable Senado de la Provincia de Buenos Aires. El objetivo de la reunión fue plantear la irregular e innecesaria privatización de Aysa.

Por Patricia Rodríguez para ANRed


Entre las exposiciones escuchadas se hizo hincapié en la inconstitucionalidad de la medida, ya que privatizar la empresa estatal significaría el recorte de inversiones y demoras en obras de infraestructura, lo que produciría un impacto ambiental y sanitario que perjudicaría la salud pública y el medioambiente. Por otro lado, pondría en riesgo la propiedad del consumidor, ya que las cuotas impagas podrían liquidarse con la propiedad del usuario.


También, se remarcó el peligro que representaría la flexibilización en los controles de calidad del agua que redundaría en una proliferación microbiológica y química que pondría en peligro sanitario a millones de personas.


Se recordó que antaño la empresa estatal admitía las sugerencias de los vecinos, logrando consensuar medias y proyectos como el programa “Agua más trabajo” que ampliaba las redes de agua potable mediante la contratación y capacitación de cooperativas de trabajadores locales desocupados. De la misma manera, representantes de las Islas del Delta marcaron la suspensión del aprovisionamiento y reparto de agua potable entre los isleños. Los exponentes coincidieron en comparar la privatización con un genocidio silencioso, porque transferir la gestión de un recurso vital a manos privadas priorizaría la rentabilidad financiera por encima de la salud pública. La empresa privada no tendría ningún prurito en cortar el servicio de agua y cloacas por falta de pago lo que duplicaría la mortalidad infantil y reduciría la esperanza de vida. La vicegobernadora Magario coincidió en marcar a la privatización como un “genocidio silencioso”, plagado de irregularidades legales y éticas.

author: Natalia Viana
title: Família de condenado por garimpo na terra Yanomami bancou vida de Ramagem nos EUA
content:
“Oii Pri, boa noite. Você tem como me enviar uma conta do apartamento de vocês no nome do meu pai? Água, luz, telefone, internet… Vamos tentar tirar a driver license do Alexandre amanhã no DMV”, diz a primeira mensagem. E a seguir: “Fiz o contrato aqui também para ele levar como se tivesse alugado o quarto. Vamos ver como vai ser”.


Essas mensagens de WhatsApp fazem parte da investigação da Polícia Federal (PF) sobre a fuga de Alexandre Ramagem para os Estados Unidos em setembro do ano passado. Elas foram enviadas por Celso Rodrigo de Mello, filho de Rodrigo Martins de Mello, conhecido como Rodrigo Cataratas, para a esposa de seu pai em 15 de setembro de 2025. Cataratas foi condenado em fevereiro deste ano a mais de 16 anos de prisão por liderar uma organização criminosa responsável pela mineração ilegal de cassiterita e ouro dentro da Terra Indígena Yanomami. Em resposta, Priscila Freitas de Melo diz apenas “Oi

 Deixa eu ver aqui”. DMV é o departamento estadual de trânsito da Flórida.


As mensagens fazem parte de uma série de diálogos, fotos e notas recuperados do celular de Priscila aos quais a

Agência Pública

 teve acesso.

Elas comprovam que a família de Rodrigo Cataratas ciceroneou, forneceu auxílio material e hospedou Ramagem logo na sua chegada à Flórida, foragido do Brasil. A apuração foi feita com apoio do ICIJ, Consórcio Internacional de Jornalistas Investigativos.


Diretor da Abin (Agência Brasileira de Inteligência) durante o governo Bolsonaro, Ramagem foi condenado pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF) em 11 de setembro de 2025 a 16 anos de prisão pela tentativa de golpe de Estado. Os ministros consideraram que ele utilizou a estrutura da Abin para monitorar adversários e apoiar a trama golpista do ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro. Na ocasião, ele também perdeu o seu mandato como deputado federal (PL-RR) e o cargo que tinha na Polícia Federal. Desde 21 de novembro, antes da condenação, o STF já havia decretado sua prisão preventiva por suspeita de fuga. Ele segue foragido da Justiça brasileira.


A família de Cataratas, incluindo Priscila e Celso, é investigada por ter ajudado a fuga de Ramagem do Brasil

através

 do município de Bonfim, em Roraima, que faz fronteira com a cidade de Lethem, na Guiana, em 9 de setembro de 2025. Da Guiana, Ramagem pegou um avião para os Estados Unidos, onde teria chegado no dia 11 de setembro, segundo a PF. Ramagem estava proibido de sair do Brasil desde junho de 2025 por medida cautelar determinada por Moraes, que também o obrigou a entregar todos os seus passaportes.


O ex-diretor da Abin chegou a ser detido pelo ICE, serviço de imigração dos Estados Unidos, motivado por uma infração de trânsito. Entretanto, ele foi liberado dois dias depois com

ajuda direta da Casa Branca

. Ele teria feito um pedido de asilo aos EUA “por perseguição política” e o

ICE disse à época

 que ele poderia esperar os trâmites em liberdade.


A reportagem não encontrou Alexandre Ramagem, Rodrigo Cataratas e Celso de Mello para comentar. O espaço permanece aberto.


“Nosso amigo Ramagem”


Segundo as mensagens analisadas, Priscila era o principal elo de ligação entre a família e a administração do Condomínio Sole Mia, residencial de luxo no norte de Miami onde Ramagem ficou hospedado durante três meses. Foi ela a encarregada, em 17 de setembro, de enviar uma mensagem pedindo um “cartão de acesso” ao estacionamento. A mensagem, assinada por Priscila e dirigida à administradora do condomínio, se referia a Ramagem como um “amigo nosso” – dela e do então marido, Rodrigo Cataratas.


“Estou escrevendo para te pedir gentilmente um cartão de acesso para o portão, já que infelizmente perdemos o originalmente designado para nosso apartamento. Como estamos viajando, não vamos conseguir retirá-lo. Portanto, autorizamos um amigo nosso, Alexandre Rodrigues Ramagem, a coletar o novo cartão em nosso nome”.


O pedido pretendia resolver um problema que Ramagem enfrentou assim que chegou nos EUA. O filho Celso estava contestando duas multas que o “amigo” teria tomado no Sole Mia por estacionar na vaga errada.


O Sole Mia é um residencial de luxo mesmo para os padrões de Miami.

 Os moradores e hóspedes podem usufruir de uma piscina e um lago artificial de 28 mil metros quadrados, com areia e coqueiros plantados ao redor, além de campo de futebol, quadras esportivas, playground, pista de cooper, trilhas para caminhadas e spa. O apartamento de Cataratas tem 96 m², dois quartos e dois banheiros, uma enorme …

author: Indymedia Pueblos Originarios
title: Punta Querandí reclama a Nordelta la reparación por la destrucción de enterratorios indígenas
content:
La Comunidad Indígena Punta Querandí rechazó la profundización del modelo urbanístico de Nordelta y exigió medidas de reparación histórica por los daños ya ocasionados sobre el patrimonio indígena y los humedales, a partir de las conclusiones del propio Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Acumulativo (EIAA). Entre las principales demandas se encuentran el reentierro de 42 ancestros en el territorio de donde fueron extraídos, la creación de un Espacio de Memoria Ancestral y fondos financiados por Nordelta destinados a las comunidades y población indígena del distrito.


Movilización en diciembre de 2021. (Foto: Omar Bogado)


La destrucción de cementerios y sitios ancestrales indígenas por el avance de los barrios privados sobre los humedales de Tigre y Escobar está en el origen mismo de la lucha de Punta Querandí. Durante dos décadas, la Comunidad denunció la destrucción y afectación de lugares sagrados, reclamó la restitución de los cuerpos humanos excavados y logró concretar los primeros reentierros en el Área Metropolitana de Buenos Aires.


Ahora, el Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Acumulativo (EIAA) presentado por Nordelta S.A. ante el Municipio de Tigre evalúa los impactos producidos durante casi tres décadas de desarrollo urbano y forma parte del proceso del que depende la posibilidad de avanzar con nuevas obras en sectores todavía no consolidados del emprendimiento. El estudio reconoce que, antes del comienzo de las obras en 1998, los sitios Arroyo Sarandí 1 y 2 conservaban su integridad como yacimientos indígenas y enterratorios ancestrales, datados entre los años 800 y 1400 d.C., y que posteriormente fueron “destruidos o sepultados como consecuencia de las obras de construcción de Nordelta”.


Frente a ese reconocimiento, la Comunidad Indígena Punta Querandí presentó ante el Municipio de Tigre una serie de demandas de reparación histórica, territorial, cultural y ambiental.


Señalización realizada en noviembre de 2016. (Foto: Archivo Punta Querandí)


Durante julio y agosto, el Municipio de Tigre abrió un proceso de Participación Ciudadana sobre el EIAA, que incluyó una Consulta Pública para que vecinos, organizaciones e instituciones pudieran presentar observaciones y preguntas sobre el estudio. El proceso incluyó además una Audiencia Pública realizada el 21 de agosto en el Teatro Municipal Pepe Soriano de Benavídez.


El reclamo de reparación se plantea por los daños ya ocasionados, independientemente de la decisión que finalmente adopten las autoridades respecto del EIAA y del futuro desarrollo urbanístico de Nordelta. La presentación contó con el patrocinio de la abogada Paula Mercedes Alvarado Mamani, perteneciente al Pueblo Kolla y especialista en Derecho Internacional de los Derechos Humanos, con trayectoria en causas vinculadas a los derechos de los pueblos indígenas.


El EIAA califica además la pérdida o afectación del patrimonio arqueológico y paleontológico como un impacto “negativo muy alto”. También advierte que otros contextos arqueológicos pueden haber desaparecido debido a la transformación de la Planicie Litoral por urbanizaciones cerradas sin estudios arqueológicos preventivos.


LOS 42 ANCESTROS DEBEN VOLVER A ARROYO SARANDÍ


Fragmento del Estudio de Impacto Ambiental Acumulativo de Nordelta.


Uno de los principales reclamos es garantizar un espacio protegido dentro del área donde se encontraba Arroyo Sarandí, actualmente dentro de Nordelta, para concretar el reentierro de los 42 ancestros que fueron excavados de ese sitio y permanecen en el Museo de La Plata.


La restitución de estos restos humanos a Punta Querandí fue aprobada por el Instituto Nacional de Asuntos Indígenas (INAI) en enero de 2022, como continuidad del proceso que permitió recuperar y reenterrar ocho ancestros en Punta Querandí y en La Bellaca.


El reclamo cuenta además con un importante antecedente institucional: en 2020, el Concejo Deliberante de Tigre declaró de interés legislativo los procesos de restitución y reentierros impulsados por Punta Querandí, incluyendo el de Arroyo Sarandí.


El lugar del reentierro deberá contar con protección jurídica permanente y Punta Querandí solicita además su reconocimiento como Sitio Sagrado.


Junto al lugar de reentierro, Punta Querandí propone crear un Espacio de Memoria Ancestral, financiado por Nordelta y administrado por la Comunidad, destinado a preservar y transmitir la memoria de los pueblos originarios del territorio, la historia de Arroyo Sarandí y las prácticas culturales …

author: La Zarzamora
title: Indonesia: Campaña de financiación para talleres de formación ante la criminalización, la violencia y las acciones represivas
content:
Durante más de una década, las comunidades de base de Bandung se han estado organizando contra la gentrificación, el desplazamiento y la pérdida de los espacios por los que han luchado para mantenerlos vivos. Miles de personas han formado parte de esta larga lucha, enfrentándose a la presión y la represión mientras seguían organizándose desde la base.

Esta campaña surge directamente de esa historia. La idea de celebrar el taller allí partió de uno de los líderes comunitarios que se encuentra en el centro de esta lucha, alguien que ha estado organizándose con la comunidad a lo largo de estos años de presión y desalojo.

El taller también reúne a antiguos presos de Chaos Star y a anarquistas sociales de base: dos grupos que, hace años, apenas podían encontrarse cara a cara. Desde el año pasado, han comenzado a trabajar juntos, reconociendo que, tras años de represión y lucha, se necesitan mutuamente.

author: Darío Aranda
title: Eduardo Cerdá: "No hay que reemplazar al glifosato, hay que cambiar el modelo de producción"
content:
Por Nahuel Lag


La Red Nacional de Municipios y Comunidades que Fomentan la Agroecología (Renama) marcha al decimosegundo

Mes de la Agroecología

. Será en noviembre, cuando las tranqueras se abrirán para demostrar un modelo de producción que está presente en todo el país. Eduardo Cerdá es el impulsor de ese espacio a partir de su trabajo como ingeniero agrónomo y asesor de campos que son “faro”, como le gusta decirles, y este año fue coautor del libro

Agroecología en Municipios

, que repasa la construcción de la primera década de la Renama.


Desde el trabajo con los productores a la construcción de políticas públicas con los municipios y de allí a la Dirección Nacional de Agroecología (DNA), que encabezó durante el gobierno de Alberto Fernández y fue eliminada con la llegada de Javier Milei. “Los funcionarios públicos aún no han llegado a comprender lo que genera la agroecología en el campo, nosotros lo vemos funcionar y escuchamos a los productores decirnos: ‘La agroecología me salvó’”, asegura.


¿En qué situación está la agroecología a tres años de gobierno de Milei? Cerdá repasa las decisiones de la gestión de La Libertad Avanza para “desfinanciar y romper todo”. Desde la disolución de la DNA a la desarticulación del programa Cambio Rural del INTA —que durante la gestión anterior llegó a reunir cerca de 200 grupos con 1.600 productores agroecológicos—, la

eliminación del Inafci

, la decisión de

prohibir la mención a la palabra “agroecología”

 para realizar investigaciones en el INTA, la desjerarquización del Instituto Nacional de la Yerba Mate (INYM), con el que se habían iniciado cursos de planteos agroecológicos para sus equipos técnicos. Esas decisiones generaron un “amesetamiento”, analiza, que esté menos en la agenda pública, pero “por debajo la agroecología sigue en pie”, asegura.


“Este modelo de gobierno propone la disgregación, que el otro es tu enemigo. Eso afectó la mirada de los gobiernos provinciales y municipales, y generó una sensación de angustia”, señala Cerdá y por eso rescata el paso por la DNA que permitió “darle institucionalidad a la agroecología”. “Durante la gestión de la DNA aumentaron las ordenanzas municipales de restricción de agroquímicos, de fomento a la agroecología, las direcciones de agroecología, los proyectos de cesión de terrenos, ferias agroecológicas, entregas de semillas, cursos, sistemas participativos de garantías (SPG)”, enumera y reconoce que eso se realizó con un gestión que buscó fomentar, pero lo hizo sin presupuesto.


Foto: Renama


“El Estado es considerado como un presupuesto. A mí me puteaban mucho porque me decían 'este no hace política porque no le da bola al presupuesto’. Para mí el presupuesto es la gran encrucijada que te plantea el Estado”, contrapone y sostiene: “Si la zanahoria tiene que ser plata para que los productores hagan agroecología, no va por ahí, es un cambio de enfoque”


De todas formas también señala

la falta de voluntad que existió para la sanción de una Ley de Fomento a la Agroecología

 —se presentaron tres proyecto en el Congreso y no alcanzaron el tratamiento en el recinto— y propone otras políticas a encarar ante la vuelta de un gobierno que mire a la agroecología: Ley de Arrendamientos —a cuatro o cinco años para poder cuidar los suelos—, un plan estatal de rotación de cultivos, una Ley de Producción Apícola, Ley de Etiquetados de Transgénicos y un organismo que se encargue, de una vez, de medir la presencia de agrotóxicos en alimentos, agua, tierra y aire. “Iría por más capacitación, por más formación, con más grupos técnicos, a obtener más información de todos los productores agroecológicos, hacer redes de compra y venta”, concluye.


"

En l

a producción


extensiv

a


es donde está el gran cambio del modelo

"


Cerdá vuelve al presente, deja de lado la sensación de angustia de los tiempos actuales y resalta que “cuando se tejen vínculos, cuando nos encontramos, nos alegramos, nos damos cuenta que avanzamos, que hicimos cosas, que tenemos un camino para compartir”. Por eso la Renama continuó celebrando estos años el

Mes de la Agroecología

, estrenó el

documental

 “La Aurora: El principio del Camino” —sobre la historia del productor “faro”

Juan Khier

— y prepara una nuevo sobre la comensalidad para pensar: “¿Cómo me las arregló para cocinar y comer sano evitando tanto conservante y los productos ultraprocesados que son los que se venden en las góndolas de los supermercados?”.

author: Comunizar
title: Revista Crítica Anticapitalista 6 – La Comuna, la clase y la lucha de clases
content:
PRESENTACION


¿Qué relación existe entre la Comuna como forma política de la emancipación social y la clase, entendida ésta no como categoría positivizada y sociológica, sino en su carácter dual y contradictorio? ¿Es la Comuna una manera de entender la clase y la lucha de clases en clave no identitaria, no positivizada? ¿La oposición entre Comuna y clase es algo derivado de una concepción anti-dialéctica de la lucha de clases? En ese campo ¿a qué dialéctica nos referimos? ¿A la dialéctica hegeliana orientada a la síntesis estatal como forma política de la identidad? ¿A la dialéctica negativa que la cuestiona? ¿La lucha de clases, entendida en clave dialéctica no-identitaria, permite entender la Comuna como proceso contradictorio de disolución de la clase? ¿Implica esto un desafío a nuestro concepto de proletariado y a la idea de revolución calcada en el canon leninista?

title: «El derecho a la protesta no es terrorismo»: CORREPI y la Gremial de Abogados reclaman el cierre de la causa contra Milton y Eneas
content:
La Coordinadora contra la Represión Policial e Institucional (CORREPI) y la Gremial de Abogados reclaman la libertad de Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft y el cierre de la causa por la que permanecen detenidos en el Complejo Penitenciario Federal II de Marcos Paz tras movilizarse el 11 de febrero contra la reforma laboral. El pronunciamiento cuestiona especialmente la aplicación del agravante del artículo 41 quinquies del Código Penal, utilizado en la acusación fiscal para intentar duplicar las penas previstas para los delitos imputados: «l

as protestas y las luchas en que participaron Milton y Eneas no son terrorismo», sostienen, dado que, aunque un juez y la Cámara de Apelaciones de la Ciudad descartaron inicialmente la aplicación de esa figura, el fiscal Carlos Stornelli volvió a plantearla y el juez federal Ariel Lijo dictó posteriormente el auto de elevación a juicio. Las organizaciones recuerdan, además, que el propio artículo establece una excepción para hechos ocurridos «en ocasión del ejercicio de derechos humanos y/o sociales o de cualquier otro derecho constitucional»

. Por ANRed.


La

Coordinadora contra la Represión Policial e Institucional (CORREPI)

 y la

Gremial de Abogadas y Abogados

 reclamaron la

libertad de Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft


y el cierre de la causa en la que permanecen detenidos tras movilizarse el pasado 11 de febrero contra la reforma laboral

. El pronunciamiento cuestiona especialmente la utilización del

artículo 41 quinquies del Código Penal

 y denuncia que

la figura de terrorismo vuelve a ser invocada en una causa originada en una protesta social

.


«

Las protestas y las luchas en que participaron Milton y Eneas no son terrorismo

«, sostienen CORREPI y la Gremial, que recuerdan que

ambos permanecen detenidos en el Complejo Penitenciario Federal II de Marcos Paz, mientras Oscar Rubén «Homero» Aguirre y Néstor Gabriel Barrera fueron excarcelados pero continúan procesados

. En este marco, los cuatro fueron vinculados a la causa abierta luego de la movilización contra la reforma laboral.


El artículo 41 quinquies establece que, cuando un delito sea cometido con la finalidad de «aterrorizar a la población» o de obligar a autoridades públicas a realizar o abstenerse de realizar un acto, «la escala se incrementará en el doble del mínimo y el máximo». La misma disposición establece que el agravante no se aplica cuando los hechos ocurran «en ocasión del ejercicio de derechos humanos y/o sociales o de cualquier otro derecho constitucional». El artículo fue incorporado al Código Penal por la Ley 26.734, sancionada en 2011, y reformado en 2024 mediante la Ley 27.739. El texto vigente mantiene tanto el agravamiento de las penas, como la excepción referida al ejercicio de derechos constitucionales.


La discusión ya había aparecido al comienzo de la causa. En febrero, e

l juez Gonzalo Rúa rechazó aplicar el agravante por terrorismo y sostuvo que la fiscalía no había acreditado que la conducta tuviera por finalidad aterrorizar a la población o obligar a las autoridades

. La Cámara de Apelaciones confirmó luego la prisión preventiva de Tolomeo y mantuvo su procesamiento por «tenencia de material incendiario, atentado y resistencia a la autoridad e intimidación pública», al tiempo que señaló que incluso sin el agravante de terrorismo la pena en expectativa permitía justificar la medida cautelar.


Foto: Sofía Saluzzi.


Según CORREPI y la Gremial de Abogados, pese a esos antecedentes, el fiscal Stornelli volvió a incorporar el artículo 41 quinquies y el juez Ariel Lijo dictó el auto de elevación a juicio. El planteo de las organizaciones es que

esa calificación no puede utilizarse para una protesta social y que la causa debe cerrarse

.


La situación de Tolomeo también fue cuestionada por las condiciones de su detención: CORREPI había denunciado que, tras su arresto, fue alojado en un sector de “alto riesgo” del sistema penitenciario federal, con restricciones severas para las visitas y las comunicaciones, pese a que el juez que había dictado la prisión preventiva había descartado inicialmente la calificación de terrorismo. Posteriormente fue trasladado a un pabellón común.


Foto: Sofía Saluzzi.


«Hoy vemos en la realidad cotidiana los resultados que la reforma laboral ha acarreado para el conjunto del pueblo trabajador. Crece la desocupación, la pérdida de puestos laborales registrados es masiva, la precarización es la …

author: Ludmila Pizarro
title: Nossa Senhora Aparecida vira evento eleitoral e aprofunda crise entre ministros do STF
content:
Nossa Senhora Aparecida se transformou em um dos maiores eventos políticos de 2026, com 1,3 milhão de publicações e 12,4 milhões de interações entre 23 e 27 de setembro, ou seja, na penúltima semana antes do primeiro turno das eleições. A informação é do monitoramento realizado nas redes sociais neste período pelo Instituto Democracia em Xeque (IDX).


Não foi sem razão, portanto, que a campanha do senador e candidato à Presidência, Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) acionou, já na sexta-feira, 25 de setembro, o Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE) tendo como o alvo a publicação do humorista Antonio Tabet.


A alegação dos advogados de Flávio era que se tratava de desinformação, uma mentira, afirmar que ele apoiava a retirada do título de “padroeira do Brasil” da santa. De fato, o post de Tabet ocorreu em meio a uma onda de desinformação sobre a relação do senador com um Projeto de Lei apresentado pelo então deputado Professor Victório Galli (PP-MT), pastor evangélico e arquivado em 2008. A proposta alterava a lei do feriado de 12 de outubro, trocando “padroeira do Brasil” por “padroeira dos brasileiros católicos apostólicos romanos”,

conforme a Agência Pública mostrou

.


Flávio Bolsonaro batizado no rio Jordão, em Israel, numa repetição de ato feito pelo pai em 2016


O que o relatório do IDX mostra, entretanto, é que o debate sobre o assunto nas redes sociais ultrapassou rapidamente a “fake news” e se desenvolveu no embate político sobre liberdade religiosa, intolerância, defesa da padroeira e impacto eleitoral.


“A maior parte da conversação está em torno do debate cultural, religioso, judicialização, liberdade de expressão e defesa da padroeira, com 83% do universo analisado. Somente 17% do universo mencionam a acusação que originou a controvérsia”, afirma o relatório do Instituto.


A própria publicação de Antonio Tabet não faz relação direta ao projeto de lei. Trata-se de uma imagem da santa com a frase: “A família miliciana odeia tanto mulher preta, que resolveu atacar Nossa Senhora Aparecida!”.


Dino versus Mendonça


O tangenciamento entre o que é desinformação e o que acabou se tornando debate político, gerou uma nova batalha de decisões entre ministros de dois tribunais superiores, que deve ser levada ao plenário do Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF).


No domingo, 27 de setembro, o ministro do STF Flávio Dino suspendeu as decisões do colega André Mendonça da última sexta-feira, 25, que determinava às redes sociais como X (antigo Twitter), Facebook, Instagram, TikTok e YouTube a retirada de postagem de Tabet e de outras contas nas redes sociais. Uma das decisões de Mendonça relaciona mais de mil links de publicações sobre o mesmo tema que deveriam ser retiradas pelas empresas responsáveis pelas mídias sociais.


Mendonça também afirmou na decisão, como atual vice-presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), que as redes sociais “atuem preventivamente contra a disseminação dos conteúdos abrangidos por esta decisão”. A decisão do ministro, derrubada por Dino, ainda fixa uma multa diária de R$ 50 mil ao provedor que não cumprir a medida.


Entre as justificativas do ministro Flávio Dino para anular as decisões de Mendonça está o risco de “censura em massa”, diante da “‘derrubada’ de milhares de postagens, inclusive de adeptos do culto à Nossa Senhora Aparecida”. Além disso, Dino afirma que o TSE “delegou largos poderes censórios às empresas de internet”, e que é necessário um “debate sobre o controle de constitucionalidade de decisões monocráticas de um ilustre ministro que faz parte de um Tribunal Superior”.


O ministro ainda salienta no documento a importância de valores como a liberdade religiosa, “já que o tema de fundo em discussão pública refere-se à determinação legal de ser Nossa Senhora Aparecida a ‘Padroeira do Brasil’”. Na mesma decisão, Dino solicita a análise da questão pelo plenário do Supremo.


Com a suspensão da derrubada de seu posicionamento, Tabet, também no domingo, publicou novamente a foto da santa com a mesma frase. O humorista ainda escreveu na rede social X: “Flavio Dino acabou de derrubar a decisão de André Mendonça, ‘preservando a liberdade de expressão e a liberdade religiosa’ dos que defendem Nossa Senhora Aparecida. Como será impossível restabelecer a postagem que foi apagada, vou publicá-la novamente. E conto com vocês para fazê-la chegar mais uma vez a todos que a viram e aos que não puderam vê-la”.

author: Unknown
title: Besê Hozat: The process cannot succeed without democratization
content:
Besê Hozat, co-chair of the KCK Executive Council, said in an interview with Medya Haber that the Peace and Democratic Society Process cannot succeed in Turkey without democratization.


This is the first part of the interview.


The discussions regarding the Peace and Democratic Society Process are ongoing. As movement, you have already taken a number of significant steps in this regard. Also, before Parliament adjourned, the framework law – which you referred to as a law that creates a foundation on which to build on – was passed. What has been done afterward, and what hasn’t? Parliament Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş stated that the process is running smoothly. Do you assess it similarly?


Before addressing your question, September 25 marked the anniversary of the martyrdom of our comrade Rıza Altun. He was commemorated extensively both in Kurdistan and abroad, and many commemorations were held. I commemorate all the martyrs of the revolution and freedom – represented by our comrade Rıza – with respect, love, and gratitude. Our comrade Rıza holds a very significant place and value within our struggle. With his theoretical, ideological, political, and practical experiences, as well as his consciousness and expertise, he has contributed greatly to this struggle. He has contributed immense value to this struggle. On the path illuminated by comrade Rıza and all our martyred comrades, we will carry out this struggle successfully – with determination, conviction, and resolve – and we will achieve success based on the principle of living up to their memory. This struggle will lead to victory. I wish to reaffirm this pledge once again on the occasion of this anniversary.


Coming to your question; we have made several statements regarding the framework law. From the very beginning, both Rêber Apo [Kurdish people’s leader Abdullah Öcalan] and our movement have clearly laid out our standing on this matter. We have made many assessments and statements based on the premise that this law should be a comprehensive one, that it should truly play the role of a foundational law, and that it should pave the way for a democratic solution to the Kurdish issue. This law did not fully meet these criteria, and accordingly, we have criticized it. It is an extremely flawed, internally contradictory, and paradoxical law. Implementing it as it stands – in a straightforward manner – is hardly possible anyway. This is quite clear. When we speak of the law’s comprehensiveness, it should have encompassed Rêber Apo’s physical freedom, his conditions for a free life and work, the leadership of the movement as a whole, and the entire organizational structure – from the top leadership down to every level – including Rêber Apo, who is excluded from the scope of this law.


The law should have demonstrated an approach and a commitment to taking democratic, political, and legal steps. It is known that both the emergence of the PKK and the armed struggle came about because of the lack of this. The existence of the Kurdish issue gave rise to the PKK and to the armed struggle. There is a very serious need for democratic, political, and legal steps that lay the groundwork for and pave the way toward resolving this issue. This law did not fully address this; that much is clear. It is also very, very difficult to describe it as a truly fundamental law in this regard. It is a legal text, and in that sense, it may have some significance. It is a step – a step on the legal level – that has emerged and developed within this process. However, it would not be realistic to ascribe much more meaning to it beyond that. Since the process began, we have taken very important steps as a movement. In particular, many steps were taken following the Call for Peace and Democratic Society on February 27, 2025 by Rêber Apo.


The PKK’s dissolution congress was a historic development. At this congress, the decision was made to cease armed struggle against Turkey. However, for this process to proceed, it was established as a fundamental requirement that Rêber Apo’s physical freedom be secured, allowing him to freely lead this process. This remains valid today. Numan Kurtulmuş made a statement the other day saying the process is running “like clockwork.” In reality, there is no such process running “like clockwork.” That is the truth of the matter. There is a process that is moving extremely slowly, a process driven by unilateral steps. At present, the state has not taken any …

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: ‘Trump not welcome’
content:
Trump is no ordinary foreign guest.

Should Filipinos welcome guests and express concerns another day?

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro thinks so in relation to the possible visit of United States President Donald Trump to the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit in November.

Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) told Malacañang, “Trump is not welcome in the Philippines.”

“Trump is no ordinary foreign guest,” the group said in a statement. “His waterloo in Iran and West Asia, his continuing support for Israel’s genocide in Palestine, the proxy war in Ukraine, and his unprovoked interventions in Venezuela and Cuba, have made the entire world suffer.”

Castro made the request when asked by a reporter during a Palace press briefing on September 23 if there were additional security measures in place for the 49th ASEAN Summit in Metro Manila, considering what happened to the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) Investment Forum held at the Grand Hyatt Manila on September 10 where protesters barged to the venue. In this incident, five paralegals who responded to the protest were arrested but were eventually released.

The 1,600-hectare industrial hub under the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative is planned to be built in New Clark City in Tarlac which is within the LEC.

Read: Why Pax Silica is bad for the Philippines

Malacañang declared November 16 to 18, as special non-working days in the National Capital Region (NCR) for the event. Other ASEAN-related meetings are also set to be held.

During the September 23 Malacañang press briefing, Castro did not confirm the attendance of Trump. But the Department of Foreign Affairs has been reportedly preparing for his possible visit, according to an Inquirer report.

Bayan stressed that the country is turning into a forward military base of the U.S. given the established military sites under agreements involving the U.S. and Philippine governments, such as the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA). It added that Pax Silica would support this alleged military agenda.

Read: Philippines as a US military base?

“Peaceful protests during an international summit are legitimate and effective means for our people to tell visiting leaders and our own government where they stand on issues that directly affect their lives, sovereignty and future,” the multisectoral group said.

It added that the Philippine National Police (PNP) should not use “security” as an excuse to establish protest-free zones. (DAA)

author: groundxero
title: Safety Out, Fear In? The Mirage of Women’s Security under ‘Double Engine’ Government/s
content:
In a society where political leaders publicly endorse custodial deaths, support those accused or convicted of sexual offences, and scrutinise the ‘moral integrity’ of victims, the fear persists.


 


Debasree Sarkar


 


For the last few months of Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) ascendency to power on May 5, 2026, in West Bengal (WB), news reports of rapes of minors and women have become part of our daily routine. For example, in May, in Bankura’s Jaipur area, a BJP leader was arrested after being accused of raping a seven-year-old girl; an Adivasi woman was found dead in the Amrakola forest in Kharagpur after being brutally raped in May; in June, in the Chandrakona Road area of Paschim Midnapur, a woman accused a local BJP leader of dragging her from her home, physically assaulting her, and attempting to rape her while her husband was away; also in June, reports came of an alleged gang-rape of a minor Adivasi girl in Durgapur. There are many other cases, such as the alleged rape of a minor in Malda’s English Bazar area and the Baruipur minor girl rape and murder case in July; the Dhupgiri gang rape case in August; the alleged rape of a minor tribal girl in Belpahari on August 23; the alleged gang rape of a tribal woman in Lalgarh, and the Dinhata minor assault case in September, and so on.


The Adivasi community has been expressing outrage over incidents of sexual violence against tribal women over the past few months in the Jangalmahal region. The tribal social organization Bharat Jakat Majhi Paragana Mahal recently held a rally in Jhargram demanding women’s safety and swift justice for the complainants of sexual assault and violence. People from the various tribal communities of the region—including Jhargram, Purulia, Bankura, and Paschim Medinipur—along with local residents and representatives from various student and youth organizations have participated in the procession. Tribal community members stated that the atrocities against women witnessed in the few months following the change of government, are unprecedented in Bengal.


 


If we juxtapose this brief chronology of crimes against women in WB with the contemporary situation on a national level, these events illustrate a concerning depiction of the ongoing susceptibility of women, especially minors, Adivasi women, and those belonging to the minority community and economically disadvantaged social groups. The month of September only can reveal the concerning trend of women’s safety in the BJP-ruled states. As

The Print

reported, from a teenager allegedly gang-raped and killed in north Delhi to minors allegedly assaulted in homes, hotels, and various public spaces, at least 13 cases of alleged rape and sexual assault have been reported across the National Capital Region in September.


 


Several women students from different Delhi University colleges marched on September 25 in protest over violence against women following the alleged rape of a minor girl at the Aastha Kunj park with the slogan “Hum Auratein Azaad Hain” (we, the women, are free).

The

organizers criticised “protectionist policies” taken by the Delhi Development Authority’s alleged move to bar women from public parks after sunset, alongside colleges enforcing stricter hostel and PG curfews that effectively cage women rather than tackling offenders. It is not safe for women to drive on the roads of Delhi anymore. On September 12, a woman scooterist alleged that two men riding a motorcycle stalked and harassed her before hitting her scooter near South Delhi’s Panchsheel Metro Station, and the very next day, a video recorded by a camera mounted on Shivani Chauhan’s bike, appears to show a white car moving close and hitting her motorcycle. In the Hasanpur-Kotwali area in Uttar Pradesh’s Amroha district, two police personnel and two Central Reserve Police Force personnel have been arrested for allegedly raping a woman on 23rd September. And how can we forget the harassment and sexual assault of the minor girl from Jamui? Within a few days of this shocking incident, another minor girl was molested at Samastipur, Bihar.

author: John David Parol, John Elvin Gonzales, Colline Nobleza, at Joanna Del Rosario
title: Edukasyon sa kuko ng komersyalisasyon
content:
Sa mga pamantasang dapat sana’y pugad ng mapagpalayang kamalayan, lalong sinisiil ang mga kabataang estudyante sa kasalukuyang kalagayan ng pagkakait sa sa edukasyon bilang batayang karapatan at sa halip ay garapalang inilalako bilang kalakal.

Sa kaibuturan, iisa ang bumubuhay sa krisis na ito: ang marahas na komersyalisasyon at neoliberal na reistruktura ng edukasyon. Sa walang-patumanggang pagyakap sa mga Kanluraning modelo, ganap na isinubasta ang silid-aralan sa interes ng pandaigdigang merkado.

Nababawasan ang diin sa paghubog sa mag-aaral bilang kritikal na tagasuri ng lipunan. Sa halip, unti-unti silang itinutulak upang umakma sa merkado bilang tagakonsumo at nakareserbang lakas-paggawa para sa umiiral na sistema. Ramdam ito sa patung-patong na bayarin, kakapusan sa mga pasilidad, at sa unti-unting pagliit ng mga demokratikong espasyo sa loob ng mga kampus.

Ayon sa Artikulo 14, Seksyon 5 ng ating Saligang Batas, malinaw na dapat itakda ang “pinakamataas na prayoridad sa badyet” para sa edukasyon. Ngunit sa kabila nito, patuloy namang kinakaltasan ang pondo para sa mga pampublikong pamantasan, partikular sa mga State Universities and Colleges (SUCs).

Sa panukalang ₱7.2 trilyong 2027 National Expenditure Program (NEP), naglaan ang Department of Budget and Management (DBM) ng ₱141.09 bilyong alokasyon para sa mga SUCs sa buong bansa.

Gayunpaman, hindi ramdam ng mayorya ang sinasabing dagdag-pondo. Ayon sa 2027 NEP, 43.46% o 49 sa 113 SUCs ang nakatakdang makatanggap ng mas mababang budget.

Sa Kamaynilaan, nangunguna sa listahan ng may pinakamalaking panukalang budget cut ang University of the Philippines (UP) System na umabot sa ₱2.95 bilyon. Kabilang din sa may malaking bawas ang Philippine Normal University (PNU) na nasa ₱394.9 milyon at ₱291.8 milyon sa Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP).

Sa UP Manila, classroom shortage ang pangunahing problema ng mga estudyante.

“Danas na danas naming mga estudyante ang kakulangan sa espasyo kung saan may mga ilang klase, online na lang dahil walang classroom. Sa course namin ay apat na baitang ang naghahati-hati sa iisang classroom. Bukod dito, nahihirapan rin kami mag-organize ng event na magpapaigting sana sa aming mga kampanya hindi lamang dahil sa burukrasya bagkus pati na rin wala talagang espasyo para pagganapan nito, sabi ni Patricia Jutie, Chairperson ng College of Public Health Student council.

Bukod sa kakulangan sa espasyo, tampok din sa ilalim ng administrasyong Marcos Jr. ang usapin ng malawakang korupsyon at maanomalyang paggastos ng pamahalaan hinggil sa flood control at iba pang infrastructure projects.Isa rito ang renovation ng Rizal Hall ng College of Arts and Sciences sa UP Manila, na ipinagawa ng Department of Public Works and Highways (DPWH) sa St. Timothy Construction Corporation, isang kumpanyang konektado sa mag-asawang Discaya. Hindi natapos ng contractor ang naturang proyekto.

Sa ilalim ng administrasyong Marcos Jr., nananatiling malaking bahagi ng pambansang paggasta ang inilaan sa imprastraktura. Para sa 2027, itinutulak naman ng administrasyon ang ₱643.95 bilyon para sa DPWH, ₱113.05 bilyon o 21.29% na mas mataas kaysa sa 2026 GAA.

“Kung titingnan natin ang UP Manila, kasama rin sa budget nito ang Philippine General Hospital (PGH). Hindi lang siya isyu ng mga estudyante; issue siya ng mamamayan. Sino ba ang mga nakikinabang sa ating hospital? Mga mamamayan natin na nangangailangan ng mapagkalingang health care system sa bansa,” saad naman ni Kabataan Partylist UPM chairperson Querobin Acsibar.

Espasyo rin ang usapin sa Philippine Normal University (PNU) at Polytechnic University of the Philippines (PUP).

“Sa loob ng pamantasan, maraming isyung kinakaharap ang mga estudyante. Isa lang po dito ang kakulangan sa espasyo, hindi matapos-tapos na imprastraktura, at lahat ng ito ay lumulundo sa kakulangan sa budget sa edukasyon,” ani Adleann Biol, Vice Chairperson ng PNU USC-Central Student Council.

“Sa kasalukuyan, mahigit 100,000 na iskolar ng bayan ang hindi nakapasok sa PUP dahil sa kabaratan ng budget sa pamantasan. Dagdag dito, ang North Wing na mahigit apat na taon ng tinatry na i-build, yung aming main academic building kung saan nakakaranas ang mga estudyante ng kakulangan sa student spaces at academic organization spaces na labis na pinapanawagan ng mga kabataan noon pa man hanggang ngayon,” ani Michael Dave Bolima, Secretary General ng PUP Sentral na Konseho ng Mag-aaral.

author: rti_admin
title: From Inheritance to Inquiry: The Courage to Question
content:
A society becomes dynamic not when everyone thinks alike, but when people possess the freedom and courage to question, debate and rethink what they have inherited. Every generation receives beliefs, customs, institutions and social practices from the past. Some enrich human life; others may perpetuate inequality simply because they have acquired the authority of tradition. The true measure of a mature society, therefore, is not how faithfully it preserves its inheritance, but how intelligently it examines it. In the Indian context, this becomes particularly important when we reflect upon caste, religion and patriarchy. These are not merely abstract concepts. They influence family life, marriage, social status, personal choices and opportunities. Yet meaningful discussion of them is often displaced by sentiment, identity politics, unquestioned authority or fear of disagreement. What India needs is not less tradition or less faith, but more reasoned discourse about their social consequences.

I. Caste, Religion and Patriarchy: Examining the Inherited Order

Caste is one of the most enduring forms of social stratification in India. It historically connects social status with birth and influences occupation, marriage, social interaction, and access to resources. B. R. Ambedkar’s Annihilation of Caste remains a foundational challenge to a social order in which birth becomes the basis of hierarchy. His analysis also highlighted endogamy—the practice of marrying within the group—as a mechanism through which caste boundaries are reproduced. The fundamental question is simple: Can the circumstances of one’s birth legitimately determine one’s dignity, status or opportunities? Modern India has transformed caste through constitutional equality, education, democratic politics, social mobility and affirmative action. Yet caste continues to influence matrimonial choices, political mobilisation, social networks and community identities. The challenge, therefore, is neither to deny caste nor to reduce it to a political slogan, but to understand how an inherited hierarchy adapts to modern conditions.

Religion raises a different but equally important question. Religion has provided meaning, morality, community and spiritual consolation to millions. It cannot simply be dismissed as superstition. A democratic society must protect freedom of belief. But freedom of belief must coexist with freedom of inquiry. When religious claims influence public behaviour or decisions concerning health and human welfare, they necessarily become open to discussion. The growing influence of charismatic spiritual figures and the wider “Baba culture” makes the question of authority especially relevant. Spiritual guidance may be valuable, but spiritual status should not automatically confer unquestionable authority. Patriarchy presents a third dimension of inherited social organisation. Traditional gender roles have often assigned authority, responsibility and freedom differently to men and women. Simone de Beauvoir demonstrated how social expectations can transform biological difference into unequal social possibilities. The question is not whether men or women are superior. It is whether gender should predetermine freedom, dignity, security and opportunity. Caste, religion and patriarchy frequently intersect within the family, marriage and community, where identities and expectations are transmitted across generations.

II. India’s Own Tradition of Questioning

The call for reasoned discourse should not be presented as an imported Western idea. India possesses a long and diverse intellectual tradition of questioning, argument and dissent. The Buddha challenged unquestioned authority and encouraged inquiry into suffering, conduct and knowledge. His intellectual approach placed emphasis on understanding rather than merely accepting claims on the basis of authority or tradition. The Charvaka or Lokayata tradition represents another striking strand of Indian intellectual history. Its materialist and sceptical orientation challenged metaphysical claims and questioned religious authority. Although much of what is known about Charvaka comes through its critics, its historical presence demonstrates that Indian thought included vigorous disagreement about religion, knowledge and reality. The Upanishadic dialogues similarly reveal a culture in which fundamental questions about existence and knowledge were explored through intellectual conversation.

author: ALR Editors
title: Announcing Asian Labour School Oct-Nov 2026 Semester
content:
Dear friends,


We are back with an amazing list of new and returning courses for the Asian Labour School. If you are interested in

acquiring democratic facilitation skills, navigating conflicts and taking collective care, working cooperatively, strengthening a union core or leading your own radical walking tours

, please check out the course information below and study with Asian Labour School.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Chie Matsumoto


We all have attended meetings where decisions were made by only a few members, most outspoken ones or someone at the top. We may have once thought, “Why am I even here?” and left without saying a word. Democracy starts in the smallest conversations, dialogues and meetings by raking in most diverse opinions and ideas, piecing them together to create something new and meaningful to all participants.


Building Movement Democracy through Democratic Facilitation (Course Starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Facilitators: Emi Do and Matt Noyes


Worker cooperatives are enterprises that are owned and governed by workers. When all of our working experiences have been in profit-maximizing enterprises, or in workplaces that are structured hierarchically, it is no wonder that we can encounter challenges when attempting to work together cooperatively. In this course we will explore the challenges and tensions when there are no bosses to hate!


Worker Cooperatives: Can Cooperating Transform How We Work Together? (Course Starts on Oct 10, 2026)


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Facilitator: Nash Tysmans


Movements are built through relationships. Yet the pressures of organizing (urgency, conflict, exhaustion, political disagreement, and unequal power) can strain those relationships and undermine our collective capacity. How can we build movements that are both effective in challenging injustice and caring in how we work together?


Careful, We’re Organizing aka How to Fight without Falling Apart (Course Starts on Oct 21, 2026)


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Facilitator: Sithar Chhim


In order to win any campaign at workplace, unions need to be strong enough to pressure the company. Building a strong and representative committee is the only way to win over the bosses who have well organized structure at workplace compare to workers.


Building Strong Union Committee at Workplace (Course starts on Oct 15, 2026)


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)


Facilitator: Kevin Lin


Have you ever thought about leading your own radical walking tour to share with friends the significance of places and histories in your city? Leading and participating in a radical walking tour is not only educational but fun and always memorable. A walking tour provides a concrete sense of places, people, and histories. This course will walk you through the conceptualisation, research and logistics of a radical walking tour, and hear ideas and experiences from other participants across Asia.


Designing Radical Walking Tours (Course Starts on Oct 12, 2026)

author: Unknown
title: MAF-DAD: Reasonable grounds to suspect war crimes in North and East Syria
content:
The Association for Democracy and International Law (MAF-DAD) has published its report, International Crimes Committed by and on Behalf of the Government of the Syrian Arab Republic, examining developments in North and East Syria in January and February 2026.


MAF-DAD’s independent Fact-Finding Mission investigated violations in North and East Syria following attacks on the Sheikh Maqsoud (Şêxmeqsûd) and Ashrafiah (Eşrefiyê) neighbourhoods of Aleppo in early January 2026. Members of the mission conducted field investigations in the region between 21 February and 17 March 2026.


The report said 32 detailed qualitative interviews were conducted as part of the fieldwork, involving a total of 62 people. Those interviewed included 25 direct victims, one victim’s family and six representatives of institutions and organisations involved in documenting violations or assisting victims.


MAF-DAD said the report was based on a comparative assessment of statements from victims and witnesses, direct field observations, medical records, reports by institutions and civil society organisations, evidence collected by the Rojava Information Center (RIC) and open-source material. The report applied the standard of “reasonable grounds to believe” that a violation had occurred.


Attacks on civilians


The report said attacks on civilians in January 2026 were concentrated particularly in the Sheikh Maqsoud and Ashrafiah neighbourhoods of Aleppo and along routes leading out of Tabqa and Raqqa (Reqa).


The field investigation documented drone strikes, artillery fire, sniper attacks, gunfire directed at vehicles, violence at checkpoints, attacks on areas where civilians had sought shelter and direct attacks on homes.


The report also included testimony that civilians attempting to flee Tabqa and Raqqa came under fire, were stopped, searched, robbed and detained, and in some cases killed.


MAF-DAD concluded that the evidence provided reasonable grounds to believe that civilians had been deliberately and indiscriminately targeted and that these acts constituted serious violations of international humanitarian law and war crimes.


Hospitals and healthcare workers targeted


The report examined attacks on healthcare infrastructure in Sheikh Maqsoud and Ashrafiah in a separate section.


MAF-DAD said Xalid Fecir Hospital and Osman Hospital were targeted by artillery fire. Evidence was also collected indicating that healthcare workers had been injured, detained, disappeared and killed.


The report said attacks on healthcare infrastructure and medical personnel were not isolated incidents, but formed part of a broader pattern in which protected medical facilities and personnel were systematically endangered or directly targeted. MAF-DAD said there were reasonable grounds to believe that these acts constituted war crimes.


Detention, torture and enforced disappearances


The report said cases of detention and disappearance occurred following the capture of Sheikh Maqsoud and Ashrafiah and at checkpoints along routes used by fleeing civilians.


Witnesses said men were separated from women and children, detainees were held in severely overcrowded facilities and their families were given no information about them.


People interviewed by MAF-DAD reported beatings, electric shocks, blindfolding, handcuffing, forced confessions and statements, inadequate food and water, poor hygiene and denial of access to healthcare.


The report said there were reasonable grounds to believe that these practices could constitute war crimes, including arbitrary detention, cruel treatment, torture, enforced disappearance or hostage-taking. It added that, where the necessary legal requirements were met, they could also amount to crimes against humanity.


Mutilation and humiliation of the dead


The report also documented serious violations involving the bodies of the dead.


MAF-DAD said it had examined direct photographic and video evidence showing the mutilation of bodies, the public display of corpses, the cutting of women’s hair or braids, the removal of tattoos from bodies and the severing of certain body parts.


Witnesses also said families had been prevented from burying the dead with dignity and that bereaved relatives had been subjected to degrading treatment.


The report said these acts were accompanied by racist, sectarian and sexist insults. MAF-DAD found reasonable grounds to believe that the acts were intended to humiliate and intimidate …

author: Danilo Arao
title: Discord
content:
Para sabihin ng gobyernong pang-gamer lang ang Discord ay napakairesponsable dahil wala itong respeto sa datos.

Hindi pinag-isipan. Walang pakialam.

Nagdesisyon ang gobyernong i-ban ang Discord dahil ginagamit diumano ng masasamang elemento. Wala pang 24 na oras, ibinalik muli ang app na ito dahil sa reklamo ng malawak na mamamayan. Humingi ng paumanhin ang ilang opisyal ng gobyerno. Ang dating na-block, naibalik na.

Tapos na ba ang isyu? Hindi. Sinasalamin kasi nito ang kawalan ng pag-iingat sa pagpapatupad ng mga polisiya. Importante ring isakonteksto ang pagdedesisyon sa limitado o wala talagang konsultasyon sa mga apektado.

Para sa mga hindi pamilyar sa Discord, ginagamit ang app na ito bilang linya ng komunikasyon sa internet. May bentahe ito para sa mga may limitadong koneksiyon dahil mababa lang ang bandwidth na nakokonsumo nito. Kahit na medyo bumabagal lalo na kung marami ang nag-uusap, nakakaya pa namang mababa ang bandwidth lalo na kung naka-off ang lahat ng kamera (at siyempre’y audio at chat lang ang pinapagana).

Akala ng mga nasa kapangyarihan, mga gamer lang ang gumagamit nito. Kung sabagay, mabilis kasi ang audio call sa mga online gamer na naglalaro kaya nakakagawa sila ng estratehiya para matalo ang kalaban. Pero kahit na sikat ito sa gaming community, hindi maikakaila ang pakinabang nito sa mga guro lalo na noong pandemya.

Sa paggawa ng Discord server, posibleng magkaroon ng “virtual classroom” lalo na para sa mga guro’t estudyanteng nagtitipid sa bandwidth. Batay sa personal na karanasan, mabilis ang uploading ng mga electronic file sa server, pati na ang posting ng mga announcement. At ang pinakaimportante, sa server mismo ginagawa ang mga video call na nagsisilbing online classes.

Hindi man kasing-high tech tulad ng Google Meet, Microsoft Teams at Zoom, libreng nagagamit ang Discord. Hindi kailangan ng paid subscription para sa unlimited na meetings at voice calls. Sa libreng account ay puwede ring magkaroon ng hanggang 100 partisipante sa isang group call kahit na limitado lang ang puwedeng mag-video streaming. Kung ikukumpara sa Zoom na hanggang 40 minuto lang ang isang online meeting, iba pa rin ang bentahe ng Discord!

Sa ganitong konteksto dapat suriin kung bakit maraming gumagamit ng Discord sa Pilipinas. Dahil 97% ng mobile users ay gumagamit ng prepaid, mahalaga ang bawat piso ng load at bawat gigabyte ng mobile data. Baka hindi ito alam ng mga nasa kapangyarihan dahil kasama sila sa mga pinagpalang may postpaid accounts na kayang magbayad ng libo-libo bawat buwan, bukod pa sa mabilis na Internet connection sa opisina at maging sa bahay.

Mahalaga ang datos sa mobile telephony dahil 98.8% ng internet users ay gumagamit ng cellphone para makakonekta. Kahit na may mga bahay namang may internet access at posibleng gamitin ang router para mabigyan ng koneksiyong wifi ang cellphone, lumalabas na 48.8% lang ito ng mga bahay sa buong Pilipinas.

Sa madaling salita, may tendensya talaga ang maraming Pilipinong magtipid ng load at bandwidth sa paggamit ng mga app lalo na sa komunikasyon. Para sabihin ng gobyernong pang-gamer lang ang Discord ay napakairesponsable dahil wala itong respeto sa datos.

Hindi pinag-isipan. Walang pakialam. Huwag nang magulat kung basta-basta na lang naglalabas ng desisyon nang walang malalim na pananaliksik.

Sino ba naman sa mga tagagobyerno ang gumagamit ng Discord samantalang may pambayad naman sila sa premium services ng iba pang app para sa komunikasyon? Handang nilang ipagbawal ang mga bagay na wala silang alam. Palibhasa, hindi sila apektado!

Tapos na ba ang isyu? Hindi. Tandaang ganitong klaseng gobyerno mayroon sa Pilipinas. Humingi man ng kapatawaran sa nangyari, hindi pa rin katanggap-tanggap ang disposisyon nila.

author: Brian Hioe
title: Does China Intend to Target Taiwan With New National Security Legislation?
content:
TAIWANESE GOVERNMENT officials, speaking under conditions of anonymity to the media, have warned that China may roll out national security legislation directed at Taiwan in the coming months. Such national security legislation would follow up on China’s recently passed ethnic unity law.

The law criminalizes actions aimed at disrupting a vaguely defined “national unity”. Although initial warnings were that the law was mainly aimed at Tibetans and Uyghurs, the Lai administration has framed such national security legislation as potentially a threat to Taiwan. Under such laws, after all, support for Taiwanese independence–or even just maintaining Taiwan’s current democratic freedoms and its de facto independence–could be construed as illegal and criminal under the law.

Such Taiwanese government officials have pointed to a number of laws, some of which are still in the review process, as potentially impacting Taiwan. This includes the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration, Measures for the Supervision and Inspection of Cyberspace Security, and National Defense Mobilization Law.

In particular, the Regulations of the State Council on Exit and Entry Administration could be used to prevent Taiwanese who have traveled to China from leaving. This already occurred in the past, however, most prominently in the case of activist Lee Ming-che, who spent over five years in Chinese jails on charges of seeking to subvert the state. Lee is thought to have been detained over exchanges with Chinese friends on Taiwan’s experiences regarding democratization. Others imprisoned, however, have been noted to include pan-Blue academics, who seem to have fallen afoul of espionage charges in spite of pro-unification viewpoints.

Measures on cybersecurity take place at a time when the Chinese government has attempted to depict Taiwan as engaged in cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. Such allegations seem to be an attempt to depict Taiwan as engaged in the same activity it routinely accuses China of being engaged in, seeing as China consistently conducts cyberattacks on Taiwan and probes key infrastructure. Importantly, such allegations could also be used to cement a casus belli to justify war.

Indeed, to this extent, the National Defense Mobilization Law has been warned as potentially intended to provide the legal grounds for wartime mobilization. Indeed, such a law might be necessary ahead of a Chinese invasion, particularly if the Chinese government intends to move Chinese society as a whole toward war footing, and mobilize all of society to conduct an invasion.

Still, at a time of highly polarized politics between the KMT and DPP, it can be expected that the KMT will probably deny that China has intentions for future national security legislation. KMT chair Cheng Li-wun has, of course, attempted to depict China as only having goodwill toward Taiwan, while depicting the DPP as, in fact, the ones who have sought to provoke China. As such claims to the media are made ahead of elections in November, they will be depicted as simply intended to drum up public fear for the sake of electioneering.
