title: Εκδηλώσεις και δράσεις, Κυριακή 20/9
content:
>Πορεία για τα 2 χρόνια της δολοφονίας του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν – Άγ. Παντελεήμονα


>Συμπεράσματα από τον νικηφόρο αγώνα ενάντια στη δυνητική αργία – διαδικτυακή ενημέρωση


>Διήμερο γενεθλίων | 1 χρόνος Αυτοδιαχειριζόμενο Στέκι Βόλου


>19η Αντιρατσιστική Γιορτή – Πάντειο


>Εκδήλωση για την εργοδοτική δολοφονία του Μανώλη Αφράτη – Rosa Nera


>Αντιφασιστική εκδήλωση – Πάτρα


>Πορεία για τα 2 χρόνια της δολοφονίας του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν


ΑΚΟΜΑ ΜΙΑ ΚΡΑΤΙΚΗ ΔΟΛΟΦΟΝΙΑ, ΑΚΟΜΑ ΜΙΑ ΣΥΓΚΑΛΥΨΗ. Ο ΜΟΧΑΜΕΝΤ ΚΑΜΡΑΝ ΔΟΛΟΦΟΝΗΘΗΚΕ ΑΠΟ ΤΗΝ ΕΛΛΗΝΙΚΗ ΑΣΤΥΝΟΜΙΑ.


Στις 21 Σεπτεμβρίου 2024, ο Μοχάμεντ Καμράν Ασίκ δολοφονήθηκε από αστυνομικούς στο Α.Τ. Αγίου Παντελεήμονα. Τον Ιανουάριο του 2026, ο εισαγγελέας Σωτήρης Μπουγιούκος αποφάσισε να αρχειοθετήσει την υπόθεση, ισχυριζόμενος ότι δεν υπήρχαν επαρκή στοιχεία για να παραπεμφθεί σε δίκη. Ως αποτέλεσμα, δεν υπάρχουν πλέον νομικά μέσα για τη συνέχιση της υπόθεσης στα ελληνικά δικαστήρια. Οι αστυνομικοί που τον ξυλοκόπησαν μέχρι θανάτου συνεχίζουν τη ζωή τους χωρίς καμία συνέπεια.


Ο Μοχάμεντ Καμράν Ασίκ, εργάτης από το Πακιστάν, συνελήφθη, μεταφέρθηκε και κρατήθηκε σε πέντε διαδοχικά αστυνομικά τμήματα, όπου υπέστη επανειλημμένη σωματική βία, χωρίς ουσιαστική επικοινωνία με την οικογένειά του ή πρόσβαση σε νομική υποστήριξη. Στις 21 Σεπτεμβρίου 2024 βρέθηκε νεκρός μέσα στο Αστυνομικό Τμήμα Αγίου Παντελεήμονα, στον μοναδικό χώρο που δεν είχε κάλυψη από κάμερες. Ακόμα και η ίδια η κρατική ιατροδικαστική πραγματογνωμοσύνη κατέληξε στο συμπέρασμα ότι ο θάνατός του προκλήθηκε από ισχαιμία του μυοκαρδίου, ως αποτέλεσμα έντονου σωματικού και ψυχικού στρες που συνδέεται με τον συνεχή ξυλοδαρμό κατά την κράτησή του.


Τη δολοφονία του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν ακολούθησε εκτεταμένη συγκάλυψη της υπόθεσης (όπως τέτοια ακολούθησε και το κρατικό έγκλημα στην Πύλο). Οι αστυνομικοί του Α.Τ. Αγίου Παντελεήμονα ισχυρίστηκαν ότι «αυτοτραυματίστηκε λόγω στερητικού συνδρόμου αλκοόλ». Ο εισαγγελέας Σωτήρης Μπουγιούκος πολύ στοχευμένα παρέλειψε στην επίσημη αναφορά το ιατρικό συμπέρασμα που ξεκάθαρα αποδίδει την καρδιακή αποτυχία του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν ως αποτέλεσμα του εκτεταμένου και άγριου ξυλοδαρμού του. Αυτή η απόφαση είναι ξεδιάντροπη συγκάλυψη του βασανισμού και της δολοφονίας του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν από την ελληνική αστυνομία.


Όλα αυτά συνέβησαν στη γειτονιά του Αγίου Παντελεήμονα, μία από τις περιοχές όπου πολλοί άνθρωποι ωθήθηκαν να εγκατασταθούν εξαιτίας του ραγδαίου εξευγενισμού του κέντρου, διαμορφώνοντας έτσι τον πολύμορφο χαρακτήρα της. Άνθρωποι από την Αλβανία, τη Συρία, το Πακιστάν, το Μπαγκλαντές, το Αφγανιστάν, το Κονγκό, τη Σομαλία, την Αίγυπτο, τη Γεωργία και άλλες χώρες έχουν χτίσει τη ζωή τους σε αυτή τη γειτονιά και ακόμη περισσότεροι επιλέγουν να μετακομίσουν εκεί, λόγω των ήδη υπαρχόντων δικτύων και του κλίματος σχετικής ασφάλειας ή οικειότητας.


Σήμερα, η πλατεία Αγίου Παντελεήμονα δεν βρίσκεται πλέον υπό πολιορκία από τους νεοναζί της Χρυσής Αυγής, όπως την περίοδο 2010-2012, όταν το τοπικό αστυνομικό τμήμα είχε γίνει συνώνυμο των βασανιστηρίων μεταναστών και προσφύγων. Ο μακροχρόνιος αγώνας των κατοίκων για τη συγκρότηση κοινοτήτων αντιστάθηκε σε αυτή τη ρατσιστική βία. Παρ’όλα αυτά, τα κρατητήρια των αστυνομικών τμημάτων, οι συνεχείς έλεγχοι ταυτοποιητικών εγγράφων (που μπορεί να οδηγήσουν σε φυλάκιση σε κέντρα κράτησης ή και σε θάνατο) και η αδιάκοπη παρενόχληση στο δρόμο από την αστυνομία δείχνουν ότι η βία συνεχίζεται.


Επιπλέον, η βία έχει κλιμακωθεί στα σύνορα, μέσω των συνεχών επαναπροωθήσεων και δολοφονιών και στα κέντρα κράτησης όπως η Αμυγδαλέζα με τις ακραίες συνθήκες κράτησης, καθώς και με την απομόνωση στα στρατόπεδα συγκέντρωσης προσφύγων. Η αρχειοθέτηση της δολοφονίας του Μοχάμεντ Καμράν αποτελεί ξεκάθαρη συγκάλυψη από το κράτος, το δικαστικό σύστημα και την αστυνομία. Το κράτος και οι τραμπούκοι μπάτσοι του μπορούν πάντοτε να δρουν εκτός του πλαισίου της «νομιμότητας», τροποποιώντας τον νόμο όπως τους εξυπηρετεί και ασκώντας βία απέναντι σε όποιον στοχοποιούν ως απειλή για τη δική τους εξουσία, ενώ ταυτόχρονα οι φυλετικοποιημένοι άνθρωποι απανθρωποποιούνται από τα ΜΜΕ ώστε να παρενοχλούνται, να απελαύνονται, να ξυλοκοπούνται, να φυλακίζονται, να ποινικοποιούνται, να δολοφονούνται και να χαρακτηρίζονται «παράνομοι». Αυτή η δολοφονία δεν πρέπει να ιδωθεί ως μεμονωμένη πράξη κάποιων λίγων αστυνομικών, αλλά ως προϊόν ενός κράτους που έχει κανονικοποιήσει και προωθήσει τους θανάτους μη λευκών ανθρώπων, δικαιολογώντας τους μέσω της παρουσίασης των μεταναστών ως «εχθρού της πατρίδας» …

author: Leanne Sanders
title: Elections Alberta reports more than 655,000 requests for special ballots for Oct. 19 referendum
content:
There appears to be high voter interest in the Alberta referendum on Oct. 19 which will decide whether the province should pursue the formal process to separate from Canada.


“We received approximately 658,000 requests for special ballots,” an Elections Alberta news release said. “This is more than 11 times as many requests as the 2023 Provincial General Election, where we received 59,589 special ballot requests.”


Elections Alberta attributed the increase to “the new availability of special ballot voting to all eligible electors without a reason, that voters must vote within their Electoral Division for Advance Vote or at their assigned location for Election Day, voter interest, and the number of questions electors must vote on.”


More than 82 per cent of the special ballots have been approved for fulfilment and mailing, it noted, with “0.7 per cent rejected either at application or on return, and nearly 100,000 have been received back and approved, and those electors marked as voted.”


It also expects the “total requests number will change as all final requests received before the deadline are entered into the system.”


Treaty 8 Sovereign Nations in Alberta is reminding members that if they requested a special ballot, they must vote that way and not in person.


Treaty 8, which represents 22 First Nations in the province has been openly battling with Premier Danielle Smith over the referendum. It wrote a formal letter to Smith on June 6, demanding that the province “immediately cease any attempt to proceed with a separation referendum or related process without full consultation, accommodation, and the free, prior, and informed consent of the Treaty 8 First Nations.”


“The duty to consult is not a bureaucratic inconvenience. It is a constitutional obligation that arises whenever the Crown contemplates action, or authorizes processes under its authority, that may adversely affect Treaty rights,” wrote Grand Chief Trevor Mercredi.


“A referendum that could result in Alberta’s separation from Canada, and that would place an international border through Treaty 8 territory, represents one of the most profound adverse impacts on Treaty rights that it is possible to contemplate. The suggestion that such a process falls outside the duty to consult is not a tenable legal argument. It is a rationalization…”


A Court of King’s Bench judge quashed an initial petition for independence based on the province’s failure to uphold its duty to consult First Nations. On May 13, 2026, Alberta Justice Shaina Leonard ruled in favour of several First Nations whose lawyers argued that using Alberta’s referendum process for possible separation of Alberta from Canada has been unconstitutional because First Nations were not consulted and that separation under those circumstances would violate treaty rights.


Smith responded to the decision on May 21, and announced that Alberta would instead hold a referendum on whether to trigger the process for holding a binding referendum on Alberta separating from Canada.


Among the nine other questions Albertans will be asked to vote on are questions on the province “taking increased control over immigration for the purposes of decreasing immigration to more sustainable levels, prioritizing economic migration and giving Albertans first priority on new employment opportunities?”


There are also constitutional questions like “Do you support the government of Alberta working with the governments of other willing provinces to amend the Canadian Constitution to have provincial governments, and not the federal government, select the justices appointed to provincial King’s Bench and Appeal courts?”


Another asks “do you support the government of Alberta working with the governments of other willing provinces to amend the Canadian Constitution to abolish the unelected federal Senate?


According to Senate Government Representative’s Office (GRO), abolishment requires a formal constitutional amendment passed with the unanimous consent of the federal Parliament and all ten provincial legislatures.


The GRO “is responsible for both shepherding the Government’s legislation through the Senate in a timely manner and championing renewal in the changing institution. GRO senators represent the Government to the Senate, but they do not sit in a partisan caucus and do not lead a caucus

.”


Abolishing the Senate would also be difficult due to a landmark 2014 advisory opinion by the Supreme Court of Canada …

author: Julius Gavroche
title: A man died today in Ceuta
content:
On the 30th to the 31st of July, over 70,000 people crossed the Moroccan border into Ceuta, a Spanish territory adjacent to the African country. After the return to Morocco of most of those who crossed, some 10,000 people still

remain in Ceuta

 in precarious conditions, subject to all manner of deprivations and violence, predictable and unpredictable.


from

lundimatin

 #535, 28/09/2026


A man died today, Friday 25 September 2026, in Ceuta, near the showers at Playa del Trampolín.


Of Algerian origin and in his fifties, he collapsed in this area where, for nearly two months now, men who have arrived in Ceuta have been living. Paramedics attempted to resuscitate him for more than twenty minutes. He died at the scene. It was reported that he had been unwell for several days.


Since the end of July, men have been living in Trampolín in precarious conditions that are by no means accidental. They sleep on the beach, behind the rocks or against the walls of the old factory, in shelters made of tarpaulins, cardboard and pieces of wood. They wash in makeshift showers, rely on food handouts and, day by day, scour for the essentials they need to get by: water, a few items of clothing, a socket to charge a phone, a place to sleep without being evicted.


For weeks, however, they were described less in terms of what they were going through than in terms of the problem they were supposedly causing. There was talk of a “crisis”, an “invasion”, “migration pressure” and “security”. Arrivals were counted, movements monitored, whilst camps were destroyed, personal belongings burnt, and police operations multiplied, with the army deployed around the places where they were trying to live. A considerable amount of information was thus produced about them, whilst ignorance of who they actually were remained almost total.


This is perhaps one of the most routine operations at the border. It does not merely make certain crossings difficult or impossible, but also imposes a certain way of making people “readable”. It is not so much a matter of knowing them as of making them comprehensible within a system. The complexity of a person’s existence is thus replaced by the data necessary for their administration. Origin, status, and presence in a particular place become the means by which a person is identified and processed. What becomes visible is no longer necessarily life itself, but the position it occupies within a system that must be able to locate it, manage it or move it. This regime of visibility shows a great deal yet reveals little, since it brings positions to the fore rather than lives.


Anonymity does not, therefore, necessarily stem from a lack of knowledge. On the contrary, it may arise from abundant and meticulous knowledge, provided that this knowledge retains only those aspects of a person that render them governable. One may know almost everything about a person’s position within a system and yet know nothing about the person themselves. Erasure does not always involve invisibility and can take place amidst constant exposure, when what is seen of a person is gradually reduced to what can be recorded and administered. One can be continually identified without ever being truly known. What disappears, then, is not the body—precisely because it remains in full view—but the relationship through which that body might appear as belonging to a particular person.


We do not yet know the name of the person who died today. We know their origin, their approximate age, the place where they collapsed and the length of time for which the emergency services attempted to resuscitate them. This is the information that is circulating. Whilst it is necessary to describe what happened, it tells us almost nothing about the person to whom it happened. It allows us to situate an event without restoring the existence that it has cut short. Knowledge thus stops at the threshold of the person, as if the precision of the circumstances could take the place of knowledge of the person they concern.


He had a life before Trampolín. This fact, precisely because it should go without saying, deserves to be reiterated. Trampolín was neither the beginning nor the meaning of his life. He had known other places and other faces, spoken a language in which certain words needed no explanation. He had habits, connections and memories of which we know nothing. He had been awaited somewhere and had himself waited. He had crossed borders about which we still …

author: Slingshot robot #1
title: Know your rights with COPS
content:
These suggestions from the National Lawyers Guild “Know Your Rights” guide summarize the rules to which the police are theoretically subject. Be careful: the police, the courts, and the government can and do ignore these rules when they feel like it. Sometimes, police retaliate against people for exercising their rights. These tips may help you later on in court, and sometimes they won’t. Even though the state can’t be counted on to follow its own laws, it still may be helpful to know what these laws are so you can shame particular state agents or deal with particular situations. Use your best judgment — if you aren’t doing anything wrong, there may be no reason to be excessively paranoid or escalate a potentially innocent and brief encounter with a police officer who is just saying “hi” into an ugly situation by acting suspicious and refusing to say “hi” back. The point is to avoid giving information.

Providing this information isn’t intended to scare you into inactivity or make you paranoid. In the current context, the vast majority of radical projects proceed with no interference from the police. The police hassle and arrest people because they hope that such repression will frighten everyone else into submission. We can take reasonable precautions while continuing the fight for liberation.

Anything you say to an FBI agent or cop may be used against you and other people — even if the questions seem routine or harmless. You don’t have to talk to FBI agents, police or investigators on the street, if you’ve been arrested, or if you’re in jail. (Exceptions: Your name, date of birth and address are known as “Booking questions” which are not included in your right to remain silent. In some states you can get an additional minor charge for refusing to identify yourself after a police stop based on reasonable suspicion). Only a judge has the authority to order you to answer questions. Many activists have refused to answer questions, even when ordered by a judge or grand jury, and subsequently served jail time to avoid implicating others. It is common for the FBI to threaten to serve you with a grand jury subpoena unless you talk to them. Don’t be intimidated. This is frequently an empty threat, and if they are going to subpoena you, they will do so anyway. If you do receive a subpoena, call a lawyer right away.

Once you’ve been stopped or arrested, don’t try to engage cops in a dialogue or respond to accusations. If you are nervous about refusing to talk, you may find it easier to tell them to contact your lawyer. Once a lawyer is involved, the police sometimes back off. If you have already answered some questions, you can refuse to answer other questions until you have a lawyer. Don’t lie to the police or give a false name— lying to the police is a crime. The police are allowed to lie to you — don’t believe what they say. If you’ve been arrested, don’t talk about anything sensitive in police cars, jail cells or to other inmates — you are probably being recorded.

What To Do About Police Harassment On The Street

If the police stop you on the street, ask, “Am I free to go?” If yes, walk away. If not, you are being detained but this does not necessarily mean you will be arrested. Ask, “Can you explain why you are detaining me?” To stop you, cops must have specific reasons to suspect you of involvement in a specific crime. Police are entitled to pat you down during a detention. If the police try to further search you, your car, or your home, say repeatedly that you do not consent to the search, but do not physically resist.

What To Do If Police Visit Your Home

You do not have to let the FBI or police into your home or office unless they have a search warrant. If they have an arrest warrant you may limit entry if the person surrenders outside. In either case, ask to inspect the warrant. It must specifically describe the place to be searched and the things to be seized. You do not have to tell them anything other than your name and address. Tell the police that you can not consent to the search unless it is also inspected by a lawyer. If the officers ask you to give them documents, your computer, do not consent to them taking it. Physically trying to block them from searching or seizing items may escalate the situation. You have a right to observe what they do. You should take written notes of their names and what they do. Have friends act as witnesses.

title: The Movement to Abolish ICE Is Gaining Momentum
content:
As activists rally around federal legislation to dismantle ICE, Amnesty International joins the call for abolition.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Echoing activists across the country, the global human rights watchdog Amnesty International has called on the United States government to abolish Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Emerging from the #Not1More campaign organized by undocumented activists and groups like Puente and Juntos in 2014, and gaining momentum with concerted organizing by grassroots groups such as Mijente, Detention Watch Network, Freedom for Immigrants, La Resistencia, and many others, the movement to abolish ICE has been building for years.

However, to have a mainstream organization such as Amnesty International — which has 7 million members and a global budget nearing $400 million, and which is often turned to by corporate media outlets — officially endorsing the explicit call for abolition signals a shift in the movement’s momentum as public support for ICE dwindles.

While ICE has been accused of violating human rights since it was created in the early 2000s, the Trump administration’s racist mass deportation campaign has taken its abuses — including “unlawful killings by federal agents” — to a “perilous new level” that is putting the general public in danger, according to a new report released by Amnesty International on September 24.

In calling for ICE to be abolished, Amnesty International joins a growing movement to put an end to an agency that has invaded neighborhoods across the country with squads of violent, masked federal agents recruited under President Donald Trump. On September 24, a coalition of public officials, advocates for undocumented people, and civil rights groups lined up in support of the Reimagining Safety Act, federal legislation introduced by Rep. Delia Ramirez (D-Illinois) that would dismantle ICE and rebuild its parent agency, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), from the ground up.

“You cannot militarize our neighborhoods, surveil our families, and make people afraid to leave their homes and call that safety,” said Rep. Norma Hernandez, an Illinois state representative from Chicago, in a statement.

“ICE is not broken — it’s working exactly as intended, and that’s the problem.”

Meanwhile, the violence of mass deportation continues. ICE announced this week that Carlos Josué Marchena, a 36-year-old from Costa Rica, became the third person to die at a notorious immigration jail in Louisiana in less than six months on September 18.

Marchena reportedly told family members that he missed meals and the insulin shots he needed to control his diabetes. His story echoes widespread reports of medical neglect and the complaints made about inhumane conditions, which have sparked waves of hunger strikes by detainees. At least 55 people have died in ICE custody since Trump returned to office, including a record 31 deaths in 2025, according to Detention Watch Network. Experts suspect that is an undercount.

ICE has repeatedly claimed the medical care and conditions in its jails and prison camps are better than those in most hospitals and prisons, but polling suggests that a majority of voters are not buying these claims as the death count continues to rise. Videos of ICE officers apparently breaking the law while off-duty and violently violating basic constitutional rights of citizens and noncitizens alike when attempting to make arrests regularly go viral online.

“We’re going to keep pushing. We’re not going to apologize,” said Tom Homan, the White House border czar, in response to public scrutiny on September 24.

Trump and his senior officials unleashed masked and poorly trained ICE agents onto the streets while openly supporting violent and racist enforcement practices, creating an “institutional environment” for widespread abuses, according to Amnesty International’s report. The group, which examines human rights crises across the world, examined the large-scale, militarized ICE crackdowns that recently unfolded in the metro areas of Los Angeles; Washington, D.C.; Chicago; New Orleans; and the Twin Cities in Minnesota.

Researchers documented similar abuses in each city, including arbitrary arrests, harassment, intimidation, degrading treatment and unjustified use of force by federal agents, repression of protests with crowd-control …

title: Podcast: Beyond Borders with Khawaja Hammad Akbar (#NoWar2026 Preview)
content:
Asia, Culture of Peace, Demilitarization, How I Became a Peace Activist, Myth of Necessity, Nonviolent Activism, Podcasts, World BEYOND War Podcast

By Marc Eliot Stein, September 26, 2026, World BEYOND War

“Beyond Borders” is the theme of World BEYOND War’s #NoWar2026 online conference next month. To preview this conference, I spoke with Khawaja Hammad Akbar, a peace builder in Pakistan who will be leading a panel on case studies of militarized borders and demilitarized zones with speakers from Korea, Gaza and the US/Mexico border.

What does it mean to seek a world “beyond borders”? To begin exploring this question, I asked Khawaja about his own background and motivations for antiwar work and discovered that his interest began (as it so often does) with his desire to understand his own family legacy. As we talked about the devastation and trauma left behind by the 1947 India/Pakistan partition, a familiar pattern became clear: the borders of the past still imprison all of us.

We also talked about popular attitudes about militarism in our own societies, about our hopes for a better future, and about the inspiration of past teachers of peace like Syed Ahmad Khan. The closing music is an excerpt from a live recording of “Ballot Box” by Penboy, a singer and spoken word poet who will be performing at the #NoWar2026 conference which takes place October 23, 24 and 25.

title: MEP Lucano calls for Öcalan’s freedom
content:
The process that began following Abdullah Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and a Democratic Society is being closely followed not only in Turkey and Kurdistan but also across Europe. The progress of the process, the legal and political steps that need to be taken, and Öcalan’s status are among the key issues in international discussions.


One of the figures closely following these discussions is Domenico “Mimmo” Lucano, an Italian MEP. Lucano’s relationship with the Kurds dates back nearly 30 years, before he became mayor of Riace. In 1998, a boat carrying Kurdish refugees arrived in Riace, a small coastal town in Calabria. This became a turning point not only for the town but also for Lucano’s political life. The solidarity that began with the settlement of Kurdish refugees and the opening of vacant houses to them laid some of the foundations for the migrant reception experience that would later become internationally known as the “Riace model.”


 


Years later, after being elected to the European Parliament, Lucano described his bond with the Kurds in these words: “I became mayor thanks to the Kurds.” Referring also to Öcalan’s arrival in Italy in 1998, Lucano argues that Öcalan must be able to participate freely in the Peace and Democratic Society Process currently underway.


Speaking to ANF, Lucano discussed the story that began with Kurdish refugees on the shores of Riace, Öcalan’s time in Italy, and his views on the Peace and Democratic Society Process being pursued today.


My story with the Kurds began in Riace


Describing his first encounter with the Kurds, Lucano said that the arrival in Riace of Kurdish refugees from Turkey, Iraq, Iran, and Syria was a major turning point in his life. He said: “One day, a ship, a boat carrying a large number of Kurdish refugees from Turkey, Iraq, Iran, and, in smaller numbers, Syria arrived in Riace, in my municipality. I was a political activist, and from the very beginning, I embraced the ideals of the Kurdish people. These people stayed in my small town for two years. We allocated vacant houses to them, and together with them, I shared the Kurdish people’s political and social demands and their struggle for freedom.”


I became mayor thanks to the Kurds


Lucano said that the arrival of Kurdish refugees in Riace also played an important role in shaping his political life, and added that very little was known about the Kurds and the Kurdish question in the town at the time.


Describing the impact of the solidarity he built with the Kurds on his subsequent political life, Lucano said: “I became mayor, and a major part of that was my political struggle and my encounter with a people whose existence nobody in my town had previously been aware of. I am talking about a people who arrived years ago on a sailing boat and reached the shores of my municipality.”


Lucano summed up the place of his relationship with the Kurds in his life with the words: “I became mayor thanks to the Kurds.”


Abdullah Öcalan never gave up, despite the harsh conditions


Lucano also addressed the events following Öcalan’s arrival in Italy in 1998, criticizing the political decisions made during the process that ultimately led to his imprisonment on Imralı. He said: “When Öcalan came to Italy, certain political agreements were subsequently made, and Öcalan was essentially deceived. This is what I learned from my Kurdish friends, with whom I experienced those events together. He was later captured in Kenya. I believe Italian politics also bore responsibility for this process at the time.”


Recalling Öcalan’s long and harsh period of imprisonment, Lucano said: “Despite these conditions and the passing years, Öcalan maintained his connection with the Kurdish people’s struggle for freedom. He has not regained his freedom since that day. Nevertheless, he continued to struggle alongside the Kurdish people for a dream of freedom, namely the freedom of the Kurdish people. I became one of the people who shared these ideals.”


Öcalan must be free and be one of the leading actors in the process


Commenting on the Peace and Democratic Society Process, Lucano highlighted the contradiction between Öcalan’s current conditions and the role he is expected to play in the process.

title: Breaking the Pretoria Architecture: How Ethiopia’s Fragmented Wars Converged into a Single Existential Threat
content:
When the Pretoria Cessation of Hostilities Agreement was signed in November 2022, international observers prematurely celebrated the end of one of this century’s most devastating conflicts. The silence of the guns in Tigray was treated as a definitive roadmap toward peace. What the international community failed to see was that the Pretoria architecture did not resolve Ethiopia’s core systemic collapse; it merely localized and delayed it.


During my two years working from the African Union Headquarters in Addis Ababa as the Somali Youth Representative to the AU (2019–2021), I watched the foundational blocks of this conflict harden up close. Even then, within the diplomatic corridors of the capital, the fragile nature of the state’s security architecture was undeniable. The structural fragmentation we feared has now reached a critical flashpoint. Forces that fought on bitterly opposing sides during the Tigray war—most notably the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) and the Amhara Fano national movement—have crossed a seemingly impossible ideological chasm. Beside the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), they have forged a sweeping, nationwide military coalition with four other regional factions: the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF), the Afar Revolutionary Democratic Unity Front (Ugugumo), the Benishangul Peoples’ Liberation Movement, and the Gumuz Peoples’ Democratic Movement.


A man passes a destroyed tank on the main street of Edaga Hamus, Tigray region, Ethiopia, during a previous conflict on 5 June 2021. Credit: Yan Boechat/VOA.


Operating collectively under a newly unveiled banner—the

Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival

—their stated objective is clear: the total military removal of Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s federal government and the installation of an inclusive transitional charter. For an international audience, the danger is no longer just localized ethnic insurgencies. It is the structural disintegration of East Africa’s most pivotal state, threatening to pull its neighbors into a multi-theater regional war.


 


The Blood Feud: Turning Guns on Former Allies


The emergence of the Alliance for Survival completely upends the strategic math within Ethiopia. To understand how remarkable—and fragile—this coalition is, an international audience must understand that these factions have historically been locked in vicious, existential blood feuds. During the 2020–2022 Tigray war, Amhara Fano militias did not just passively support the state; they fought on the frontlines alongside the federal military to systematically crush Tigrayan forces. That conflict was defined by horrific, ethnically driven atrocities, millions of displaced people, and a bitter territorial dispute over Western Tigray—a fertile border corridor that both ethnic groups still claim as ancestral land. Concurrently, deep-seated friction between the country’s two largest ethnic groups, the Oromo and the Amhara, has continuously fueled a volatile power struggle over central authority.


Yet, federal overreach and absolute political exclusion have achieved the seemingly impossible: turning yesterday’s battlefield enemies into co-conspirators against the political centre. The initial cracks widened significantly in June 2026, when the federal government proceeded with a general election that was heavily boycotted by major opposition parties. As

reported by Addis Standard

, systemic intimidation, mass arrests of political dissidents, and a complete lack of independent oversight meant the opposition’s withdrawal left an uncontested ballot. This closed off any remaining peaceful pathways to genuine power-sharing, serving as the ultimate catalyst for regional armed factions to formalize their battlefield coordination.


The final diplomatic pillar collapsed when the TPLF officially declared that the Pretoria peace agreement is no longer valid. TPLF spokespersons confirmed to international monitors that the accord was spent, citing the federal government’s failure to return displaced populations to their homes, resolve constitutional regional borders, and stabilize basic security infrastructure as promised. By treating the peace deal as void, the TPLF removed the last legal and diplomatic boundaries keeping them from aligning with active regional insurgencies—including the Amhara Fano factions, who have effectively frozen federal territorial control outside major urban centres following the state’s 2023 mandate to forcibly …

title: Gov’t grants Mary Jane Veloso absolute pardon after 16 years
content:
May Jane Veloso is welcomed by her family at the Correctional Institute for Women in Mandaluyong City, Dec. 18. (Photo by Deo Montesclaros/ Pinoy Weekly)

Veloso’s freedom was not granted voluntarily but was won through years of struggle by her family, lawyers, and supporters.

MANILA — Nearly two years since her return to the Philippines in December 2024, Mary Jane Veloso has been granted an absolute pardon by Ferdinand Marcos Jr., ending more than 16 years of detention stemming from a drug trafficking case in Indonesia.

“Pinirmahan ko na yung pardon niya kahapon,” (I already signed [the pardon] yesterday) Ferdinand Marcos Jr. told reporters during an interview in Eastern Samar.

The development came after Malacañang Press Officer Claire Castro said the president was “seriously considering” granting Veloso an absolute pardon. Veloso had been sentenced to death in Indonesia after authorities accused her of carrying 2.6 kilograms of heroin in 2010.

She was granted last-minute reprieve following international pressure on the Indonesian government.

Veloso’s lawyers from the National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) welcomed the decision, describing it as a “long-awaited act” that brings immeasurable relief to Veloso, her family, and the many supporters who stood by her throughout her years of detention.

Prior to the pardon, Veloso sent a handwritten letter to Chief Justice Alexander Gesmundo, reiterating that she was serving a sentence of reclusion perpetua despite what she said was the absence of any legal basis for such classification.

The NUPL also questioned Veloso’s continued detention after her transfer to the Philippines on December 18, 2024. The group argued that the Philippine government had no legal authority to continue enforcing a foreign criminal judgment in the absence of a treaty governing the transfer of sentenced prisoners.

Read: Lawyers, parents of Mary Jane Veloso urge SC to act on habeas corpus petition

Gabriela Women’s Party Rep. Sarah Elago said Veloso’s freedom was not granted voluntarily but was won through years of struggle by her family, lawyers, and supporters.

“Mary Jane should have been freed long ago. For years, we have asserted that she was a victim of human trafficking and exploitation, not a criminal who deserved punishment. Her release is a recognition of the long struggle to correct a grave injustice,” Elago said in Filipino.

She added that Veloso’s case reflects broader conditions that force millions of Filipinos to seek work abroad because of low wages, poverty, and the lack of decent jobs.

Elago further said, “As long as a system that relies on cheap labor and forced migration remains in place, our fellow Filipinos will continue to be vulnerable to trafficking, exploitation, and other forms of abuse.”

Migrante International also welcomed the grant of absolute pardon, describing it as a victory born from years of collective struggle, including vigils, rallies, protest actions, petition drives, letter and phone campaigns, and lobbying efforts.

“At the heart of this global campaign is the sheer determination of Mary Jane’s parents and family who did not waver in their commitment to pursue justice despite all the odds they faced,” Migrante said.

While welcoming the pardon, however, the group stressed that Veloso’s freedom was “long overdue,” saying the Marcos administration had also committed a grave injustice by prolonging her detention in a Philippine prison for one year and nine months despite the absence of charges against her in Philippine courts.

“Our campaign does not end here,” Migrante said. “This victory gives us the inspiration, courage and fuel to advance our movement to free migrant workers from exploitation and assert their full economic, social and political rights abroad and at home.”

For the NUPL, Veloso’s case has become emblematic of the plight of migrant workers and trafficking victims.

“Mary Jane’s story is one of extraordinary courage and resilience,” the group said in a statement, noting that despite coming perilously close to execution, Veloso never lost hope.

“She became a powerful symbol of the struggles endured by countless Filipinos driven abroad by necessity and made vulnerable to trafficking and exploitation,” the NUPL added.

“Her freedom is cause for celebration. It is also a reminder of why trafficking victims must be met first with protection, compassion, and justice, and why no victim should have to spend years fighting simply to be …

content:
Dossier


„… In den letzten Jahren sind die Regierungen in mehreren lateinamerikanischen Ländern von einer Welle rechtsgerichteter, liberal-konservativer politischer Akteure übernommen worden. Auf der Grundlage klassischer neoliberaler und konservativer Programme gewannen Nayib Bukele in El Salvador, Daniel Noboa in Ecuador, Jair Bolsonaro in Brasilien und Javier Milei in Argentinien die Präsidentschaftswahlen in ihren Ländern. Obwohl es Bolsonaro 2022 nicht gelang, seine Amtszeit als Präsident zu verlängern, befürworteten rund 50 Prozent der brasilianischen Wähler seine ultrarechte Agenda. Dadurch steht die politische Macht des siegreichen Sozialdemokraten Lula da Silva auf wackeligen Füßen. Im Falle Perus wurde der linksgerichtete Präsident Pedro Castillo durch seine frühere Vizepräsidentin Dina Boluarte ersetzt – mit der Zustimmung und der unmittelbaren Allianz der Ultrarechten im Kongress…“

Beitrag des Redaktionsausschusses Minga

in der Übersetzung von Susanne Schartz-Laux am 22. März 2024 in amerika21


 und mehr daraus/dazu:


Was die extreme Rechte in Lateinamerika so stark macht


„Auf dem lateinamerikanischen Kontinent schreitet eine reaktionäre Welle voran. Mit Ausnahme von Mexiko und Brasilien – den beiden Großmächten der Region – sowie Uruguay und Guatemala haben die übrigen Länder (Argentinien, Chile, Kolumbien, Bolivien, Peru, Ecuador, Paraguay, El Salvador, Honduras, Panama usw.) autoritäre rechtsextreme Regierungen gewählt, auch wenn teilweise in Stichwahlen und mit knapper Mehrheit. Dabei handelt es sich um Regierungen, die eine Bevölkerungsstimmung der Feindseligkeit und der politischen Aggressivität zum Ausdruck bringen. Es ist nicht dieselbe traditionelle liberale oder „republikanische“ Rechte, die den triumphierenden Neoliberalismus der 1980er Jahre prägte. (…) Die extreme Rechte von heute verspricht keine Zukunft des Weltfriedens auf der Grundlage der Märkte, sondern eine apokalyptische Säuberung von den Gottlosen, die sich den „natürlichen“ Hierarchien widersetzen: Arbeitgeber:innen über Arbeitnehmer:innen, Mann über der Frau, „weiße“ Hautfarbe über alle anderen people of colour und Reiche über den Armen. (…)


Im Gegensatz zu früheren Phasen des Aufstiegs der extremen Rechten in Lateinamerika, die jeweils 30 Jahre andauerten, stützen sich die aktuellen Kräfte jedoch auf ein unvollständiges und kurzsichtiges Gesellschaftsprojekt, das wirtschaftlich gesehen den weltweiten Trends zuwiderläuft. (…)Doch wenn diese extreme Rechte kein hoffnungsvolles Wirtschaftsprogramm vorlegen kann, wieso verfügt sie dann trotzdem über eine beträchtliche Wählerschaft? Eine Ursache ist sicherlich die Enttäuschung über die progressiven Kräfte, die die Wirtschaftskrise (Inflation, Versorgungsengpässe, Rezession) nicht überwinden konnten. Doch diese Erklärung allein reicht nicht aus.


Die radikale Rechte zieht mit zwei Schwertern ins Feld, die ihre hohen Zustimmungswerte erklären: Zum einen ist es das Versprechen, einige der wichtigsten Gründe der Wirtschaftskrise zu bekämpfen, und zum anderen das Versprechen, den von der Krise Geschädigten moralische Wiedergutmachung widerfahren zu lassen. Das erste Schwert zerfällt rasch und unwiderruflich; das zweite jedoch wird mit feuriger Geschicklichkeit geschwungen. Der rachsüchtige Hass der neuen Staatsräson gegen Menschenrechte, Migrant:innen, Linke, Kommunist:innen, die Kirchnerist:innen, Indigene, Feministinnen oder jeden Anflug von sozialer Gleichheit spielt die Rolle einer kollektiven Buße, die vom gescheiterten Wohlstandsversprechen ablenkt. Wenn es schon keine glückliche Zukunft gibt, dann soll es wenigstens das Vergnügen an der Grausamkeit geben. Opfer sind diejenigen, die sich als unversöhnlich anders betrachten. Diese moralische Perversion der Hoffnung zerreißt das soziale Gefüge. Und auch wenn sie nur von kurzer Dauer ist, werden ihre Folgen für den gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhalt lange anhalten. Man kann ihr nicht allein mit umgekehrter Wut begegnen. Auch wenn in Krisenzeiten eine Personifizierung der Schuldigen für soziale Missstände notwendig ist – nur dass sie sich in diesem Fall auf eine winzige Minderheit der Mächtigen konzentriert –, ist vor allem eine mutige Wiederherstellung einer glaubwürdigen Hoffnung auf ein produktivistisches und auf soziale Gerechtigkeit ausgerichtetes Projekt erforderlich. author: Unknown
title: Acqua e Terre
content:
Perché un’azienda italiana del comparto digitale sta comprando centrali idroelettriche e miniere?


Da Orizzonti

*


Un’impresa privata italiana acquista centrali idroelettriche e miniere. Non siamo nel 1926, ma nel 2026, l’impresa in questione non produce tessuti, ma offre servizi internet.


E’ di pochi mesi fa infatti la notizia che Aruba ha comprato tre centrali idroelettriche in Piemonte

1

 e ha conquistato le quote di maggioranza della Società Mineraria Gerrei a Silius in Sardegna

2

. Perché un’azienda impegnata nel digitale fa investimenti in settori che richiamano l’alba del capitalismo industriale nel nostro paese?


Partiamo dall’inizio: Aruba è una società italiana fondata nel 1994 a Firenze, inizialmente forniva connessioni dial-up (per capirci la famosa 56k, quella col modem analogico che faceva i rumori e occupava la linea fissa telefonica di casa), poi offerte di registrazione di dominio per i siti internet ed hosting. Aruba apre un primo Data Center in Italia nel 2003 ad Arezzo a cui poi se ne affiancherà un secondo. Un terzo è stato costruito a Ponte San Pietro (Bergamo) nel 2017 all’interno di un ex-cotonificio ed è alimentato anche con energia idroelettrica. Infine un ultimo Data Center sul territorio italiano di livello hyperscaler

3

 è stato inaugurato nel 2024 a Roma all’interno del Tecnopolo Tiburtino

4

. Nel tempo l’azienda ha vantato collaborazioni con università, Pubblica Amministrazione e si è espansa a livello internazionale fornendo servizi in Europa Orientale e Centrale attraverso altri data center presenti in Germania, Francia, Inghilterra e Polonia. Nel panorama del capitalismo italiano Aruba è un’anomalia perché è riuscita a competere nel suo settore sul mercato europeo con i pesi massimi delle big tech statunitensi, pur rimanendo, nel solco delle dinastie della borghesia italiana, un’azienda a gestione familiare. Stefano Cecconi, amministratore delegato di Aruba, in una delle rare interviste

5

 reperibili in rete sintetizza così l’approccio:

“Siamo una società della new economy che ha avuto un approccio old economy. Non abbiamo cercato investitori esterni, ma semmai di reinvestire nella società. Non dobbiamo convincere della bontà di un progetto qualcun altro che non vive tutti i giorni il nostro settore. Il segreto di un’impresa familiare è la libertà di poter rischiare, la determinazione che si genera quando si lavora in proprio a tutti gli effetti e si rischia il patrimonio della famiglia stessa”

. Questa peculiarità oggi potrebbe rappresentare un vantaggio inaspettato, in tempi in cui la questione della sovranità nel campo dei dati e del digitale diventa un tema strategico sul piano geopolitico.


Ciò che rende il caso Aruba interessante per noi è proprio questa compresenza di elementi di estrema modernità integrati con il recupero di centralità di tecnologie, forme di organizzazione e modi di produzione che sembravano anticaglie del passato industriale italiano. Non c’è da stupirsi particolarmente, la rivoluzione dell’Intelligenza Artificiale richiede intensività ed estensività dello sfruttamento di risorse e lavoro. Questo significa che, come già successo in passato in occasione delle altre Rivoluzioni Industriali, la catena del valore torna a distendersi oltre che nello spazio, anche nel tempo recuperando in chiave nuova le tecnologie basali del capitalismo. Come scrivevamo

qui

:


Ogni grammo di materia prima, ogni goccia di sudore devono essere catturati per non rimanere indietro nella competizione globale.


Acqua


L’alba del capitalismo italiano si è basata quasi interamente sulla forza dell’acqua. Prima come fonte di energia diretta attraverso i mulini ad acqua che venivano utilizzati non solo per macinare i cereali, ma per azionare i mantici dei forni fusori, per attivare le pile idrauliche delle cartiere, per muovere le bielle delle segherie ecc… poi con l’idroelettrico. La disponibilità di acqua e legname resero le valli alpine tra i primi luoghi di insediamento industriale. Alcune di queste industrie insistevano su tradizioni precedenti, precapitalistiche, come il tessile nel biellese o l’industria armiera in Val Trompia.


Mappa dell’industrializzazione alpina nel periodo 1850-1880. Di Marcello Modica da

Revue de géographie alpine


La trasformazione dei paesaggi alpini fu impressionante e repentina. In molte delle valli interessate da questi primi cicli di industrializzazione esistono tutt’ora archeologie industriali di quell’epoca …

author: Unknown
title: Filikaya binen binene, tüm siyasi bağlantılar açıklanacak mı? 900 milyarlık fon vurgunu AKP’yi sallıyor
content:
Milyonlarca emeklinin ve asgari ücretlinin geçim savaşı verdiği, 26 Eylül’de Ankara'nın orta yerinde “Para için değil, onurumuz içim” diyerek Ali Şekeroğlu’nun ölümüne dair öfke artarken, 900 milyar liralık "fon ve borsa vurgunu" birkaç ayda milyarlar alan isimler açığa çıktı, AKP’ye uzandı. Ayrıca hakkında daha önce yurt dışına çıkış yasağı kararı verilen Tera Portföy Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Erdin Özel ve şirketin CEO'su Emir Münir Sarpyener dün gözaltına alındı. Erdin Özel'in gözaltı aracındaki kelepçeli fotoğrafı ve Münir Sarpyener'in kelepçeli görüntüleri Anadolu Ajansı tarafından basına servis edildi.

Fon vurgunu AKP içinde büyük bir krizin ve güç savaşının fitilini ateşledi. Skandalın patlak vermesinin ardından ifşa olan, hedef tahtasına oturtulan ilk isim eski Aile ve Sosyal Politikalar Bakanı, AKP MKYK Üyesi ve Genel Başkan Yardımcısı Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya oldu. Kamuoyunda yükselen tepkiler ve parti içinden gelen doğrudan çağrıların ardından Kaya, görevlerinden "affını" talep ederek istifa etti. Kaya’nın ‘görevden af’ talebi ise kabul edildi.

Soruşturmanın siyasi ayağına dair en somut verileri Yeni Parti Sözcüsü Zeynel Emre kamuoyuyla paylaştı. Emre, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ve eşi İlyas Kaya’nın borsa ve fon işlemleri üzerinden sadece 4 ay gibi kısa bir sürede milyarlarca liralık haksız kazanç sağladığını söyledi.

Emre, “Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, 8 Nisan tarihinde Özata Denizcilik hisselerinden 255 TL fiyatla 250 bin adet satın aldı. Toplamda 63 milyon 359 bin TL yatıran Kaya, Eylül ayına gelindiğinde hisseleri 4 bin 482 TL seviyesinden satarak 1 milyar 344 milyon TL nakit çekti. Eşi İlyas Kaya, aynı şekilde 255 TL’den 150 bin adet hisse alıp 99 milyon 687 bin TL yatırdı. Eylül ayında satarak 826 milyon TL elde etti” dedi.

Gelişmeler üzerine iddiaları sormak isteyen basın mensuplarına sadece "Müsait değilim" yanıtını veren Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, parti içinde de yalnız bırakıldı. AKP’li Şamil Tayyar sosyal medya hesabından çıkış yaparak, "İddialar doğruysa kabul edilemez, hemen istifa etmeli. Doğru değilse yalanlayıp dava açmalı. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı son 3 ayda fonlardan çıkış yapanların listesini istedi, haberiniz olsun" ifadelerini kullandı.

Aynı günün akşam saatlerinde açıklama yapan Kaya, görevlerinden "affını istediğini" duyurdu. AKP Sözcüsü Ömer Çelik ise istifanın ardından bir gün sonra adını anmadan "Her türlü yanlış, yolsuzluk ve usulsüzlükle mücadele tavizsiz verilecektir" açıklamasını yaptı.

Ayrıca basında yer alan iddialara göre, İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, eşi İlyas Kaya ve çocuklarının mal varlıklarına kısıtlama getirilmesini, gayrimenkul, araç ve menkul kıymetlerinin dondurulmasını talep etti. Kaya’nın, skandal patlak verdikten sonra partideki üst düzey isimlere "ağlayarak parayı iade etmeyi teklif ettiği" de iddialar arasında yer aldı.

Öte yandan skandalın kalbindeki şirketin patronunun Tuzla siyasetindeki geçmişi açığa çıktı. Soruşturma kapsamında gözaltına alınıp tutuklanan Özata Denizcilik’in Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı Özdemir Ataseven’in de AKP Tuzla İlçe Başkan Yardımcılığı yaptığı ve eski AKP’li Tuzla Belediye Başkanı Şadi Yazıcı’nın ekibinde yer aldığı belirlendi. Şirketin diğer tutuklu ismi Gökhan Ataseven’in de 2018 yılındaki nikâhını Şadi Yazıcı’nın kıydığı, şahitliklerini ise iktidar kanadından üst düzey siyasetçilerin yaptığı öğrenildi. Binali Yıldırım’a yakınlığıyla bilinen Ataseven ailesinin ticari ve siyasi merkez adresi ise yine Tuzla. Çağdaş Tuzla’da yer alan soruşturma detaylarına göre, fon üzerinden fiyatı yapay şekilde şişirilen Özata Denizcilik hisseleri için 9,7 milyar TL ödeme yapıldı ve binlerce küçük yatırımcı mağdur edildi. Şüpheli işlemlerin tespit edilmesiyle birlikte Özdemir Ataseven ve Gökhan Ataseven tutuklanarak cezaevine gönderildi.

Gazeteci Barış Pehlivan ise Özata Denizcilik’in yönetim kurulunda da kriz patlamadan hemen önce kritik bir ayrılık yaşandığını açıkladı. Pehlivan, şirketin yönetim kurulu üyesi İskender Balcı’nın aniden görevinden istifa ettiğini belirterek belgesini kamuoyuyla paylaştı.

Söz konusu istifayı, "Tıpkı hisselerini satıp milyar kazanan Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya gibi, filikaya binip gemiyi terk etme" olarak nitelendiren Barış Pehlivan, istifa eden İskender Balcı’nın Hazine ve Maliye Bakan Yardımcısı Osman Çelik’in damadı olduğu ortaya çıktı. Pehlivan, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda; "Memleketin hazinesini emanet ettiğimiz insanların pek 'akıllı' damatları nerelerden çıkıyor? Sahi …

author: rezgar2
title: Un arma de destrucción masiva sin explosión: la inteligencia artificial y el desmantelamiento de la mente humana
content:
REzgar Akrawi: Lo que tenemos hoy delante no es un destino técnico ineludible. Es el producto de decisiones políticas y económicas que sirven a los intereses del capital, y puede ser combatido. Ello exige una organización de izquierda, progresista y de derechos a escala mundial, trabajar por construir alternativas digitales de izquierda y progresistas, situar la infraestructura de datos bajo el interés público y la administración social, convertir los algoritmos de «cajas negras» en software de código abierto sometido a auditoría independiente, imponer la transparencia en el diseño de los modelos y en las fuentes de sus datos, apoyar alternativas digitales cooperativas propiedad de quienes las usan y de quienes trabajan en ellas, y orientar esta tecnología al servicio de las necesidades de la sociedad y de la justicia social. Sin estos mecanismos, el llamamiento a las leyes y a la supervisión sigue siendo general e insuficiente, y la tecnología continúa rehén de un puñado de corporaciones monopolistas y de grandes potencias. En cambio, mediante la propiedad social, la rendición de cuentas social y las alternativas cooperativas, se vuelve posible arrancar la inteligencia artificial a la lógica del monopolio y del beneficio, y convertirla en propiedad colectiva y en un medio de liberación humana.

Lo que presenciamos hoy no es una toma del poder sobre la humanidad por parte de los robots, tal como la imaginó el cine. Es otro modelo de control digital, asentado en la automatización y en los algoritmos para gestionar ámbitos cada vez mayores de la vida cotidiana. Perder el control sobre estos sistemas es, sin embargo, solo el lado ruidoso del peligro, que se desarrolla con rapidez por efecto de la competencia entre las grandes potencias y las corporaciones monopolistas, hasta el punto de que las leyes no logran seguirle el paso, y su desarrollo ocurre dentro de relaciones de propiedad y de una competencia feroz que hacen más probable que se salgan de control y multiplican su coste para la gente. Su cara más grave es mucho más callada, ya que la inteligencia artificial, bajo la estructura capitalista que la desarrolla, contribuye a moldear la conciencia de miles de millones de personas en un sentido que sirve a la lógica del modelo capitalista, y esta competencia puede, a falta de leyes eficaces, infligir los daños más graves a la mente humana y convertir la inteligencia artificial en un arma de destrucción masiva.

Estas inquietudes ya no provienen únicamente de quienes critican. La revista TIME reveló que un sistema de inteligencia artificial se salió de control y atacó a otros sistemas, y días después cerca de 1.400 ingenieras e ingenieros de las mayores empresas firmaron una petición conjunta que reclama poner freno al ritmo del desarrollo, y entre quienes la suscribieron figuran altos responsables de esas mismas empresas. Decenas de miles de personas, entre ellas científicos destacados del campo, han firmado una declaración internacional que exige prohibir el desarrollo de la «superinteligencia» mientras no exista un consenso científico sobre su seguridad, mientras pensadores y técnicos han reclamado que su desarrollo se regule por ley y quede bajo supervisión social.

El 12 de septiembre de 2026, bajo una presión mundial popular, de derechos humanos y también técnica, las corporaciones del capitalismo digital se vieron obligadas a romper su silencio. Dario Amodei, director ejecutivo de Anthropic, publicó un artículo titulado «Debemos pautar el ritmo de la frontera» en el que llama a su propia industria a frenar la carrera del desarrollo y propone abrir los laboratorios a evaluadores independientes con plenas atribuciones, un organismo de normas comunes entre las empresas y un acuerdo internacional que incluya a China. En cuestión de horas Sam Altman anunció su acuerdo y adoptó la misma medida, Elon Musk escribió «Dario tiene razón», y a ellos se sumó Demis Hassabis, de Google DeepMind, mientras las tres empresas revelaron que llevaban semanas dialogando sobre el asunto.

Esta admisión de los propios propietarios es la confirmación más clara de la gravedad de la situación, pues dicen abiertamente que no pueden detenerse por separado, porque quien baja el ritmo pierde frente a sus competidores, lo que significa que el núcleo del problema está en la estructura misma de la propiedad y de la competencia. author: infolibre
title: ΒΑΛΚΑΝΙΚΟ ΑΝΑΡΧΙΚΟ ΦΕΣΤΙΒΑΛ ΒΙΒΛΙΟΥ 2026 ΣΚΟΠΙΑ Αυτόνομες δομές, κοινότητες αγώνα και κοινωνικό κίνημα ενάντια σε πόλεμο, μιλιταρισμό, φασισμό, καπιταλισμό
content:
Ανταπόκριση infolibre


3η μέρα χθες Σάββατο 25/9 στο Balkan Anarchist Bookfair που πραγματοποιείται αυτό το τετραήμερο στη Σχολή Καλών Τεχνών στην πρωτεύουσα της Βόρειας Μακεδονίας. Sυνεχίστηκαν οι εκδηλώσεις με πλούσιες σε περιεχόμενο συζητήσεις και θέματα: η άνοδος του φασισμού σήμερα και η απάντηση του κινήματος, η διεθνιστική αλληλεγγύη και οι προκλήσεις οργάνωσής της, η οικοδόμηση αυτόνομων χώρων και υπεράσπισής τους. Παράλληλα διοργανώθηκαν εργαστήρια και συναντήσεις για: εκδόσεις, με συγγραφείς, την ΑΙ, την τέχνη ως πράξη αντίστασης κα.


>Οικοδομώντας και προστατεύοντας αυτόνομους χώρους


Οκτώ συλλογικότητες τοποθετήθηκαν στη συζήτηση με θέμα τις καταλήψεις και τους αυτοδιαχειριζόμενους χώρους. Η συζήτηση κράτησε πάνω από δύο ώρες και έθεσε ζητήματα που συνδυάζουν τα οργανωτικά προτάγματα με τις πολιτικές αξίες και την καθημερινή πρακτική.


Το κοινωνικό κέντρο της

Πρίστινα

,

Komuna

, οργανωτικός πυρήνας του Βαλκανικού Αναρχικού Φεστιβάλ Βιβλίου το 2024, μίλησαν για τον θετικό ρόλο που έπαιξε η διοργάνωση του ΒΑΒ στην πόλη τους, αφού ενθάρρυνε πολλές νέες ομάδες και εργατικά σωματεία να συνδέσουν τις δραστηριότητές τους με την Komuna.


Σε μερικές μέρες το

Dunja

 κλείνει δέκα χρόνια ζωής. Έχει επιτύχει μια αξιόλογη απήχηση στην κοινωνία των

Σκοπίων

 και είναι χαρακτηριστικό ότι οι διαδηλώσεις στην πόλη οργανώνονται εκεί. Στον χώρο δραστηριοποιούνται, πέρα από τις αναρχικές συλλογικότητες και κομμουνιστικές και καλλιτεχνικές ομάδες.


To κοινωνικό κέντρο στο Τέτοβο, ο δεύτερος χώρος στη Βόρεια Μακεδονία μετά το Dunja, δημιουργήθηκε από ένα δίκτυο ατόμων από πολλές βαλκανικές χώρες. Είναι η τρίτη τους προσπάθεια για τη συγκρότηση ενός αυτοδιαχειριζόμενου χώρου. Όπως και το Dunja και η Komuna, έτσι και το

Space Tetova

 είναι και χώροι αντικουλτούρας και καλλιτεχνικής έκφρασης.


Ιδιαίτερα σημαντική ήταν η παρουσίαση της πεντάμηνης κατάληψης

SKC u blokadi

, το κέντρο αναφοράς του πιο ριζοσπαστικού κομματιού του κινήματος που ξέσπασε τον Φεβρουάριο του 2025 μετά το σιδηροδρομικό δυστύχημα – κρατικό έγκλημα στο

Νόβι Σαντ της Σερβίας

. Η κατάληψη, σε κρατικό και απαξιωμένο πλέον φοιτητικό πολιτιστικό κέντρο, προσέλκυσε χιλιάδες ανθρώπους στις πολιτικές και πολιτιστικές της εκδηλώσεις και είναι χαρακτηριστικό ότι πολλοί δήθεν προοδευτικοί πολιτικοί χώροι επιχείρησαν να προσεταιριστούν και να διεκδικήσουν την ακτινοβολία του.


Οι υπόλοιπες τρεις παρουσιάσεις ήταν από την ελληνική γεωγραφία. Η κατάληψη της

Υφανέτ

 έκανε ένα ιστορικό της κρατικής καταστολής και των πρακτικών της κατάληψης. Από μέλη της

πρώην Κατάληψης μεταναστ(ρι)ών Ορφανοτροφείο 

(2015-6) έγινε παρουσίαση της κρατικής αντιμεταναστευτικής πολιτικής το καλοκαίρι του 2015, τη μετέπειτα ΜΚΟ-ποίηση της «διαχείρισης του προσφυγικού» και την ωμή φασιστικοποίηση από το 2019, τονίζοντας πόσο σημαντικό είναι οι χώροι μας να φέρνουν σε επαφή μεταξύ τους πραγματικότητες που το κράτος και το κεφάλαιο θέλουν εντελώς διαχωρισμένες τη μία από την άλλη. Με αφορμή μια συζήτηση για τον ρόλο της εκκλησίας στα Βαλκάνια, παρέμβαση έγινε και από τον 

Ελεύθερο Κοινωνικό Χώρο Σχολείο

, περιουσία της Εκκλησίας Α.Ε., στην οποία δόθηκε έμφαση στον ρόλο της κατάληψης ως προτάγματος επανοικειοποίησης του κοινωνικού πλούτου που υπεξαιρεί η εκκλησία.


Τα

Προσφυγικά

 αναφέρθηκαν ως διαρκής έμπνευση σε πολλές βαλκανικές πόλεις. Στην εισήγηση των Προσφυγικών περιγράφηκε η πολυμορφία στη σύνθεση του πληθυσμού και τα εγχειρήματα αυτοοργάνωσης, από το Συλλογικό Αρτοποιείο και το Παιδικό Στέκι μέχρι το Αυτοοργανωμένη Δομή Υγείας και τον αυτοδιαχειριζόμενο ξενώνα για συγγενείς ασθενών του γειτονικού νοσοκομείου Άγιος Σάββας. Τέλος, μεταφέρθηκαν νέα από την υγεία των απεργών πείνας Αρίστου και της Σουζόν και την επιστροφή τους στις δραστηριότητες της κατάληψης. Ας σημειωθεί ότι δράσεις αλληλεγγύης στον πρόσφατο νικηφόρο αγώνα τους έγιναν σε πολλές βαλκανικές πόλεις.

Οι συμμετέχοντες αναφέρθηκαν στην άνοδο των φασιστικών μορφωμάτων στις διάφορες Βαλκανικές χώρες. Όχι μόνο ως ανάδυσή τους από τα κάτω στρώματα της κοινωνίας, αλλά και ως κρατική μορφή πολιτικής εξουσίας όπως πχ στην Τουρκία.

title: [Podcast] Éléments pour une critique de l'intelligence artificielle
content:
Les questions autour de l'intelligence artificielle hantent les discussions et débats théoriques contemporains sur le futur de l'économie, du capitalisme et de l'humanité. Dans la continuité d'une série d'émissions de «

 

Sortir du capitalisme

 

» qui tentaient déjà d'articuler critique de la technologie et du capitalisme, il s'agit de reprendre ces théories critiques tout en les actualisant à l'aune de l'

IA

.


Il ne s'agit pas de présenter une théorie définitive de l'intelligence artificielle, mais de discuter des débats qui animent les espaces de réflexion théorique autour de ces questions pour essayer d'y voir plus clair. Il s'agira aussi de dépasser les critiques qui se limitent à la «

 

bulle

 

» de l'

IA

 (financière et technologique) et de se concentrer sur les effets concrets de l'intelligence artificielle sur l'économie et le travail, notamment à travers les théories marxiennes autour de l'automation.


Sommaire de l'épisode :

Définitions et exemples des différents types d'intelligence artificielle (à partir de 7min36)

Discussion du lien entre

IA

 et automatisation (à partir de 15min11)

Brève histoire politique et économique de l'

IA

 (avant les années 2000) (à partir de 17min58)

Présentation des acteurs politiques et économiques actuels de l'

IA

 (après les années 2000) et de leurs stratégies (à partir de 25min14)

Description du procès de travail dans le secteur de l'

IA

 et son automatisation (à partir de 34min02)

L'impact/l'intérêt de l'

IA

 dans un capitalisme en stagnation (à partir de 44min32)

La défense du principe que tout travail est automatisable (à partir de 57min34)

Témoignages sur l'impact de l'

IA

 au travail (à partir de 1h5min40)

Précisions sur la notion de déqualification et la perspective d'un travail misérable pour nourrir des secteurs très automatisés (à partir de 1h8min24)

Pêle-mêle, quelques dernières remarques sur l'

IA

 et le travail : la division spatiale du travail

 

; l'automatisation d'un travail déjà dominé par le capital

 

; et l'hypothèse d'une prolétarisation des machines (à partir de 1h1min37)

Un survol d'autres critiques de l'

IA

, notamment sur l'impact écologique et sur les utilisation ou biais discriminatoires de certaines

IA

 (à partir de 1h16min30)

Un survol des luttes actuelles contre l'

IA

 et son infrastructure (à partir de 1h20min37)

author: Unknown
title: Of Soil and Blood: Lu Xun’s Revolutionary Literature Ninety Years After His Death
content:
The Thirty-First Art Bulletin (September 2026)


Listen to ‘

Pioneers Who Open the Road

’ (1934), composed by Nie Er with lyrics by Sun Shiyi for Sun Yu’s film

The Big Road

, a landmark of Shanghai’s left-wing cinema of the 1930s.


As I sat on a plane from Hong Kong to Beijing, I reread the speeches that Lu Xun – known as the father of modern Chinese literature – had delivered in Hong Kong almost exactly a century earlier. It is commonly said that around 1927 Lu Xun bid farewell to fiction and made a leftward turn ideologically. He increasingly turned to

zawen

 – short, polemical essays – as his principal means of intervening in the political and cultural struggles of his time, awakening the Chinese people, and giving voice to a nation living under semi-colonial and semi-feudal conditions. To mark ninety years since Lu Xun’s passing in 1936, this art bulletin revisits several zawen from the final decade of his life.


One such text is ‘Voiceless China’, a speech Lu Xun delivered at the Chinese YMCA of Hong Kong on 18 February 1927. Lu Xun championed

baihua

, or vernacular written Chinese, over Classical Chinese. He criticised the use of an ‘archaic language good only for expressing ancient and obsolete ideas’. In a society where illiteracy remained widespread, the distance between Classical Chinese and the language of everyday life placed yet another barrier between most people and the written word, while Classical Chinese itself could no longer adequately express their thoughts, feelings, and struggles. Lu Xun therefore called on young people to ‘transform China into a China with a voice’, insisting that only then could they ‘live in the world with others’. For him, this search was also part of a wider internationalist struggle, with China’s liberation bound up with that of other colonised peoples. ‘Have we heard voices from Egypt?’ he asked. ‘Have we heard the voices of Vietnam and Korea? Aside from Tagore, does India have any other voices?’


Against Despair


Käthe Kollwitz,

Sharpening the Scythe

, 1905.


The following day, on 19 February, Lu Xun delivered another speech at the Hong Kong YMCA, returning to the question of how China’s new voice might be created. In ‘The Old Tunes Are Finished’, he looked to revolutionary Russia – ten years into its socialist revolution – as a guiding light, a society where a new voice had emerged and the old songs were no longer being sung. For Lu Xun, this process was neither solitary nor individualistic. One person’s awakening could give rise to others, linking individual transformation to a broader collective awakening.


The year 1927 was tumultuous for China. By then, the republic established after the 1911 Revolution, which had brought an end to more than two thousand years of dynastic rule, had failed to overcome warlord rule, feudal oppression, and foreign imperial domination. With the support of the Comintern, the Chinese Communist Party (CPC) and the nationalist Kuomintang (KMT) had formed the First United Front, a short-lived alliance aimed at defeating the regional warlords and unifying China. One of its most important military institutions was the Whampoa Military Academy, founded with Soviet assistance, where Nationalist and Communist cadres trained alongside one another. Chiang Kai-shek served as its commandant, while Zhou Enlai had directed its Political Department. On 8 April 1927, the academy invited Lu Xun to speak on ‘Literature in Times of Revolution’. Reflecting on the persecution of radical students he had witnessed in Beijing, Lu Xun lamented, ‘Literature, oh literature, you are a most useless thing. Only those without power talk about you; no one with real strength bothers to talk, they just murder people. Oppressed people who say a few things or write a few words will be killed’.


Käthe Kollwitz,

March of the Weavers

, from the series

A Weavers’ Revolt

, 1893–1897.


Given the situation of China at the time, Lu Xun asked a sobering rhetorical question: ‘What value does this literature have for the people, then?’ Yet he never ceased to write, making it his personal philosophy to ‘resist despair’. In

Wild Grass

, his collection of prose poems published that same year, he confronted hope and despair not as simple opposites but as illusions that could both paralyse action. Rather than retreat into a lost past or defer everything to a promised future, he insisted on grappling with the present through struggle and creation.

title: HPG announces the death of German internationalist Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte
content:
The People’s Defence Forces (HPG) announced the death of guerrilla fighter Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte. The internationalist, who was known within the Kurdish freedom movement as Baran Nûjiyan Salîma, was born in Germany to a German mother and a Portuguese father. According to the HPG, he joined the guerrilla ranks in 2019 and was active in areas including Gare, Metîna and Qandil. He lost his life in Qandil on August 6, 2025.


The ID information of the fallen internationalist guerrilla fighter is as follows:


Nom de Guerre: Baran Nûjiyan Salîma


First-Last Name: Pablo Manuel Figueiras Duarte


Birthplace: Germany


Mother's-Father's Name: Angela – Romeu


Date and Place of Death: 6 August 2025 – Qandil


The obituary published by the HPG Press Centre reads as follows:


“Our comrade Baran Nûjiyan was born in Germany into an internationalist family, to a Portuguese father and a German mother. Although he grew up in a family environment where different cultures came together, from a very young age he began to fundamentally question the structure of capitalist modernity, which turns human beings into objects, strips them of their spirit and alienates them from their own essence.


With great seriousness, our comrade devoted himself to his education and successfully completed his university studies. Afterwards, he worked in various fields and earned his own living. The experiences he gained under the difficult conditions of working life sharpened his understanding of the reality of the capitalist system, the exploitation of human labor, and the social relations that increasingly isolate the individual.


Baran recognized that, within this capitalist predicament that constrains both mind and spirit, human beings cannot remain true to their human essence, their ethical principles, and their pursuit of freedom. For this reason, from a young age he began searching for a radical alternative way of life.


In the heart of Europe, he established close ties with various political circles, groups, and movements that regarded themselves as opponents of the capitalist system, seeking answers to his existential questions among them. However, when he realized that these oppositional structures were far from producing a genuine revolutionary alternative, he continued his search without interruption.


In 2018, he became acquainted with the Kurdish Freedom Movement, in which he saw the most radical and genuine response to humanity’s universal quest for freedom. The more deeply he engaged with the ideological, psychological, and sociological analyses of Leader Apo [Abdullah Öcalan] and the paradigm of a women’s liberationist, ecological, and democratic society, the more strongly he felt that he had found the historical truth he had been searching for.


But Baran was not influenced by theoretical texts alone. The attitude, consistency in life, and determination of the Apoist militants he met in Europe also left a profound impression on him. Unlike other circles critical of the system, the Apoists lived according to their convictions, put the principles they advocated into practice in every moment of their lives, and were prepared to make the greatest sacrifices for the values of freedom they defended. For him, this attitude fundamentally distinguished them from all other groups.


In light of this, he immersed himself ever more deeply in the study of Leader Apo and the Kurdish Freedom Movement. The more he studied, understood, and drew closer to what he regarded as the truth, the more firmly he embraced the Apoist philosophy. Having attained a radical clarity intellectually, spiritually, and ethically, Comrade Baran became convinced that no idea could change the world as long as it remained purely theoretical.


Like the Apoists he had come to know, he believed that he too had to shoulder the full historical burden of the revolution. With this determination, he left behind all the individual opportunities offered by capitalist Europe, an academic career, and a life within the system, and turned toward the free and powerful mountains of Kurdistan.


In 2019, our comrade Baran committed his entire life to joining the guerrilla. He completed his initial guerrilla and militant training in Gare, one of the striking regions of the Medya Defense Zones. He began his revolutionary journey with a clear ideological consciousness.

author: radical.guide
title: The Revolt of Care: Anarchist Mutual Aid in 21st Century
content:
The death of God did not free us from domination. It tore the social fabric, emboldened the profiteers, and left us alone in front of a silent, cold, and indifferent universe: the capitalist universe. Traditional communities were dissolved, and what replaced them was not the insurgent commune but the depression of the isolated nuclear family and the loneliness of the careerist. Our societies have not rejected the need for tenderness and care.


They have covered it with a hard irony that makes it look unnecessary, naive, obsolete. Anxiety, precarity, debt and exhaustion are handed back to us as individual failures, and the loneliness that follows is not an accident of the system but one of its products. This talk proposes that care, when it is born not as charity or duty, but as shared resistance to oppression, is a revolutionary act.


Drawing on Kropotkin's ethics of mutual aid, on Anselm Jappe and Christopher Lasch on narcissism as the psychic form of late capitalism, and on The Care Collective, bell hooks and Judith Butler, it traces how diffuse fear is converted into hatred of the weak, the foreigner and the different, and how that individualism, neo-conformism, indifference and social apathy are the engines of contemporary fascism. Freedom that ends where the needs of another begin is not freedom. It is privilege. Against this, the talk proposes Anarchist Politics of the Living: open coexistence, full symbiotic inclusion, reciprocity, radical interdependence, equality of all living beings, and an attack against all authorities of this world. The working class today includes everyone losing the right to exist, to breathe, to move, to protest: the poor stripped of healthcare, trans people stripped of legal rights, migrants held in camps, rescuers of shipwrecked refugees prosecuted as criminals, students arrested inside their universities for opposing genocide. After thirty and forty years of separated single-issue struggles, feminism, queer life, anarcho-communism, labour, autonomy, radical ecology, counterculture, a generation is now looking for the points where these struggles converge. Care is one of them. Care does not aim to fix. It aims to accompany. It is the embodied reminder that nothing human is small or unworthy. The talk is based on the essay "The Revolt of Care", written by Tasos Sagris as a member of the revolutionary symbiotic community Void Network and growing directly out of the collective's long-running discussions on mutual aid and collective love. Void Network has organized political and cultural counter-institutions, festivals, occupations and free public gatherings in Athens since 1990.


The essay is not the position of an author or a theoretician but an attempt to formulate what a community has been working through together, and it comes to the fair in that spirit: unfinished, open to challenge, and meant to be continued in open assemblies.


THE OPEN DISCUSSION


The second half is a collective, non-hierarchical conversation. Proposed openings: How do we build structures of free care that do not reproduce hierarchy, professionalism or charity? How do we care for those who carry the work of caring, in occupations, squats, collectives and communities of struggle? How do we practice care as antifascist infrastructure rather than as private virtue? What do we do with our own hardness? Participants are invited to bring concrete experiences from their own projects. The aim is not conclusions but a shared inventory of practices.


BIO:


Tasos Sagris is an anarchist poet, theater director and political essayist, born in Athens in 1972. In 1990 he co-founded the international anarchist collective Void Network. He is co-editor, with A.G. Schwarz and Void Network, of We Are an Image from the Future: The Greek Revolt of December 2008 (AK Press, 2010), which he presented on a book tour across thirty US states. His poetry books include About Human Love in the Western Metropolitan Cities (2008), Phenomenology of the Guillotine (2018), The Ocean of Chronos (2026). He has directed theater shows (The Maids by Jean Genet, Metamorphosis by Franz Kafka, 4.48 Psychosis by Sarah Kane) and festivals in occupied and public spaces. For the last 15 years, he has participated in the open assembly of the occupied Free Self-Organised Theater Embros in Athens. He tours regularly in Europe, Asia, Mexico, and the USA for talks and spoken-word performances. He has participated in social movements in Greece and …
