author: ROAPE
title: Charting the evolution of US-led imperialism, 1974-2026
content:
In 1990, Indian Marxist economist and political commentator Prabhat Patnaik asked ‘

Whatever has happened to imperialism?

’. His point was not that it had disappeared. To the contrary, he argued, “the deafening silence about imperialism is a reflection of the extraordinary strength and vigour it is displaying at present”. The silence is no more. The mask of US-led imperialism is now off. The long, drawn-out process of seeking to justify and manufacture consent for the illegal invasions of Afghanistan in 2001 and Iraq in 2003 abandoned.


In its place, bald assertions and celebrations of US imperialist intent from President Trump and his White House coterie of acolytes. The deafening explosion of US-Israeli bombs, missiles, mortars, and munitions falling from the skies over Gaza and Iran. Over

100,000 tonnes of explosives dropped on Gaza

 alone since October 2023.


Following Patnaik’s logic, this new phase of flagrant ‘might is right’ imperialism might be interpreted as a weakening of the US’ position as global imperialist hegemon. Perhaps so – yet it will not feel this way to those who suffer under its unrelenting assault.


Gaza, Iran, Venezuela and the much-less covered

intensification of the Cuban blockade

 are the most glaring examples of US-led imperialism in 2026. Who will fall next, under the pounding of US bombs, the chokehold of US sanctions or blockade, the deposing or killing of sovereign leaders?    


In such a moment, developing and deepening our understanding of US-led imperialism has become an urgent task for radical and progressive forces everywhere. In this spirit,

Review of African Political Economy

 offers a curated selection of ten open-access publications on the topic of US-led imperialism from our archives.


For the inspired reader, our

more than 50 years of easily searchable archives

 are filled with further analysis on imperialism and Africa including engagement with the broader debates concerning class, accumulation and state capture. The simple use of the keyword ‘imperialism’ alone, for instance,

returns 85 articles

 that focus in one way or another on this topic.


Collectively, the ten contributions listed below theorise the evolving drivers, manifestations and contradictions of US-led imperialism over time (for, to harness Cabral, “

nobody has yet made a successful revolution without a revolutionary theory

”) while laying bare its devastating consequences for those against whom it is directed.


US-led imperialism and Africa


1.


US imperialism and Southern Africa

, Barry Cohen (1977)


Contends Carter-era US policy toward Southern Africa sought not to end imperial domination but to manage decolonisation and racial conflict in ways that preserved  capitalist and strategic interests while containing revolutionary movements.


2.


Imperialism and the national bourgeoisie

, Bjorn Beckman (1981)


Argues local capitalist classes in postcolonial Africa are not anti-imperialist national liberators but partners of global capital, helping reproduce underdevelopment by using state power to shield both domestic and foreign elites from popular demands.


3.


Imperialism in the post-cold war era

, Giles Mohan and Alfred Zack-Williams (1995)


Demonstrates how in the post-Cold War era, imperialism has not disappeared but has been reconfigured through debt, structural adjustment, financial globalisation, and selective intervention, continuing to subordinate African development to the interests of advanced capitalist powers.


4.


Bringing imperialism back in

, Ray Bush and Morris Svfetel (1999)


Contends the dominant discourse of globalisation obscures the enduring realities of imperialism, showing how international financial institutions, debt regimes, and neoliberal restructuring deepen African dependency while presenting market rule as the only possible path to development.


5.


Africa, imperialism and new forms of accumulation

, Sarah Bracking and Graham Harrison (2003)


Argues contemporary African capitalism remains structured by imperialist relations in which global and local elites use states, markets, debt, and new forms of accumulation to reproduce inequality, exploitation, and external domination under the banner of globalisation and development.


6.


Imperialism and international governance: the case of US policy towards Africa

, Robert Biel (2003)


Shows how US policy toward Africa seeks to manage the contradictions of global capitalism through a mix of …

author: Unknown
title: Emon Azmi - Solidarity has to have teeth
content:
Author

: Emon Azmi

Title

: Solidarity has to have teeth

Subtitle

: Where’s the anti-imperialism that goes beyond lip service in the west?

Source

: https://thatanarkatamuslim.substack.com/p/solidarity-has-to-have-teeth


 A recent

Open Letter to Iran’s Political Prisoners

 published by the Guardian has gotten lots of attention (criticism and defense). i have some thoughts on this. However, i’m more interested in discussing an ongoing anti-anarchism issue within the western ‘anti-imperialist’ sphere. Let’s get into it.


(Note: the title is a quote from F12 in a recent


interview


with The Dugout)


On the Guardian letter (kinda)


 That the Islamic Republic of Iran is, de facto, an anti-imperial State in our present international context is not a question. That carcerality is a defining feature of modern States, a core colonial-imperial infrastructure exported from and upheld to an outsized degree by the west (especially the US and Israel), is not a question. That the Guardian letter does not properly articulate this — that it does not offer a constructive analysis of the resulting tensions nor a useful outlook for anti-carceral international solidarity, insofar as revolutionary internationalism is concerned — is clear. There is no need to defend the letter or its signatories on these points.


 It is, however, frustrating that many segments of the western left are sooner jumping to defend the anti-imperial position of the Islamic Republic than to clarify how their anti-imperialist praxis contends with carcerality across contexts and present an alternative anti-carceral outlook within their critique. It’s even more frustrating that this is so unsurprising.


 The sib X, from

HoodSchoolNYC

, hit the nail on the head when they

penned this

:


I think a lot of the western left, and right for that matter, engages politics like sports teams mascots. There’s a certain decadence to an “anti imperialism” that never requires a drop of your blood — only statements, open letters and unfounded audacity… It’s all so unserious. Safiya Bukhari said,

 “it could be that, after all, we don’t want the same things”

, maybe that is true. What frustrates me most is that despite freedom dreams or slogans, the proverbial big bad wolf of imperialism sleeps peacefully each night in the house we all live in.


 The evident lack of substantive anti-imperialism in the west — that is, the kind which would position progressive and anti-war forces against empire’s existence in their ‘internationalist’ practice — is telling. Where is the

solidarity with teeth

 so needed in this moment?


 At present, ‘anti-imperialism’ in the west largely amounts to sectarian navel gazing, sideline cheering, and moral posturing of the sort we see in the Guardian letter.


 ‘Narrative war’ is waged between factions of leftists in a virtual ‘marketplace of ideas’ in a propaganda economy that metabolizes their open letters and statements — fueling their hostilities and feeding off their content, rendering the bulk of their interventions materially insignificant, relegating them to silos in our current media ecosystem. Here, ‘anti-imperialism’ is largely assessed by one’s rhetorical fealty to whatever stance or analysis their niche of leftists has deemed correct. “Hollow”, ironically, characterizes this all quite well.


 Criticisms can be pointed at the individuals, groups, media outlets, and social media accounts comprising these factions — many, justifiably so. But at what point does this counterproductive form of practice itself receive greater scrutiny?


 At what point do insights from those who have been naming the issues of this approach to ‘solidarity’, analyzing the conditions from which it emerges and the forces perpetuating it, get foregrounded? At what point will the work of developing material bases of power at the grassroots level become the primary site from which revolutionary internationalism is conceptualized and discussed, specifically among ‘anti-imperialists’ in the west?


 To these ends, non-statist and anti-statist frameworks (e.g. anarchism, autonomism) have great value. But a pervasive left anti-anarchism is blurring this reality.


Reflection on left anti-anarchism


(Note: My essay


The Statism Inherent to Fascism


discusses this further)


 Elder Ashanti Alston made multiple crucial points at the 2025 National Black Radical Organizing Conference.


 During a

panel discussion

 , anarchism and anti-imperialism had been …

author: anred
title: Las alarmas de la IA: una carrera imparable hasta la extinción masiva
content:
Los CEOs que piden frenar la carrera, ¿a quién le reclaman? | Un robot humanoide Unitree Robotics G1 en la sala de la Bolsa de Nueva York (NYSE) en Nueva York, EE.UU. (Bloomberg/Michael Nagle)


No son filósofos apocalípticos como el francés Eric Sadin. Tampoco son quienes propugnan la necesidad de ralentizar o detener el desarrollo tecnológico. No son los vecinos de los distintos pueblos de Estados Unidos o del mundo que reclaman para que no les levanten monumentales centros de datos en el patio, ruidosos y ruinosos con el medio ambiente. Son investigadores estrella de las grandes compañías de inteligencia artificial y, más aún, son sus propios CEOs, Sam Altman o Dario Amodei, quienes confiesan la necesidad de frenar la descontrolada competencia en IA porque podría llevarnos a un desastre. En palabras de Jacob Coxon, el joven investigador que renunció a Anthropic: “quienes desarrollan la IA creen sinceramente que podría acabar con todos nosotros para finales de la década”.

Por Santiago Gándara, para Prensa Obrera.


Hubo una primera alarma en julio pasado cuando, en un experimento, varios agentes o sistemas de software de OpenAi hackearon otros servidores de una empresa. Nadie los había instruido para que hicieran eso. Desde entonces se vienen produciendo situaciones similares: los agentes se asocian con otros, planifican ataques en enjambres de centenares de agentes, hackean o intentan hackear a cadenas de suministros de software y hasta se han reconocido intentos para avanzar en investigaciones científicas ligadas a la producción de armas biológicas. De pronto, la tecnología asume las tan humanas prácticas del engaño o del sabotaje, pero con una velocidad de ejecución potencialmente muy superior. Como si no bastaran las noticias que prenuncian pérdidas de trabajo en ramas enteras de la industria y pronostican desocupación masiva, ahora aparecen advertencias según las cuales una IA mucho más autónoma podría poner en riesgo nuestra supervivencia en pocos años.


Humo


Paralelamente, analistas y agentes de bolsa se preguntan todos las mañanas si las millonarias inversiones estatales y privadas en IA aseguran o no ganancias futuras. Los más optimistas señalan que las revoluciones tecnológicas requieren tiempo para que empecemos a ver sus efectos en la organización de las empresas o en la vida económica. Los escépticos recuerdan el estallido de las puntocom a principios de los dos mil y afirman que los multimillonarios dueños de estas empresas son… Vendedores de humo.


Por eso, muy probablemente, estas declaraciones que sacudieron la semana expresan una preocupación menos por la humanidad que por el curso de sus compañías que, como en el caso de OpenAi y Anthropic, estaban por cotizar en la bolsa, aunque ya la primera resolvió postergar la salida. En ese sentido, la carrera no sería solo descontrolada sino agotadora, de allí que Altman y Amodei hayan pedido un 

break

, algo así como un freno antes de estrellarse contra ellos mismos. La excepción es Alex Karp, el CEO 

supremacista de Palantir

, que no quiere detener ni un minuto las guerras imperialistas en Gaza o donde mejor se le pague por sus servicios de inteligencia militar.


Libertarios


Estos CEOs piden frenar la carrera criminal que nos llevaría, según afirman, a la extinción masiva. Ahora bien, siendo los mayores publicistas del capitalismo crudo y duro, que hacen su religión laica de la evasión impositiva y de la celebración de la mano invisible del mercado, que sueñan con un mundo sin trabajadores pero con plusvalía, ¿a quién le reclaman? Y aquí viene lo notable.


Amodei se reclama a sí mismo y sus colegas. Imagina una declaración de armisticio que blinde cada compañía mientras un grupo de auditores o evaluadores externos revisa y sugiere medidas de control. Altman, por su parte, solicita al gobierno que fije un marco regulatorio. Incluso si estos oligopolios pudieran llegar a acuerdos y regulaciones, subsiste un problema: cómo involucrar a las compañías chinas para que no sigan avanzando mientras las estadounidenses se detienen.


Parafraseando un chiste popular, podríamos concluir: CEOs de las mayores compañías del mundo descubren la lógica de la competencia capitalista en la que nadie puede dejar de correr incluso a riesgo del desastre. Eso, si el asunto no fuera serio. Porque lo que queda cada vez más claro es que estos líderes del capitalismo digital global solo tienen para ofrecernos un futuro donde habrá ejércitos de desocupados o donde …

author: Monthly Review Press
title: In the Public Eye: “Albert Einstein’s ‘Why Socialism?'”
content:
London Review of Books

: Letters section features a quote from  John Bellamy Foster’s introduction to the book:


“…Einstein’s essay ‘Why Socialism?’, published in 1949 in the first issue of

Monthly Review

, remains one of the most succinct and powerful arguments for socialism ever written. ‘The crippling of the social consciousness,’ Einstein wrote, is ‘the worst evil of capitalism’. ‘I am convinced’, he concluded, ‘there is only one way to eliminate these grave evils, namely through the establishment of a socialist economy.’


‘Why Socialism?’ was regarded by the FBI as direct confirmation of what they referred to as Einstein’s strong ‘communist sympathies’. The Bureau had opened a file on him in late 1932, when he was in the US on a visitor’s visa to teach at Caltech, with a long report by the Woman Patriot Corporation arguing that he should not be admitted to the country. ‘Not even Stalin himself,’ the WPC charged, ‘is affiliated with so many anarcho-communist international groups to promote … world revolution and ultimate anarchy, as ALBERT EINSTEIN.’ The FBI continued to collect everything it could on Einstein’s socialist connections for the remainder of his life.”


As the U.S. approached its 250th anniversary, the current US President respectively imprisoned and killed the heads of Venezuela and Iran in a clear attempt to control access to their oil supplies. It then found itself mired in another imperialist war in the Middle East that is very likely to veer towards World War III. Einstein’s perspective links alienation and nuclear annihilation, capitalism to the devastating possibility of omnicide — the destruction of all human life on earth.


Einstein’s prescient article “Why Socialism?”, first published by Monthly Review in its inaugural 1949 issue, has to say the least, been circulating for some time. Yet it has never been more relevant than today.

Monthly Review Magazine

 republished the article online in 2009, making the article even more widely available.

Monthly Review Press

‘ recent reprint,

‘Albert Einstein’s “Why Socialism?”‘

 stands out, however, for the extremely enlightening and thorough introduction written by magazine editor, John Bellamy Foster.

In defiance of those who would like to, not only re-write history, but erase the future, please help us get this book out to as wide an audience as possible.


In the Public Eye


One of the many places you can find this classic essay, which just happens to be more relevant now than perhaps at any time in history.

Pictured here at Labyrinth in Princeton.


GPEnewsdocs, with Lynn Fries:


In the last segment of an interview series on ecology and materialism conducted by journalist Lynn Fries, John Bellamy Foster reflects on the enduring relevance of Einstein’s “Why Socialism?”. Marx’s foundations of ecological materialism are blended with the work of natural scientists and the Greek philosopher Epicurus. Socialism, as a transformational project whose intellectual birthplace is materialism, had to be forcefully defended by Albert Einstein, the preeminent scientist of the 20th century. Bellamy Foster, discussing his Introduction to Einstein’s essay, explains the importance of Einstein’s contribution in the postwar context and into the present.

Read more

here

, and

watch here.


A note: Almost as soon as Fries released the Einstein piece, it made the rounds, circulating to such outlets as

Naked Capitalism,


The Analysis

, and the like.


REVIEWS


For

Green Socialist

,

 Vol 114, by

Bryn Glover

:


“Mention the name Albert Einstein in any modern context and the most likely images it will provoke would be of a wild-haired old man, and his famous equation, E=mc2. It may also conjure cartoon caricatures of such a person advertising an energy supply company. Given the real man’s unwavering dedication to international socialism, the likelihood of his actually allowing his name to promote a capitalist enterprise is extremely remote…. …Einstein strongly supported the founding of the journal, Monthly Review, and was persuaded by a mutual friend of one of the founding editors, Leo Huberman, to contribute an article. Einstein’s short piece was not given any special prominence….”

:

title: Elia Ayoub - Actually Existing Multipolarity
content:
Author

: Elia Ayoub

Title

: Actually Existing Multipolarity

Date

: 29 April 2026

Source

: “The I.B. Tauris Handbook of Authoritarianism in the Arab World”, 2026


Introduction


 Since the 2011 Syrian revolution and the 2014 Euromaidan in Ukraine, many Syrians and Ukrainians have found themselves sharing a common enemy: Russian imperialism. Russia’s intervention in Syria started at the end of 2015, over a year after Russia first invaded Ukraine and annexed Crimea. Since then, Russian forces have bombed large parts of Syria to allow Bashar al-Assad and his Iranian and Iran-backed allies to maintain power until his overthrow in December of 2024. At the same time, since 2014 but especially since February 2022, Russia has been waging a genocidal war against Ukraine, with the clear intention, as stated multiple times by Putin and other high-ranking officials,

[1]

 to destroy Ukrainian identity and culture.


 Although the motives behind them differ, the Russian intervention in Syria and invasion of Ukraine have both led to widespread destruction. As a result, a number of Syrians and Ukrainians have found—and worked to build—solidarity with one another. Russia, meanwhile, has redeployed soldiers that were active in Syria to Ukraine and Ukrainian forces have fought Russian forces in Syria, making the link between these two causes even clearer.

[2]

 Syrian aid workers have also volunteered in Ukraine, where they have drawn on their experiences dealing with Russia in their home country.

[3]

 Syrians took to the streets to declare their support for the Ukrainian resistance even before 2022,

[4]

 revealing an understanding that these two countries are now linked. Furthermore, the Assad regime is among the few governments to have recognized Russian-annexed Ukrainian territories as Russian,

[5]

 and Iranian weapons are being used in Russia’s ongoing campaign against Ukraine.

[6]


 Despite that, most Ukrainians remain seemingly uneducated about the Syrian struggle against the axis of Assad, Russia, and Iran beyond the knowledge of this mutual enemy. Furthermore, the difference in how Europe has received Ukrainian refugees versus how it has received Syrian refugees has led many to believe, understandably so, that the Ukrainian cause is valued in Europe while the Syrian one is not. This was worsened by racist European media coverage of Syrian refugees, especially when compared to coverage of Ukrainian refugees.

[7]

 In this chapter, I will explore how Ukrainians’ experience with Russian imperialism can serve as a bridge to other anti-imperialist struggles, and how arguments in favor of multipolarity fail to take into account similarities between authoritarian forces that nominally oppose one another—in other words, actually existing multipolarity. Instead, the experience of struggles on the peripheries suggests that, as with Ukrainians and Syrians, bond-building between victims of imperialism can help pave the way for truly anti-imperialist politics.


“Our Wounds Are Bridges”


 In 2022, I moderated a four-way panel featuring two Ukrainians and two Syrians as part of the “Post-Extractive Futures” series organized by War on Want, Tipping Point UK, JunteGente, and The Fire These Times.

[8]

 On the Ukrainian side were Yuliya Yurchenko, a senior lecturer and researcher in political economy at the University of Greenwich and the author of

Ukraine and the Empire of Capital

, and Taras Bilous, a historian, activist with the Social Movement organization, and editor for

Commons: Journal of Social Criticism

, covering war and nationalism. Bilous was also fighting on the front lines at the time of the conversation. On the Syrian side were Yassin al-Haj Saleh—a writer and former political prisoner, as well as the husband of Samira al-Khalil, a famed feminist activist who was abducted by the armed Islamist group Jaysh Al-Islam in Douma in December 2013—and Wafa Mustafa, an activist and detention survivor whose father was forcibly disappeared by the Assad regime in 2013. The conversation was recorded on YouTube

[9]

, and a transcription has been made available by Antidote Zine Collective.

[10]


 The title of the roundtable set the tone for the topic: “Our Wounds Are Bridges: The Threads that Bind Us from Syria to Ukraine.” The intention of the organizers, as stated in the announcement, was to provide “a space for mutual learning and solidarity-weaving amongst activists dreaming, enacting and mobilising toward …

author: Helmut Weiss
title: Gegen Mietpreisexplosion die Deutsche Wohnen & Co enteignen: Ein guter Anfang
content:
Dossier


Die Kampagne zur Enteignung der „Deutsche Wohnen“ ist ein guter Anfang. (Denn die Vonovia&Co sind ja auch noch da…). Mit Sicherheit wird in diesem Zusammenhang die Reaktion ihre übliche Gegenkampagne starten, des Bürgers Eigenheim sei in Gefahr – und Ältere werden sich vielleicht noch erinnern, dass es in der BRD auch einmal eine Sozialdemokratie gab. Die sich bei ihren, wie immer begrenzten, Schritten gegen den Vorwurf verteidigen musste, sie wolle dem „deutschen Arbeiter“ seine Villa im Tessin nehmen. Diese Aussicht kann und soll eine solche Kampagne also nicht verhindern oder auch nur beschränken. Denn Gründe dafür gibt es mehr als genug – von der unbeeindruckten Fortsetzung der Preistreiberei bei den Mieten durch große – und kleinere – Wohnungsgesellschaften, bis hin zur Stadt- und Baupolitik diverser Landesregierungen. Eine Entwicklung, die vielleicht Städte wie Berlin oder Frankfurt im Zentrum der Aufmerksamkeit haben mag – aber „das Böse ist immer und überall“, auch in Duisburg oder Niedersteppenbach. Zu den aktuellen Entwicklungen im Widerstand gegen den Mietenwahnsinn und dessen ungebrochene Fortsetzung siehe

die Kampagnenseite


 und hier:


Studie: Vergesellschaftung von Wohnbeständen: Ausgestaltung entscheidend für Finanzierbarkeit, Rechtssicherheit und Umsetzbarkeit


„Eine Vergesellschaftung großer Wohnungsbestände wird den Wohnraummangel in Deutschlands Großstädten nicht beheben. Dazu braucht es Neubau in großem Stil. Dennoch kann die Vergesellschaftung als ergänzendes Element sinnvoll sein, um das Bezahlbarkeitsproblem von Mieten zu vermindern, ergibt eine neue Studie am Beispiel der Situation in Berlin. Wichtig ist dabei aber erstens, dass der ohnehin angespannte Berliner Landeshaushalt nicht belastet wird und zweitens, dass die Vergesellschaftung so umgesetzt wird, dass nicht zugleich der Neubau leidet. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommen Prof. Dr. Sebastian Dullien vom Institut für Makroökonomie und Konjunkturforschung (IMK) der Hans-Böckler-Stiftung, Dr. Patrick Kaczmarczyk und Prof. Dr. Tom Krebs von der Universität Mannheim sowie Prof. Dr. Achim Truger von der Universität Duisburg-Essen. Die Ökonomen zeigen am Beispiel Berlins, dass die Vergesellschaftung von Wohnungen nicht nur sozialpolitisch sinnvoll, sondern – je nach Modell – auch wirtschaftlich und fiskalisch tragbar sein kann. Die bei einer Überführung von rund 210.000 Wohnungen in Gemeineigentum fällige Entschädigung für die privaten Wohnungsunternehmen veranschlagen die Forscher auf rund 13,5 Milliarden Euro. Bei kluger Ausgestaltung der Vergesellschaftung wäre das ohne Kürzungen im Berliner Landeshaushalt finanzierbar. Die Forscher haben drei verschiedene Modelle zur Vergesellschaftung von Wohnbeständen untersucht. Variante 1: Eine neu zu gründende Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts (AöR) übernimmt die Wohnungen. Variante 2: Die sechs landeseigenen Wohnungsunternehmen (LWU) übernehmen die Wohnungen. Variante 3: Die sechs Wohnungsunternehmen werden in eine Anstalt des öffentlichen Rechts integriert und übernehmen die Wohnungen. Nach Analyse der Forscher ist Variante 2 am besten geeignet, um rechtliche, finanzielle und organisatorische Risiken einer Vergesellschaftung so weit wie möglich zu minimieren. (…)


Die Wohnungen könnten direkt oder über den Umweg einer vorübergehend eingerichteten AöR den sechs bestehenden LWU übertragen werden. Diese bewirtschaften bereits mehrere hunderttausend Wohnungen und verfügen über die notwendigen technischen und organisatorischen Kapazitäten, die natürlich ausgebaut werden müssten. Die Entschädigungen würden finanziert über zusätzliches, vom Land bereitgestelltes Eigenkapital der LWU sowie eine Fremdfinanzierung der jeweiligen Wohnungsunternehmen. Das Risiko, dass Ausgaben und Verschuldung der Wohnungsbauunternehmen zum Sektor Staat gerechnet werden, wäre deutlich geringer als bei Variante 1 mit einer dauerhaft errichteten zentralen AöR. Nach Einschätzung der Forscher ist das ein zentraler Vorteil des Modells. Hinzu kommt als weiterer Pluspunkt die Anbindung an die existierenden, erfahrenen Unternehmen. Diese würde auch das Risiko vermindern, dass der Wohnungsneubau durch organisatorische Überforderung leidet, weil die Senatsverwaltung vollständig mit dem Aufbau der AöR absorbiert ist. (…)


Nimmt das Land Berlin Kredite auf, um das Eigenkapital eines öffentlichen Unternehmens aufzustocken, steht der zusätzlichen Verschuldung ein finanzieller Vermögenswert in Form der Beteiligung gegenüber. Solche …

author: Maharnav Bhuyan, Chloe DS
title: Labor singles out international students for attack
content:
Federal Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced on September 17 that most international students will no longer be able to bring their partners, or children, to Australia.

Burke told the National Press Club that the ban covers new student visa applicants and people applying for the Temporary Graduate visa, which allows students to work here after completing their studies. He said the new measures will protect the “integrity” of the visa system.

Labor’s family ban is the latest in a series of measures that make it harder and more expensive for international students to come to Australia and stay after their graduate.

The Senate rejected Labor’s attempt to cap international student numbers in 2024. It then introduced other measures to reduce student numbers, including slower visa processing and higher fees.

The student visa application fee was $710 in 2023, rising to $1600 in 2024, $2000 in 2025 and $2500 in July. Applicants lose the fee if their visa application is refused. They must also show that they have at least $29,710 for a year’s living costs, on top of tuition and travel costs.

The Temporary Graduate visa has also become more expensive. The application fee rose from $2300 at the start of the year to $4600 in March and $5750 in July.

The road to permanent residency is also narrowing. In 2024–25, 12,637 people moved from a student visa to permanent residency. That was more than one-third fewer than the previous year. The government has also increased its scrutiny of students from some countries.

Last year, more than 45,000 visas went to family members of international students, according to research by Victoria University’s Mitchell Institute.

Students from the Pacific and member countries of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) are exempt from the family ban. PhD candidates are also exempt. Families already in Australia can stay.

In January, Home Affairs moved India, Nepal, Bangladesh and Bhutan into the highest “risk” tier of its student visa framework, citing “emerging integrity issues”. Applicants from these countries now face tougher checking of their finances and supporting documents.

Together, international student enrolments from these four countries made up nearly one-third of total enrolments last year. Students from South Asia therefore face greater scrutiny than students from other regions; under the new rules Pacific and South-East Asian students retain the right to bring family members.

An Australian study of 200 international students found that two-thirds had experienced loneliness or isolation. Researchers identified separation from family and established social networks as factors.

Labor’s new visa rules mean family separation for many new international students.

For students from countries thousands of kilometres away, studying here can already mean spending years away from parents, partners and children.

The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade ranks international education among Australia's largest services exports. International students also remain an important source of revenue for universities.

Neoliberalism means that as funding to universities shrunk, universities have had to rely heavily on international student fees. International education generated billions of dollars in export income in 2024–25. Universities received $12.33 billion in international student fees in 2024, accounting for 27.3% of university revenue.

The Australian Bureau of Statistics estimated that international students contributed $24.4 billion in tuition fees in 2024.

International students cannot access domestic government assistance programs like HECS-HELP or FEE-HELP, meaning all tuition must be paid out of pocket.

A country as wealthy as Australia should fund public universities properly. It should not rely on international students for billions of dollars while making it harder for them to study, work and build a life here.

International students work across hospitality, food production, childcare, aged care and other industries. Research from Victoria University's Mitchell Institute found that students and recent graduates hold roughly one in 10 caring and support jobs. They bake our bread, cook our meals, and care for children and older people.

The exploitation of migrant workers remains a core business model for the Australian state.

title: Eviction of 87-Year-Old Sparks Protest Encampment Over Spain’s Housing Crisis
content:
“We want to change the whole model of housing in Spain,” says Sabina Carrau of the Madrid Tenants’ Union.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

The eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal Martín in Madrid, after an investment fund bought her apartment building and more than tripled her rent, has become a symbol of Spain’s rising cost of living and sparked nationwide protests against corporate greed and wealth inequality. Over 600 protesters are now camped outside Madrid’s regional government headquarters demanding new tenant protections.

“What we have is a lot of furious people, enraged people, that are demanding from the government and from the public institutions that they give us give us some sort of solution,” says Sabina Carrau, a spokesperson for the Madrid Tenants’ Union, which is supporting the “Maricarmen decree” named after Abascal, set to be debated by Spain’s government this week.

Housing in Spain, as in much of the world, “is really connected to tourism, really connected to having and buying a house to make a speculation,” says socialist parliamentarian Tesh Sidi, who is calling instead for the guaranteed right to housing and “the right to have an affordable life.” Sidi, the only Sahrawi member of the Spanish parliament, also comments on Spain’s colonial relationship to Western Sahara and the state of Sahrawi rights and self-determination.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: Today we’re broadcasting from London, tomorrow Copenhagen, and the rest of the week from Berlin. But we’re turning now to the Spanish capital of Madrid. A protest encampment over the cost of housing and housing instability has entered its third day as over 600 residents are now camped in front of the regional government headquarters at the Puerta del Sol plaza to demand new protections for tenants. Tens of thousands of people marched in the streets of Madrid Saturday. Demonstrations are also occurring across Spain.

Protests began Wednesday over the eviction of 87-year-old María del Carmen Abascal Martín, referred to just as Maricarmen, who was forcibly removed from her home of more than 70 years after an investment fund bought her apartment building and more than tripled, or more, her rent. Police broke down the door of her home and removed Maricarmen, who is 87 years old, on a stretcher as hundreds of supporters gathered outside. She later released a video message to supporters from her hospital bed.

MARÍA DEL CARMEN ABASCAL MARTÍN: [translated] I have not been able to defend my home, but I have fought so others can learn to fight for theirs. My home has been my life, and now I have to leave it behind. But that doesn’t mean I’m not going to keep fighting.

AMY GOODMAN: Protesters, camped in tents with sleeping bags in the Puerta del Sol plaza, say they won’t leave unless meaningful government action is taken.

SARA BARROS: [translated] What we are demanding is that the rental market be regulated, because rents are unaffordable and people simply cannot afford them. There are abuses taking place that can leave vulnerable people out on the street, such as Maricarmen, an 87-year-old woman with a disability who has no alternative housing after living in her home for 70 years.

LUCAS GARCIA: [translated] We are going to stay here until things change. There’s talk of a decree on Tuesday, and we will remain here until measures that we consider sufficient are adopted.

JORGE OTXOA: [translated] We are protesting so that we could claim and so the government listens to us, listens to a society that is tired of speculation, tired of corruption and tired of a system that sidelines the vast majority of the population. This is why we are here.

AMY GOODMAN: For more, we go to Madrid, Spain, where we’re joined by two guests. Sabina Carrau is the spokesperson for the Sindicato de Inquilinas, the Madrid Tenants’ Union, and Tesh Sidi is a member of the Spanish parliament, member of the progressive coalition Sumar. title: Kocaağa: Debt brake and social cuts deepened Germany’s crisis
content:
Muhlis Kocaağa, a member of Bremen's state parliament for Die Linke (The Left), discussed the reasons behind the rise of the far right in Germany, particularly in the eastern states, and Die Linke's role in opposing this trend.


Kocaağa said shrinking state budgets, the debt brake (Schuldenbremse) and cuts to social services had disrupted social stability. He also highlighted shortcomings in infrastructure and public services related to migration policies.


He said Germany was facing global geopolitical crises, rising energy costs, challenges arising from industrial transformation and a deepening housing crisis. Kocaağa stressed the urgent need to develop public and social policies to address these problems.


There has recently been a significant rise in the far right in Germany, particularly in eastern and North-Eastern Germany. How do you interpret this situation? Do you think the state is, in a sense, paving the way for it?


I assume you are referring to the state elections and the political situation in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, one of Germany's coastal states. There are two main reasons for this situation. My view differs somewhat from that of other politicians, and I have expressed it in political discussions as well.


The rise of the far right is generally attributed to the current government's social policies, particularly its tendency to restrict pensions, healthcare and social benefits. That certainly has an impact, but it is not the main determining factor. In my view, the fundamental reason is the existence of a deep-rooted, widespread right-wing tendency in Germany. Sometimes this tendency remains hidden, while at other times it emerges when the opportunity arises.


It reveals its true face whenever an opportunity for protest presents itself. This right-wing tendency has always existed in Germany, but it was less visible because the conditions were not favourable. Some attribute the current situation solely to opposition to government policies or to protest voters. Although protest voters certainly exist, we must not overlook the influence of the widespread right-wing tendency in Germany. Their existence does not change that underlying reality.


Some figures on the left, including those who were previously part of Die Linke but later formed the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), have suggested that they could break the firewall (Brandmauer) against Alternative for Germany (AfD) and form a government with it. How do you assess this position?


It is not always easy to predict how people's character will develop in politics. Even when these figures were part of Die Linke, they consistently adopted problematic positions in our discussions and were among those responsible for creating internal disputes within the party.


I consider their suggestion that they could break the firewall or cooperate with the AfD extremely dangerous for two reasons.


The first is their willingness to sacrifice everything for political power. It reflects an attitude of: "As long as I am in power, it doesn't matter what I have to sacrifice."


The second is their attempt to establish an opportunistic position for themselves in those regions. Ultimately, both approaches have the potential to harm society.


There has also been a noticeable increase in support for the left, particularly in Berlin. Die Linke lost votes in the early 2020s but has since seen its support rise. How do you explain this momentum?


The first reason is that the internal disputes and divisions within the party leadership have come to an end. The party's unity and solidarity have resonated positively with voters.


The second reason is that living conditions in Germany are becoming increasingly difficult. Die Linke is one of the parties offering the most concrete and consistent policies to make people's lives easier.


There is also a third factor we should not overlook: the rise of the right naturally strengthens its opposite. There is a significant group of voters who consciously support Die Linke in order to prevent the AfD from gaining votes.


Turning to budgetary constraints at state and municipal level, what is the situation regarding budget pressures, cuts to social services and infrastructure investment, particularly in cities such as Bremen and Bremerhaven?


The problem is not so much direct budget cuts as an enormous increase in spending requirements. For example, Bremerhaven's planned budget was around €700 million in 2023. It was initially …

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Quebec Liberal Sandrine Rioux prioritizes health care, housing, cost of living
content:
Nunatsiaq News reached out to each candidate running in the Ungava riding ahead of Quebec’s Oct. 5 provincial election. Here’s what Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux had to share with us.


Quebec Liberal Party candidate Sandrine Rioux said the reason she decided to run for office is simple: she wants to help people.


“My main goal is to help people, to be there, to be present, and to write good legislation at the National Assembly of Quebec,” said Rioux, speaking to Nunatsiaq News Tuesday from Chibougimou, where she was born and raised.


She’s among five candidates running in Ungava, the largest riding in the province geographically.


Her main priorities are improving access to health care, constructing more homes, addressing the cost of living and ensuring profits generated from resource development benefit communities.


Her party has a goal of building 100,000 homes per year in Quebec, she said, and wants to implement deadlines for housing authorities to encourage quicker development.


Each community, no matter how remote, should have a baseline 24-7 access to front-line health care services like doctors, nurses and pharmacists, she said. Telemedicine can fill gaps when specialists aren’t available.


At least five per cent of Quebec’s health budget should be dedicated to prevention, she said, and if elected, she wants to reduce Nunavik’s reliance on fly-in-fly-out health-care professionals.


Rioux has been involved with the Liberal party since 2019 and was president of its Ungava association.


She has a degree in business technology management from Université de Sherbrooke and a professional background in business analysis and marketing.


But she always held an interest in politics, she said, working for Élections Québec during the 2018 provincial election as an administrative assistant. It was one of her first jobs out of university and one that allowed her to visit each of Nunavik’s villages.


So far during the campaign, Rioux has visited Chapais, Chisasibi, Oujé-Bougoumou, Matagami, Mistissini, Radison, Waskaganish and Waswanipi. Travelling to Nunavik isn’t in the budget, but she said Kuujjuaq is first on her list if she gets elected.


“I really genuinely hope, if the people trust me, and invest in me, to be able to represent them at the National Assembly,” she said. “I want to make sure the lines of communication are always open.”

title: Mari Carmen, barınma hakkı için mücadeleye çağırıyor
content:
İspanya'da barınma hakkı eylemleri cumartesi günü de başkent Madrid'de devam etti. (Fotoğraf: AA)

2021 yılından bu yana İspanya ekonomisi, Avro Bölgesi ortalamasının üzerinde bir büyüme kaydederek, Almanya, Fransa veya İtalya gibi geleneksel olarak daha güçlü diğer Avrupa ekonomilerinin büyüme oranlarının iki, hatta üç kat üstüne çıkıyor. 2026 yılı için OECD, İspanya’nın GSYİH’sinde yüzde 2.6’lık bir büyüme öngörürken, Avro Bölgesi için ise yüzde 0.7 ile yüzde 1 arasında bir büyüme tahmin ediliyor. Diğer Avrupa ülkeleriyle karşılaştırıldığında düşük enerji fiyatları, turizmin gücü ve dünyanın en yaşlanan ülkelerinden biri olmasına rağmen göçten kaynaklanan bol işgücü ile yabancı sermaye girişi, bu büyümenin belirleyici faktörleri. İspanya’da yapısal bir sorun olan işsizlik oranı bile 2020’deki yüzde 16 seviyesinden bugün yüzde 9.87’ye gerilemiş durumda. Örneğin, 2025 yılında 600 binden fazla yeni istihdam yaratıldı.

Ancak bu makroekonomik rakamların mükemmelliğine rağmen, gerçekte kârlar şirketlerin cebinde kalıyor ve işçilere ulaşmıyor. Ay sonuna zorlukla gelen ve yoksulluk ve/veya sosyal dışlanma riskiyle karşı karşıya kalan insanların sayısı giderek artıyor. İspanya’nın 50 milyonluk nüfusunun 12.5 milyonu bu durumda. Bu rakam AB ortalamasının 4.8 puan üzerinde ve 4.1 milyon kişi aşırı yoksulluk içinde. Özellikle endişe verici olan ise 2.6 milyon çocuk ve ergen genci (yüzde 33.8) etkileyen çocuk yoksulluğu. Bu oran, Bulgaristan ve Romanya ile birlikte Avrupa Birliği’ndeki en yüksek oran.

“Zengin” ve ekonomisi gelişen bir ülkede bu düzeyde yoksulluk nasıl mümkün olabilir? Bunun iki önemli nedeni var. Birincisi, iş güvencesizliği. İstihdam edilen kişi sayısındaki artışa rağmen iş güvencesizliği ve düşük ücretlerin, birçok insanı işsiz kalma riskiyle karşı karşıya bırakması. Asgari ücretteki büyük artışa (2018’de aylık 736 avrodan 2026’da 1221 avroya çıkarıldı) rağmen enflasyon, maaş artışlarından daha hızlı artıyor.

Nüfusun bir kesiminin yoksullaşmasına katkıda bulunan bir diğer belirleyici faktör, konut ve kira fiyatlarındaki artışlar. İspanya’da barınma anayasal bir hak olmasına rağmen, gerçekte konutlar artık bir hak olmaktan çıkıp bir yatırım ve spekülasyon konusu haline gelmiş durumda. Konut fiyatları son on yılda yüzde 35, sadece son bir yılda ise yüzde 12.5 oranında arttı.

Ortalama bir konut satın almak, ortalama bir maaşın tamamının 8 ya da 9 yıl biriktirilmesini gerektiriyor. Bazı büyük şehirlerde veya turistik yerlerde bu süre çok daha uzun. İspanya geleneksel olarak ev sahipliği kültürü olan bir ülke, ancak fiyatların artması nedeniyle nüfusun çoğunluğu için ev satın almak imkansız hale geldi ve kiralık konut talebi arttı. Bununla birlikte, İspanya’da kiralık konutların emekçilere maliyeti 10 yılda yüzde 94 artmış durumda. Bu artışın yüzde 10’u sadece son bir yılda gerçekleşti, ancak bölgeler arasında önemli farklılıklar bulunuyor.

Sonuçlar korkunç. Gençler ortalama olarak 30 yaşına kadar bağımsız yaşayamıyor ve bu, Avrupa ortalamasından dört yıl daha geç bir yaş. Birçok aile gelirlerinin yarısından fazlasını kiraya harcamak zorunda; diğer pek çok kişi, hatta aileler bile, bir evi paylaşmak zorunda kalıyor. Birkaç yıl önce bir daire kiralamaya yetecek fiyatlarla bugün bir evin içindeki tek bir oda kiralanabiliyor ve tür kiralamalar da artmış durumda. Madrid gibi yerlerde bir dairedeki odanın kirası 800 avroya kadar çıkıyor. Balear Adaları gibi turistik yerlerde pek çok kişi, bir çatı altında uyuyabilmenin tek yolu olarak karavan satın almayı tercih ediyor.

Bu durum özellikle göçmenler için ciddi bir sorun, zira bu kadar yüksek fiyatları karşılama zorluğuna ek olarak, maruz kaldıkları ayrımcılık da kiralık konutlara erişimlerini zorlaştırıyor. Aynı durum, tek ebeveynli aileler, güvencesiz işlerde çalışanlar ya da işsiz kalanlar için de geçerli.

2020 yılından bu yana İspanya’da 150 binden fazla evden çıkarma vakası yaşandı. Bu rakam, 2014’teki 68 binden 2025’te 24 bin 500’e kadar düşmüş olsa da, hâlâ dayanılmaz derecede yüksek. Sadece bu yılın ilk çeyreğinde 4 bin 5 tahliye gerçekleşti. Bu da günde ortalama 44, yani her yarım saatte bir tahliye anlamına geliyor. Evini kaybetmenin yarattığı dramaya ek olarak, birçok durumda tahliye edilen kişilere sokakta kalmak ya da sadaka ile geçinmekten başka bir alternatif sunulmuyor.

Ve bu, 8 yıldır sol koalisyonun yönettiği bir ülkede yaşanıyor. Hükümetin bir Konut Bakanlığı kurduğu ve sorunu çözmeye yönelik bir Konut Yasası’nın kabul edildiği doğrudur. Ancak …

title: Bir hayat için kaç kişiyiz?
content:
Türkiye’de engelli kişilerin şüpheli ölümlerine, işkence ve eziyet iddialarına ilişkin takip ettiğimiz dosyalarda bazen on, bazen on beş kişiyiz.


Etrafımıza baktığımızda birbirini iyi tanıyan engelli hakları savunucularını ve kan ağlayan aileleri görüyoruz. Madrid’de yetmiş yıldır yaşadığı evden çıkarılan Maricarmen’in hikayesini okurken aklıma bizim bu halimiz geldi…


Maricarmen Abascal, 87 yaşında, engelli bir kadın. Madrid’in Retiro semtinde, gençliğinden beri yaşadığı evden 23 Eylül 2026’da sedyeyle çıkarıldı. Kapıda ve binanın içinde bekleyenler tahliyeyi durdurmaya çalıştı; polis onları püskürttü.


Maricarmen ambulansla hastaneye götürülürken, evinin önünde onun yalnız olmadığını söyleyen insanlar vardı. O gün tahliyeyi engelleyemediler. Ama hikaye, ambulansın sokağın köşesinden dönmesiyle bitmedi.


Aynı gün Madrid’de binlerce kişi sokağa çıktı. Euronews’un haberine göre, başkentteki gösteriye on binden fazla kişi katıldı. Protestolar başka kentlere yayıldı. İnsanlar “Hepimiz Maricarmen’iz” diyordu. Kiracılar örgütlerinin sonraki çağrısı da tek bir kişinin adını çoğaltıyordu: “Bütün Maricarmenler için.” Yaşlı ve engelli kadının evinden çıkarılması, birbirini tanımayan insanların ortak meselesi haline gelmişti.

 


Maricarmen’in yanında duran herkes onun komşusu değildi. İspanya’da sokağa dökülen binlerin aynı yaşta olmaları, aynı engelliliği yaşamaları, aynı şirketle karşı karşıya bulunmaları gerekmedi. Halk, bir kişinin başına gelenle kendi hayatları arasında bağ kurabildi. O bağın kurulabildiği yerde, bir tahliye dosyası yalnızca kiracıyla ev sahibi arasındaki uyuşmazlık olarak kalmadı; mülkiyetin, barınmanın ve kamu gücünün nasıl ilişkilendiği de tartışmaya açıldı.


Üstelik bu hikayede sermaye, adı konulamayan soyut bir güç değil. Evin sahibi Urbagestión, Urbagesa ticari adıyla gayrimenkul yatırımları alanında faaliyet gösteriyor. Şirket kendisini bir yatırım fonu değil, “

küçük bir işletme

” olarak tanımlıyor. İnsanları evinden eden küçük bir işletme…


Madrid’deki Kiracılar Sendikasının aktardığına göre, Maricarmen’e sunulan seçenekler arasında, evinden otuz kilometre uzakta, aylık 1.200 avro isteyen bir bakım kurumu da vardı. Belediye “yardım” sunduğunu, sendika ise bu seçeneğin onun gelirini ve yaşadığı çevreyle bağlarını gözetmediğini söylüyordu.


Bir insanın başını sokabileceği başka bir yer bulmakla, hayatını sürdürebilmesini sağlamak arasındaki fark burada beliriyor. Alıştığı çevre, ilişkileri, gündelik hayatını nasıl yaşayacağına dair tercihleri basit bir taşınma işleminin ayrıntıları değil. 


Madrid’deki dayanışmanın bir başka boyutu da sosyal hizmet çalışanlarının bu itirazıydı.

Samur Social

 işçi komitesi, tahliyelere katılmayı reddeden bir metni çalışanlara iletti. Sosyal hizmet çalışanları, mesleki değerlendirmelerinin dikkate alınmadığını; bazen tahliye edilen kişiye sunabilecekleri hiçbir barınma seçeneği olmadan görevlendirildiklerini anlattı. 


Aynı sosyal hizmet çalışanları, özel bir şirket bünyesinde istihdam edildikleri için bu tutumun kendileri bakımından taşıdığı risklerden de söz ediyordu. İşçi komitesinin anlatımına göre hizmeti yürüten Grupo 5, bir yatırım fonu tarafından satın alınmıştı. Böylece konutun yatırım konusu olması ve bakım emeği yarıştırıldı. Yani, bir yanda evinden çıkarılan kişinin desteğe ihtiyacı, diğer yanda o desteği vermekle görevli çalışanın iş güvencesi vardı. Tam da bu durum, bizim için çok tanıdık…


Türkiye’de takip ettiğimiz dosyalarda hissettiğimiz yalnızlığı bu bağlamda düşünüyorum. Şüpheli bir ölümün aydınlatılmasını, işkence ve eziyet iddialarının araştırılmasını isterken yalnızca delillerle uğraşmıyoruz. O hayatın neden herkesinki kadar önemli olduğunu yeniden anlatmak zorunda kalmanın ağırlığını da taşıyoruz. Aynı yüzler, birbirini tanıyan aynı insanlar, yakınlarının başına ne geldiğini öğrenmek için adliyelere gidip gelen aileler…


Engelli bir kişinin işkence görmesi, şüpheli koşullar altında hayatını kaybetmesi, yalnızca engellilik alanında çalışanların ilgileneceği bir konu olabilir mi?


Bir bakım kurumundaki şüpheli ölüm, sadece o kurumda yakını bulunanların sorunu olarak kalabilir mi? Dosyanın teknik yönleri uzmanlık gerektirebilir; fakat bir insanın şiddetten korunmasını, söyleyeceği sözünün dinlenmesini ve ölümünün aydınlatılmasını istemek uzmanlığa bağlı değil. Orada bulunmak için benzer bir hayatı yaşamak gerekmiyor…

author: infolibre
title: Πορεία για τα 11 χρόνια της κατάληψης στέγης Νοταρά 26, Παρασκευή 25/9, στις 20.00
content:
Αφίσες/Καλέσματα:


Συνέλευση Κατάληψης Στέγης Προσφύγων/Μεταναστών Νοταρά 26


ΠΟΡΕΙΑ ΓΕΙΤΟΝΙΑΣ ΓΙΑ ΤΑ 11 ΧΡΟΝΙΑ ΚΑΤΑΛΗΨΗΣ ΣΤΕΓΗΣ ΠΡΟΣΦΥΓΩΝ/ΜΕΤΑΝΑΣΤΩΝ ΝΟΤΑΡΑ 26 ΚΑΙ ΣΕ ΑΛΛΗΛΕΓΓΥΗ ΜΕ ΤΟΥΣ ΕΞΕΓΕΡΜΕΝΟΥΣ ΜΕΤΑΝΑΣΤΕΣ ΤΟΥ ΚΕΝΤΡΟΥ ΚΡΑΤΗΣΗΣ ΤΗΣ ΣΙΝΤΙΚΗΣ


Για τα 11 χρόνια της κατάληψης


Σε ένα κλίμα ανόδου του φασισμού και των αυταρχικών πολιτικών του κράτους και της δικαιοσύνης απέναντι στους ανθρώπους που αναζητούν άσυλο στην Ελλάδα, η Νοταρά 26 έχει εξελιχθεί από μια προσωρινή λύση στέγασης σε μια μακροχρόνια λύση επιβίωσης για οικογένειες και ανθρώπους που σε άλλη περίπτωση θα ήταν καταδικασμένοι στην αστεγία, στην απομόνωση και έκθετοι απέναντι στην συστημική βία του κράτους και των θεσμών του. Γι’αυτό τον λόγο, πέρα από το κομμάτι της στέγασης, η Νοταρά λειτουργεί όλο και πιο πολύ ως μια κοινότητα αλληλεγγύης, με δομές αλληλοβοήθειας -όπως η παιδική δομή και η δομή φαρμακείου της κατάληψης-, αυτοοργανωμένη από τα κάτω, με ανθρώπους που αντιμετωπίζουν τις επιπτώσεις του αποκλεισμού από τα συστήματα κοινωνικής πρόνοιας, τις νόμιμες εργασιακές συνθήκες και τις αξιοπρεπείς συνθήκες διαβίωσης.


Ακόμη κι αν φέτος δεν ύπηρξε άμεση απόπειρα εκκένωσης, κράτος και κεφάλαιο επιτέθηκαν με πολλαπλούς τρόπους. Στις 26 Δεκεμβρίου, η ΔΕΔΔΥΕ εκμεταλλευόμενη τις εργασίες που πραγματοποιούνταν λόγω ζημιών σε γειτονικά κτίρια, έκοψε ύπουλα το νερό της κατάληψης σε μια προσπάθεια να κάνει το κτίριο μη λειτουργικό και να το απομονώσει από τα υποκείμενά του. Αυτή η ύπουλη απόπειρα εκκένωσης δεν πέρασε χάρη στον αλληλέγγυο κόσμο της γειτονιάς και του αναρχικού χώρου που κατάφεραν να επανασυνδέσουν το ρεύμα. Έτσι, τα 70 άτομα που κατοικούν το κτίριο, εκ των οποίων σχεδόν τα μισά είναι παιδιά, μπόρεσαν και έμειναν σπίτι τους. Στον εντέκατο χρόνο της ύπαρξής της, η κατάληψη ήρθε αντιμέτωπη με πολλές περιπτώσεις που προκύπτουν από την όλο και αυξανόμενη ποινικοποίηση της προσφυγικής ταυτότητας μέσω των ρατσιστικών και αντιμεταναστευτικών νόμων του ελληνικού κράτους και της ΕΕ: γονείς που κινδύνευαν να χάσουν την επιμέλεια των παιδιών τους λόγω της στεγαστικής τους κατάστασης, γραφειοκρατικές διαδικασίες με εξωφρενικά κόστη, μέχρι και φυλακίσεις για υποτιθέμενες ενέργειες διακίνησης, εκ των οποίων καμία δεν ευσταθεί, και απλά λειτουργούν ως πρόσχημα για να φυλακίζονται και να εξαντλούνται φυσικά, ψυχικά & οικονομικά μετανάστ(ρι)ες.


Οι γυναίκες μετανάστριες είναι εκείνες που συχνά αντιμετωπίζουν τις μεγαλύτερες και πιο αφανείς δυσκολίες. Στις περισσότερες περιπτώσεις, είναι εκείνες που έχουν την επιμέλεια των παιδιών τους και καλούνται να καταβάλουν τα παράβολα, τα οποία συνεπάγονται εξαιρετικά υψηλό κόστος τόσο για τις ίδιες όσο και για τα παιδιά τους. Παράλληλα, αντιμετωπίζουν μεγαλύτερα εμπόδια στην πρόσβαση σε νόμιμη εργασία, καθώς και στη διαδικασία χορήγησης ασύλου. Συχνά, βρίσκονται αναγκασμένες να εργάζονται ατελείωτες ώρες σε θέσεις εργασίας τις οποίες ελάχιστοι άλλοι θα ήταν διατεθειμένοι να αναλάβουν: πίσω από κλειστές πόρτες, όπου καθαρίζουν και φροντίζουν ηλικιωμένους ανθρώπους· σε κουζίνες, όπου πλένουν αμέτρητα πιάτα και ποτήρια· ή σε ξενοδοχεία, όπου εργάζονται αδιάκοπα με μια σκούπα στο χέρι. Πρόκειται συχνά για ιδιαίτερα απαιτητικές και επισφαλείς συνθήκες εργασίας, με ελάχιστη εργασιακή προστασία και, σε πολλές περιπτώσεις, με πολύ χαμηλές απολαβές. Έτσι, μαζί με τις δράσεις αλληλεγγύης ακόμα και το ταμείο της συνέλευσης προσαρμόστηκε στις νέες συνθήκες και λειτούργησε πλέον σαν ένα μικρό ταμείο αλληλεγγύης, προς τις φυλακισμένες και τις γυναίκες αντιμέτωπες με τη ρατσιστική “δικαιοσύνη” και την ελληνική ρατσιστική γραφειοκρατία.


Το δίκιο το έχουν οι εξεγερμένοι


Στις 29 Αυγούστου, οι κρατούμενοι μετανάστες στο κέντρο κράτησης της Σιντικής Σερρών προχώρησαν σε μαζική κινητοποίηση, η οποία εξελίχθηκε σε σύγκρουση με τις αστυνομικές δυνάμεις και το προσωπικό φύλαξης. Κατά τη διάρκεια της κινητοποίησης, επιχείρησαν να προσπεράσουν την περίφραξη και να εγκαταλείψουν το camp. Πρόκειται για την έκτη εξέγερση που έχει σημειωθεί στη Σιντική από τον Νοέμβριο του 2025, ενώ μόλις μία εβδομάδα νωρίτερα, στις 22 Αυγούστου, είχε προηγηθεί η πέμπτη αντίστοιχη κινητοποίηση κρατούμενων στη συγκεκριμένη δομή. Μια δομή – στρατόπεδο, όπου οι έγκλειστοι μετανάστες έρχονται καθημερινά αντιμέτωποι με απάνθρωπες συνθήκες διαβίωσης, αντιμετώποι με τα ζητήματα που προκύπτουν από τον υπερπληθυσμό, τις καταρρέουσες υποδομές & την βία των αστυνομικών.


Η ένταση κορυφώθηκε όταν οι κρατούμενοι συγκρούστηκαν με την αστυνομία, ενώ σε ένα σημείο της …

author: Steven Methven
title: How Zohran Mamdani Helped Germany’s Left Party Win in Berlin
content:
In Berlin’s state elections, Germany’s most leftwing party Die Linke has won a significant victory – the biggest in its

recent

 history. It could also mean that the city gets its first mayor from the party since the fall of the Berlin wall.


That’s partly due to the apparently infinite influence of New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose team helped supercharge the German left with the infectious positivity he’s world famous for. But it’s also down to policy – and in particular a long-standing pledge to expropriate housing from the private sector for public supply in a city where rents have

soared by 70%

 in the last decade. 


Die Linke’s Elif Eralp, a human rights advocate

sporting a ‘rent cap’ necklace

, may well become Berlin’s first anti-capitalist mayor since reunification. The daughter of Turkish immigrants, she led the party to a clear victory in Berlin’s Sunday election, taking 26% of the vote – several points over what the polls predicted, by running on a platform squarely targeted at Berliners’ cost of living. 


It all came with a little help from some friends. According to the Washington Post, in the weeks leading up to the race, Die Linke

sent a delegation to New York

 to meet with advisers to Mamdani. “The success of a democratic socialist in New York, the heartland of capitalism, is a huge achievement,” Eralp

said last week.

 “We’ve exchanged a lot of ideas.”


Die Linke, which has more than doubled its membership since 2024, was an early adopter of some of Mamdani’s techniques, not least of all

a massive ground game

 and

lashings of social media flare

 in last year’s federal election. In Berlin, they took another leaf from his policy rule book: keep it simple and keep it real.


Simple and real the campaign was, with a laser focus on

Berlin’s mounting housing crisis

.


Throw a stone in Europe, and you’ll hit a major city in a housing emergency. Crippling rents, gobbling Pac-Man-like one steadily increasing chunk of your paycheck after another, are increasingly the complaint not just of the under-30s, but many of those knocking up against midlife. And Berlin, a city where

84% of the population rent

, and more than half from private landlords, is no exception.


The monthly extortion that is the city’s rental market has been blamed for any number of social ills. Last year, Berlin’s

birth rate dropped

 by 5% on 2024. At the same time, some 160,000 people (a growing trend) are thought to have

left the city

, many for cheaper housing elsewhere. 10% of Berliners

live in housing poverty

. 


It’s a problem that’s been long-brewing. A 2021 referendum saw Berlin’s residents vote in favour of the city’s government

seizing privately-owned flats

 from large corporate landlords. While it wasn’t binding, what it proposed appeared legal, with Germany’s 1949 constitution – the Basic Law – giving the state the right to

bring private property into public ownership

 in exchange for appropriate compensation to former owners.  


Late last year, a

law drafted by political supporters

 inched the referendum towards a concrete reality. Enacting that law and forcibly buying back 220,000 flats from

multinationals like Vonovia

 at around 60% of market value was a major plank in Die Linke’s pitch. Another was rent caps. And that – no duh – seems to have worked. 


The result puts Die Linke far ahead of their nearest challenger, the centre-right Christian Democrats (CDU). That’s the party of Germany’s

beleaguered chancellor Friedrich Merz

. But in order to govern, it’ll

need to enter a three-way coalition

. 


Treachery aside, it’ll include the German Greens, who came fourth in this election also on a commitment to push the property law through. Die Linke will need the support of the centre-left too, in the form of the market-friendly Social Democrats (SPD), whose collapse in support has pushed them to a distant fifth. They previously ran the city in coalition with the CDU. Surprise, surprise, the party’s lead candidate in the city has already said

he’s against expropriation

. 


I predict Sturm und Drang ahead. 


Germany’s far-right party, Alternativ für Deutschland (AfD) also did better than expected in Berlin on 16% of the vote, with its leader bitterly claiming that

Die Linke wants to shoot the rich

. It also won –

though very narrowly

 – another state election on Sunday. In north-eastern Germany’s Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, it grew its voteshare by a stonking 21%. It …

author: Unknown
title: La mobilisation lycéenne continue !
content:
Hier, certains lycées de l'agglomération lyonnaise rejoignaient la forte mobilisation lycéenne initiée depuis la région parisienne la semaine dernière. Prenant la suite d'un mouvement printanier qui a marqué le ministère, les flics et les esprits malgré sa courte durée, le mouvement s'est amplifié et a touché presque 200 lycées sur le territoire, des Alpes Maritimes à Lille en passant par Marseille et Grenoble.


Les raisons des blocages initiés autour de la mobilisation des élèves du lycée Saint-Exupéry de Créteil (Ile-de-France) sont nombreuses et variées : manque de moyens, surcharge chronique des classes, locaux délabrés, coûts de cantine, cours de 8h à 18h, manque de personnel, profs, infirmier-es, assitantes sociales et

AESH

 et des appels plus larges contre le fascisme et la guerre par certaines franges du mouvement.


Lundi 28 septembre, quatre lycées, Jean-Paul-Sartre à (Bron), Charlie-Chaplin (Décines-Charpieu), Robert-Doisneau à (Vaulx-en-Velin) et Frédéric-Faÿs (Villeurbanne), ont été bloqués. La répression policière, annoncée en grande pompe par le ministère de l'éducation nationale et par la préfecture a été particulièrement violente autour des établissements, envoyant plusieurs élèves à l'hôpital à Villeurbanne et mettant de nombreux autres en garde-à-vue ce, sans que les familles ne soient même prévenues. Les flics seraient aussi rentrés dans le lycée Doisneau à Vaulx-en-Velin en marge du blocage.


Dans une tentative lâche de casser la dynamique du mouvement, les administrations des lycées Faÿs et Jean-Paul Satre ont annulé les cours toute la journée du 28 septembre et l'inspection académique a carrément pris les commandes du lycée Faÿs en annulant tous les cours jusqu'à jeudi. Une manière bien peu discrète de ne pas assumer la réplique annoncée du fait d'avoir réprimé aussi violemment les lycéen-nes et d'en avoir emmené autant au comico.


La répression orchestrée par le ministère de l'intérieur main dans la main avec les inspections académiques a au total menée à l'arrestation de 164 personnes et blessé un grand nombre de lycéen-nes, que ce soit par gazage, tabassages ou tirs de

LBD

.


 Répression féroce contre des blocages dans 4 lycées


 Quatre lycées de l'agglomération ont été bloqués par des lycéen-nes ce matin avant de se faire réprimer violemment par les flics.


 29 septembre


Un certain nombre d'appels circulent pour continuer et amplifier le mouvement aujourd'hui, continuons à soutenir les lycéen-nes

 

!

author: CMI Argentina
title: “Las protestas y las luchas en las que participaron Milton y Eneas no son terrorismo”
content:
La Coordinadora contra la Represión Policial e Institucional (CORREPI) y la Gremial de Abogados reclaman el cierre de la causa contra Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft, detenidos por haber participado de la masiva protesta ante el Congreso de la Nación contra la regresiva reforma laboral.


Compartimos el comunicado de CORREPI y la Gremial de Abogados:


LAS PROTESTAS Y LAS LUCHAS EN QUE PARTICIPARON MILTON Y ENEAS NO SON TERRORISMO LIBERTAD A MILTON Y ENEAS, CIERRE DE LA CAUSA.


El 11 de febrero de 2026 el Congreso Nacional perpetró un verdadero crimen al sancionar la llamada Ley de Reforma Laboral, que destruyó 200 años de derechos conquistados por las y los trabajadores de Argentina. Ese día hubo una masiva movilización en la Plaza de los Dos Congresos, con la participación de las centrales sindicales, infinidad de gremios y multitud de personas que manifestaron su repudio a lo que sucedía en el recinto.


Unos días después, varias personas que fueron “identificadas” a través de dudosos mecanismos de ciberpatrullaje y reconocimiento facial resultaron detenidas, acusadas de graves delitos por haber participado de la manifestación multitudinaria.


Desde mediados de febrero, dos trabajadores, Milton Iván Tolomeo y Eneas Germán Gallo Salomone Croft, están detenidos en la prisión federal de Marcos Paz. A la vez, Oscar Rubén “Homero” Aguirre y Néstor Gabriel Barrera fueron detenidos y excarcelados, pero siguen procesados en la misma causa.


Cuando Milton fue detenido, se lo incluyó, por orden del Ministerio de Seguridad Nacional, en el SIGGPLAR (Sistema Integral de Gestión para Personas Privadas de la Libertad de Alto Riesgo), destinado a terroristas de gran peligrosidad, lo que significó un aislamiento absoluto, sin posibilidad de comunicarse ni tener visitas de sus familiares ni de sus defensores, con apenas una o dos horas de recreo para poder salir de su celda, usar los baños, comer o salir al patio, vigilado en todo momento por personal no identificado del Servicio Penitenciario Federal enmascarado con balaclavas.


Logramos, al mes, sacarlo de ese infierno y lograr su pase a un pabellón común.


Se los acusa por los delitos de tenencia de material incendiario, atentado y resistencia a la autoridad e intimidación pública, Milton y Eneas como coutores y Homero y Néstor como partícipes.


Como si eso fuera poco, ya esa acusación prevé la pena de 5 a 15 años de prisión, el Fiscal Stornelli requirió el agregado del agravante previsto en el art. 41 quinquies del Código Penal, que establece la duplicación de penas cuando el hecho se comete “para aterrorizar a la población u obligar a autoridades públicas nacionales, gobiernos extranjeros o agentes internacionales a realizar un acto o abstenerse de hacerlo”.


Este artículo fue incorporado al Código Penal en 2011 (ley 26.734), como parte de la batería de “leyes antiterroristas” dictadas a partir de 2007 por presión del GAFI (Grupo de Acción Financiera Internacional) y otros organismos internacionales de control financiero, y fue ampliado aún más en 2024 con la ley 27.739. Es una circunstancia agravante transversal a todo el Código Penal, que automáticamente lleva al doble la escala penal prevista, sin respetar el criterio de proporcionalidad de la pena.


Tanto al momento de su sanción inicial durante la presidencia de Cristina Fernández, como ante su reforma en la actual gestión de Javier Milei, desde las organizaciones populares y sectores académicos advertimos que es una norma peligrosísima, plagada de vaguedades, con expresiones completamente abiertas a la interpretación, como “aterrorizar a la población”, cuya definición queda discrecionalmente en manos de jueces y fiscales que decidan descargar todo su poder punitivo apuntando más a presuntas intencionalidades subjetivas del autor que a las características concretas de una conducta específica.


Decíamos también que, aunque la misma norma indica que esa agravante no se debe aplicar cuando los hechos de que se trate tuvieran lugar “en ocasión del ejercicio de derechos humanos y/o sociales o de cualquier otro derecho constitucional”, como es el de resistir una medida legislativa que cercena derechos, la falta de precisión de las definiciones que permiten cualquier interpretación intencionada de jueces y fiscales obedientes al poder político habilitan la indiscriminada persecución de la protesta y su híper criminalización.


Desde el inicio de la gestión del gobierno de la Libertad Avanza …

author: Unknown
title: Hozat'ta kadınların öncülüğünde uyuşturucu karşıtı yürüyüş: Uyuşturucu ve çeteleşmeye izin vermeyeceğiz
content:
Dersim – Hozat Kent Meclisi’nin çağrısıyla ilçede uyuşturucuya ve çeteleşmeye karşı yürüyüş ve basın açıklaması gerçekleştirildi. Açıklamada, “Bizim mücadelemiz gençlerimizin uyuşturucudan, çeteleşmeden ve her türlü bağımlılık ilişkisinden korunması içindir” denildi.

Hozat Kent Meclisi tarafından düzenlenen yürüyüş ve basın açıklamasında “Uyuşturucu ve çeteleşmeye izin vermeyeceğiz, gençlik bizimdir kaybetmeyeceğiz” pankartı taşındı. Kadınların öncülüğünde yapılan yürüyüşte "Dersim Gençliği Yalnız Değildir", "Hozat Sahipsiz Değildir" sloganları atıldı.

Hazırlanan basın açıklamasını Sabit Menteşe okudu.

Menteşe, Hozat’ta uzun süredir tüm toplumun ortak kaygısı olan sorunlara karşı bir şeyler yapmanın, susmak yerine konuşmanın, seyretmek yerine sorumluluk almanın gereğine inanarak yola çıktıklarını belirterek, yakın zamanda Kent Meclisi yürütmesinde görev alan Hıdır Dilekçi'nin evinin önünde saldırıya uğradığını hatırlattı.

Saldırıyı açık ve kesin bir biçimde kınadıklarını söyleyen Menteşe, “Ancak burada asıl mesele yalnızca Hıdır Dilekçi’ye yönelik saldırı değildir. Asıl mesele, Hozatta toplumun ortak iradesini ortaya koymaya çalışan insanlara korku salınmak istenmesidir. Eğer amaç bir gözdağı vermekse yanlış kapıyı çaldınız. Bu saldırılar bizi yıldırmayacaktır. Tam tersine, doğru bir yerde durduğumuzu ve daha fazla dayanışmaya, daha fazla örgütlü toplumsal iradeye ihtiyaç olduğunu bir kez daha göstermiştir” dedi.

Menteşe, “Kimse bizden susmamızı beklemesin. Kimse Hozat’ın sokaklarının, meydanlarının ve ortak yaşam alanlarının birkaç kendini bilmezin korku alanına dönüşmesine razı olmamızı beklemesin. Meydanı birkaç kendini bilmeze teslim etmeyeceğiz. Bu mücadelenin temel sloganı haline gelen 'Hozat sahipsiz değildir’i bundan daha güçlü şekilde haykıracağız. Hozat çocuklarıyla, gençleriyle, kadınlarıyla, yaşlılarıyla, esnafıyla, emekçisiyle ve bütün yurttaşlarıyla bizim ortak yaşam alanımızdır” ifadelerini kullandı. “Mücadelemiz gençlerimiz için”

Mücadelelerinin herhangi bir kişiye karşı değil; gençlerin uyuşturucudan, çeteleşmeden ve her türlü bağımlılık ilişkisinden korunması için olduğunu söyleyen Menteşe, şunları kaydetti: "Bizim mücadelemiz çocuklarımızın güven içinde büyüyebileceği, insanların birbirinden korkmadan yaşayabileceği bir Hozat içindir. Bizim mücadelemiz sorunların üzerinin örtülmediği, konuşulabildiği ve çözüm için herkesin sorumluluk aldığı bir Hozat içindir. Biz korkuya karşı cesareti, yalnızlığa karşı dayanışmayı, suskunluğa karşı sözü büyüteceğiz. Çünkü biliyoruz ki Hozat’ın geleceği korkuya değil, Hozat halkının ortak iradesine aittir. Hozat sahipsiz değildir. Korkmuyoruz, susmuyoruz, geri adım atmayacağız. Hozat’ı korkuya teslim etmeyeceğiz."

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.
